<.heading level={1}>Heading H1</.heading>

Press <.kbd>Ctrl</.kbd> + <.kbd>K</.kbd>, or run <.inline_code>mix test</.inline_code>.

The canvas text roles are colours too: ink (titles and figures), fg (running text), subtle (secondary text, the canvas muted) and faint (meta and help). muted keeps Ledger UI's light grey, which is the canvas faint in the light theme. A page title is size="title":

<.text size="lead" color="subtle">Contas a pagar e a receber das filiais.</.text>

Icons: Hugeicons Stroke Rounded by name, and the small glyphs Ledger UI's own components draw (the cross of a toast, the chevron of a select, the check of a checkbox, the tools of the text editor).

<.icon name="huge-search-01" class="size-4" />
<.glyph name={:chevron_down} class="size-4" />

boxed puts the icon in the canvas icon box (lu-ic, 36px with 11px corners), tone colours the box by state:

<.icon name="huge-tick-02" boxed tone="success" />
<.icon name="huge-file-01" boxed box_size="sm" />

A box can hold an SVG of its own (the inner block replaces name), in any size in pixels and with the canvas tone names (acc, pos, neg, warn, info):

<.icon boxed tone="acc" box_size="30">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" class="size-4"><path d="M5 12l5 5 9-10" /></svg>
</.icon>

icon/1 draws huge-* classes from Hugeicons (the free Stroke Rounded set, which the app vendors with mix ledger_ui.icons sync (or get NAME, search TERM, update; --dir, --ref) and assets/css/hugeicons.cjs turns into classes; see the README) and passes any other class name through, so name="fa-solid fa-house" works with Font Awesome. Write the name in full, never interpolated, or Tailwind cannot see the class.

glyph/1 is for the components: it draws Ledger UI's own SVG by default and the matching Hugeicons icon when the app sets

config :ledger_ui, :icons, :hugeicons

The setting is read when the page renders; the hooks that draw glyphs in the browser read it from the data-icons attribute of their element (see icon_set/0). The table below is mirrored in assets/js/ledger_ui/lib/glyphs.js for the glyphs those hooks draw, and a test keeps the two equal.

The big two-tone icons of the sidebar, the arrows of tooltips and popovers and the spinner are artwork, not glyphs, and stay as they are in every set.

kit CSS's button (btn): filled, outlined, soft, ghost and glass, in every theme color.

<.button>Neutral</.button>
<.button color="primary">Save</.button>
<.button color="error" variant="outline">Delete</.button>
<.button color="info" icon aria-label="Search"><svg>…</svg></.button>
<.button navigate={~p"/orders"} color="primary" variant="soft">Orders</.button>
<.button icon variant="flat" color="current" aria-label="Menu"><svg>…</svg></.button>
<.button variant="glass">On a gradient card</.button>

With href, navigate or patch it renders a link that looks the same.

The classes are kit CSS's: btn, its color (btn-primary, btn-error…), style (btn-outline, btn-soft, btn-ghost), size (btn-xs to btn-xl) and shape (btn-square, btn-circle), so the theme (data-theme) paints it, and any other kit CSS or Tailwind class can be added.

While work runs, loading disables the button (no double submit), marks it aria-busy and puts kit CSS's spinner (loading loading-spinner) before the label; change the label to the gerund yourself:

<.button color="primary" loading={@saving}>{if @saving, do: "Saving…", else: "Save"}</.button>

A button and a field of the same size have the same height (kit CSS's --size-field), so control is no longer needed to line them up; it is kept so existing calls compile. A disabled button is faded. An icon button takes pip, the accent dot on its corner (indicator and status) that tells there is something new:

<.button icon variant="outline" pip aria-label="Notifications"><svg>…</svg></.button>

Ledger UI's rich text editor (Quill's snow toolbar in Ledger UI's skin) on a plain contenteditable: bold, italic, underline, strike, quote, code, headings, lists, sub/superscript, indent, text direction, size, font, colors, alignment, links and clean.

<.text_editor field={@form[:body]} placeholder="Enter your content..." />
<.text_editor name="note" toolbar={[~w(bold italic underline), ~w(list-ordered list-bullet header-1 background)]} />
<.text_editor name="post" filled content_class="h-72" />

The HTML of the text is submitted through a hidden input named like the field, and each edit fires a bubbling input event, so phx-change runs. The editor cleans the HTML it is given and the HTML it pastes (only formatting tags and safe links stay), but the server should still sanitize what it stores. A value sent by the server replaces the text; the same value echoed back does not touch it.

Commands, variables, the assistant and a footer

slash opens a menu of blocks when "/" is typed at the start of a word (text, headings, lists, quote, code, divider) and variables adds the placeholders of a template to it: {cliente} is drawn as a chip in the editor and goes to the server as the plain text {cliente}. The :ai slot is a button at the end of the toolbar (on_ai is pushed with the HTML and the selected text; answer with insert_html/3), and footer draws a bar with a hint and the word count:

<.text_editor field={@form[:description]} slash variables={~w(cliente preço)} footer
  hint="Markdown shortcuts work. / opens the commands" on_ai="write">
  <:ai>Write with the assistant</:ai>
</.text_editor>

The menu takes commands of your own: an entry of slash_items whose key is not one of the blocks is pushed to on_slash with that key (the "/" text is removed first), and hint is the line after its label:

<.text_editor name="post" slash on_slash="slash"
  slash_items={[%{key: "paragraph", label: "Text"}, %{key: "image", label: "Image", hint: "Upload a picture", icon: "▣"}]} />

def handle_event("slash", %{"id" => id, "key" => "image"}, socket), do: ...

Image, variable and highlight buttons

Three toolbar buttons are opt-in (the default toolbar does not have them), added to a group of toolbar:

<.text_editor name="post" variables={~w(cliente preço)}
  toolbar={[~w(bold italic mark), ~w(link image variable)]} />
  • mark toggles a <mark> around the selection (the highlight; pressed while the caret is in one). It is styled by .ql-editor mark, so rendering the saved HTML inside a ql-editor element draws it too, in dark mode as well.
  • variable opens a menu of variables at the caret and inserts the chosen {name} as a chip, like the "/" menu does; it is disabled while variables is empty.
  • image opens a small field for the address and the description of a picture and inserts an <img src alt>. With on_image set no field opens: the event is pushed with %{"id" => id} so the app can upload the file, and answers with insert_image/4:
    <.text_editor id="post" name="post" on_image="image" toolbar={[~w(bold image)]} />

def handle_event("image", %{"id" => id}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, TextEditor.insert_image(socket, id, ~p"/uploads/photo.png", "A photo")}

An <img> is kept by the HTML cleaning only in an editor with the image button, on_image or images, and only with an http(s) or relative src (never data:, javascript: or //host), a width and height of 1 to 4000 pixels and an alt of up to 300 characters. <mark> is kept everywhere. The names of the buttons come from tool_labels (%{"image" => "Imagem", "variable" => "Variável", "mark" => "Destacar"}).

Showing saved text

text_editor_content/1 draws saved HTML read-only, in the editor's type (14px on 22px lines, lists and marks as in the editor), for a page that shows what someone wrote. It takes the markup as its inner block, or value: a string is escaped and shown as text; pass {:safe, html} (or Phoenix.HTML.raw/1) only for HTML your server has sanitized.

<.text_editor_content value={Phoenix.HTML.raw(@sanitized_body)} />
<.text_editor_content><p>Olá, <strong>Joel</strong>!</p></.text_editor_content>

A phone number field with a country picker: a button at the left with the ISO code and the calling code (BR +55), and the number input. The number is written in the national format of the country as it is typed ((11) 91234-5678), and what the form submits is the E.164 number (+5511912345678).

<.phone_input field={@form[:phone]} label="Phone number" />
<.phone_input name="phone" country="US" label="Phone number" />
<.phone_input field={@form[:phone]} country="PT" country_order={~w(PT BR)} />
<.phone_input field={@form[:phone]} countries={~w(BR PT AR UY)} clearable />
<.phone_input field={@form[:phone]} except={~w(KP)} locale="en" />
<.phone_input name="phone" value="+5511912345678" size="lg" variant="filled" />

country is the country the field starts with, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. It is "BR" unless said otherwise, because Ledger UI's users are Brazilian; set it to the country of your own audience, or use value with an international number, which selects its own country.

The picker

The button opens a list with a search field, as wide as the field (at least 16rem), and a 1px divider separates the button from the number. Each entry shows the ISO code (in mono type), the country name and its calling code (PT Portugal +351); a country that shares its code with others and has its own area codes shows them after it (+1 787, 939 for Puerto Rico). Typing narrows the list by name (in Portuguese or English, and common names such as usa), by ISO code (br) and by calling code (55 or +55), ignoring case and accents. The arrows move, Enter chooses, Esc closes and gives the focus back to the button. The names are in the language of locale.

country_order lists the countries to show first, in that order; the rest follow by name. countries limits the picker to a set and except removes some from it. The look is ISO codes because flag emoji do not render on Windows, which draws two letters in their place. flags brings the emoji back, in the button and in the rows, for apps whose users are on platforms that draw them.

Typing and pasting

The field shows the number in the national format as it is typed: the separators appear when a digit follows them, so a number that is still being typed stays as typed ((11) 9), and digits past the usual length are kept. Typing or pasting an international number (+55 11 91234-5678) switches the country to the one the calling code belongs to, and the field shows the rest in that country's format. Countries that share a calling code are told apart by the first digits: +1 876 is Jamaica, +1 416 is Canada, +44 7911 is Guernsey. The trunk prefix people dial before a national number (0 in Brazil, 1 in the United States) is not part of the number and is dropped.

What the form submits

A hidden input with the field's name carries the E.164 number (empty while there are no digits), and the visible input has no name. When the number changes the hidden input fires a bubbling input event, so the surrounding phx-change runs and gets %{"phone" => "+5511912345678"}; it does not fire again when the server only echoes the same value. phx-debounce and phx-throttle go to the hidden input.

The value the server sends wins over the one in the browser, and re-rendering the same value does nothing. value is an E.164 number (its country is read from the calling code) or a national number (read as the number of country).

Formatting is not validation

The format only helps the person read what they typed. A person can submit anything, so the server must validate the value it gets. LedgerUI.Components.PhoneInput.Format reads a submitted number the way the field does:

case LedgerUI.Components.PhoneInput.Format.e164(params["phone"], "BR") do
  {:ok, e164} -> e164
  {:error, reason} -> reason
end

It normalizes to E.164 and rejects what cannot be a number, but it does not know which numbers a carrier issues. For that, check the E.164 string with a library that has number metadata.

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.PhoneInput hook, so the field needs a stable id (it gets one from field or name).

<.phone_input>

Renders the phone input.

Events: the hidden input dispatches a bubbling input event when the E.164 value changes, so the form's phx-change receives %{"phone" => "+5511912345678"} ("" when the field is emptied). With on_country_change, choosing a country (or typing an international number of another one) also pushes that event with %{"id" => id, "country" => "US", "code" => "1"} to target or to the LiveView/LiveComponent the field is in.

Ledger UI's selects: the styled native <select> of the Select page and the searchable listbox of the Tom Select page, with chips, groups, a clear button and created options.

<.select native label="What type of event is it?" options={~w(Wedding Birthday Other)} />
<.select native variant="filled" shape="pill" size="sm" field={@form[:kind]} options={@kinds} />
<.select native inline shape="pill" size="sm" name="period" options={~w(Week Month Year)} />

<.select field={@form[:state]} options={[{"Alabama", "AL"}, {"Alaska", "AK"}]} multiple removable
         placeholder="Select a state..." />
<.select field={@form[:author]} options={@authors} on_search="search_authors" target={@myself}>
  <:option :let={author}>{author.label} · {author.job}</:option>
</.select>

Options are strings, {label, value} tuples, keyword entries, or maps with :label and :value (other keys reach the :option and :item slots); {group_label, [options]} is a group. See LedgerUI.Components.Select.Options.

Pillbox

A multiple listbox is a pillbox by default (overflow="count"): it keeps one line, 38px high (sm 32px, lg 48px), and the chips that do not fit are hidden behind a +N chip that names them in its title and, for screen readers, in aria-label (more_label is its word: 3 more: Pix, Boleto…). The wrapper carries data-overflow="count"; the hook measures the chips on mount, on every change and when the control is resized. overflow="wrap" lets the chips break into more lines and the control grow instead.

<.select field={@form[:methods]} options={@methods} multiple removable more_label="more" />
<.select field={@form[:tags]} options={@tags} multiple overflow="wrap" />

The chosen option shows a check in a 16px slot before its label in the list.

The listbox submits through a hidden <select> named like the field (name[] when multiple), and fires a bubbling input event when the person changes the choice, so a surrounding phx-change runs. A value the server sends wins over the one in the browser; re-rendering the same value does nothing.

<.select>

Renders a select.

With native it is the browser's <select> in Ledger UI's look; otherwise the listbox.

Fixed choices, no search

The listbox searches by default (see search). For a short, fixed list (a status, a period, a unit, yes/no) use native: the browser's own <select>, with no hook and no search, that submits like any input, opens the system picker on a phone and works with the keyboard as a plain select does. prompt adds a first, empty option; {group, options} entries become <optgroup>s; inline shrinks it to its content for a card header.

<.select native field={@form[:status]} label="Status" prompt="Any status"
         options={[{"Open", "open"}, {"Paid", "paid"}, {"Canceled", "canceled"}]} />
<form phx-change="period">
  <.select native inline shape="pill" size="sm" name="period" value={@period}
           options={[{"This week", "week"}, {"This month", "month"}]} />
</form>

Only variant, size, shape, inline and prompt apply to it; multiple renders a form-multiselect box. The listbox-only attrs (removable, clearable, create, on_search, the slots...) are ignored.

Search

search sets where the person searches the options of the listbox, always in the tonality of the component:

  • "control" (default): types in the control itself, as in Ledger UI's Tom Select.
  • "panel": the control is a plain trigger and the list opens with a search field on top (search_placeholder is its text). Arrow keys, Enter and Esc work from that field.

  • "none": no search, the control is a plain trigger (a short list that fits the screen).

    <.select field={@form[:state]} options={@states} search="panel" search_placeholder="Find a state" /> <.select field={@form[:status]} options={@statuses} search="none" placeholder="Any status" />

A narrow field makes a narrow list. panel_min_width gives the list a width of its own, aligned to the field's left edge, and panel_class merges classes into it:

<.select name="customer" options={@customers} class="w-56" search="panel" panel_min_width="26rem" />

Size

The same size is the same height for every control: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px, for the native select, the listbox and multiple pillbox, the input, the date picker and, with control, the button. The tokens are --ctl-h-sm, --ctl-h-md and --ctl-h-lg.

Events: with on_search the listbox stops filtering on its own and pushes on_search with %{"id" => id, "query" => text} as the person types (after debounce ms), to target or to the LiveView/LiveComponent the select is in; the server answers by re-rendering options.

Load more: with on_load_more and has_more, scrolling the list to within 48px of its end (or opening a list too short to scroll) pushes on_load_more once, with %{"id" => id, "query" => text, "offset" => n} (n is how many options are in the list), to target or the LiveView. The server appends the next page to options and sets has_more; the list keeps its scroll position. While has_more is true a last "Loading…" row (loading_label) shows; it is not an option. Nothing is pushed while has_more is false or a request is waiting for its answer (it ends when the list is rendered again).

def handle_event("load_more", %{"offset" => offset, "query" => query}, socket) do
  limit = 30
  page = Customers.search(query, limit: limit, offset: offset)
  {:noreply, assign(socket, options: socket.assigns.options ++ page, has_more: length(page) == limit)}
end

A new search makes the server answer with page 1 (and has_more) again. A load_more answer that arrives after the term changed is not dropped by the client: compare the "query" of the event with your current term on the server and ignore it if they differ.

A text input with a list of suggestions under it, in Ledger UI's Tom Select look: the person types, the list narrows (or the server searches), and choosing a suggestion sets the field.

<.autocomplete field={@form[:customer_id]} label="Customer" options={@customers}
               on_search="search_customers" placeholder="Pick a customer" clearable />

<.autocomplete field={@form[:product_id]} options={@products} on_search="search_products"
               no_results="Nothing for \"%{query}\"" open_on_focus target={@myself}>
  <:option :let={product}>{product.label} <small>{product.data.sku}</small></:option>
</.autocomplete>

<.autocomplete field={@form[:city]} options={["Salvador", "Santos", "São Paulo"]} free_text />

Options are strings, {label, value} tuples or maps with :label and :value (other keys reach the :option slot as option.data), as in LedgerUI.Components.Select.Options. A :hint key (%{label: "Ana Souza", value: "1", hint: "ana@exemplo.com"}) draws a small dimmed note on the right of the row without needing the :option slot, and a disabled option is dimmed.

The choice is submitted through a hidden input named like the field; the visible input only shows the chosen option's label. A bubbling input event fires from the hidden input when the value changes, so a surrounding phx-change runs. Leaving the input with text that is not an option puts the chosen label back; leaving it empty clears the value.

With free_text the typed text itself is the value (the suggestions only complete it): every keystroke updates the hidden input, and choosing a suggestion writes its value.

Without on_search the list filters itself on the client (ignoring case and accents). With it, the hook pushes the query to the server, shows loading_text until the reply, and the server answers by re-rendering options.

The text typed shows in bold primary colour inside each suggestion (no background). While the server searches the list is aria-busy, the previous suggestions leave and loading_text shows with a 16px spinner as a role="status"; "no results" is a status too. The clear button is a real button (clear_label names it) that can be reached with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space.

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.Autocomplete hook, so the field needs a stable id (it gets one from field or name).

<.autocomplete>

Renders the autocomplete.

Events: with on_search, typing pushes on_search with %{"id" => id, "query" => text} (after debounce ms, once the query has search_threshold characters) to target or to the LiveView/LiveComponent the field is in. Choosing, clearing or (with free_text) typing fires the form's phx-change with the field's value.

Options are strings, {label, value} tuples or maps with :label and :value, as in LedgerUI.Components.Select.Options. A map can also carry

  • :count: a faint mono number on the right of its row;
  • :color and :initials: a person. Its pill gets a 22px avatar with that background; the initials default to the first letters of the first and last word of the label.

Single choice

multiple={false} is a searchable single choice with the same look: the chosen option is one pill in the field, the list opens with the search on top, choosing a row replaces the pill and closes the list (no check boxes), and the value is submitted as name (not name[]). clear and readonly work as in the multiple one.

<.pillbox name="product_id" value={@product_id} options={@products} multiple={false} label="Product" />

Size

size (sm 32px, md 36px, lg 48px) is the height of an input of that size, so a row of fields lines up.

Panel width

The list is as wide as the field. In a narrow field, panel_min_width (a CSS length: "22rem", "360px") gives it a minimum width of its own, still aligned to the field's left edge, and panel_class merges classes into the list.

<.pillbox name="customer" options={@customers} multiple={false} class="w-56" panel_min_width="26rem" />

Overflow

By default the field keeps to the width the layout gave it and stays on one line (overflow="one"): the pills that do not fit are hidden and a +N pill takes their place. Its title lists the hidden names and its aria-label is hidden_label ("3 hidden"; %{count} is the number). The hook measures on mount, on every change and when the field is resized. overflow="wrap" lets the pills break into more lines and the field grow; use it only where the height can vary.

The list

It opens on click, Enter or the arrow keys. The search field on top (search_placeholder) filters the options ignoring case and accents and shows what matched in bold. Arrow keys move, Enter or a click toggles the option (the list stays open), Backspace on an empty search takes the last pill back and Esc closes. With create a typed term that is not an option is offered as a last row (create_label before the term in curly quotes, and create_hint, the key, on the right); choosing it adds a pill and an option. When nothing matches, empty_label (%{query} is the term) is said above that row.

Form

The pills are submitted as name[], with an empty name[] first so that an emptied field still reaches the server, and each change fires a bubbling input event for phx-change. readonly keeps the values in the form but takes the x, the chevron and the list away; disabled does that and leaves them out of the form.

It is the LedgerUI.Components.Select listbox (multiple, search="panel"), so it shares its hook (LedgerUI.Select), the options and the server-side search (on_search, target, debounce).

<.pillbox>

Renders a pillbox.

Events: with on_search, %{"id" => id, "query" => text} is pushed to target (or the LiveView) as the person searches, debounce ms after the last key; the server answers by re-rendering options.

Load more: with on_load_more and has_more, scrolling the list to within 48px of its end (or opening a list too short to scroll) pushes on_load_more once, with %{"id" => id, "query" => text, "offset" => n} (n is how many options are in the list), to target or the LiveView. The server appends the next page to options and sets has_more; the list keeps its scroll position. While has_more is true a last "Loading…" row (loading_label) shows; it is not an option. Nothing is pushed while has_more is false or a request is waiting for its answer (it ends when the list is rendered again).

def handle_event("load_more", %{"offset" => offset, "query" => query}, socket) do
  limit = 30
  page = Customers.search(query, limit: limit, offset: offset)
  {:noreply, assign(socket, options: socket.assigns.options ++ page, has_more: length(page) == limit)}
end

A new search makes the server answer with page 1 (and has_more) again. A load_more answer that arrives after the term changed is not dropped by the client: compare the "query" of the event with your current term on the server and ignore it if they differ.

A filter button that opens a menu of filters: one row per group (Status, Sales channel, Seller) that opens a second panel to its side with the group's options as checkboxes, and flat sections (Sort by) in the same menu. It is the Signetum canvas's "Menu de filtros com submenus", and the replacement for a row of status chips that eats a toolbar. It is built on dropdown/1 and its filter items, so the keyboard and ARIA are the dropdown's.

Nothing is applied until Apply (mode="apply", the default): ticks only stage, a group's row shows how many values are staged, Apply shows how many records they leave (from the options' count), Clear unticks the filter groups, and closing the menu any other way takes the staged values back. The trigger shows how many values are applied, from the value of the groups. This is an orders list inside a form; Apply submits it:

<.form for={@form} phx-submit="apply_filters">
  <.filter_menu
    id="orders-filter"
    label="Filtrar"
    locale="pt_BR"
    variant="outline"
    dashed
    size="sm"
    groups={[
      %{
        name: "filter[status]",
        label: "Status",
        icon: "huge-checkmark-circle-02",
        value: @filter["status"],
        options: [{"Faturado", "invoiced", 3}, {"Aprovado", "approved", 2}, {"Rascunho", "draft", 2}, {"Cancelado", "canceled", 1}]
      },
      %{
        name: "filter[channel]",
        label: "Canal de venda",
        icon: "huge-store-01",
        value: @filter["channel"],
        options: [{"Balcão", "counter", 3}, {"Representante", "rep", 3}, {"Loja online", "online", 2}]
      },
      %{
        name: "filter[seller]",
        label: "Vendedor",
        icon: "huge-user",
        value: @filter["seller"],
        options: [{"Ana Souza", "ana", 3}, {"Carlos Lima", "carlos", 3}, {"Juliana Moraes", "juliana", 2}]
      },
      %{
        name: "filter[sort]",
        label: "Ordenar por",
        caption: "Ordenar por",
        display: :section,
        type: :single,
        value: @filter["sort"],
        options: [{"Mais recentes", "recent"}, {"Maior valor", "value"}, {"Cliente A-Z", "client"}]
      }
    ]}
  />
</.form>

Every option is a real input named filter[status][] (a multiple group) or filter[sort] (a single one), so a plain form posts them too, and the LiveView gets them on Apply. A group with nothing ticked posts no key, so merge the defaults, and assign the result back: the values are what the menu then shows as applied.

def handle_event("apply_filters", %{"filter" => params}, socket) do
  defaults = %{"status" => [], "channel" => [], "seller" => []}
  {:noreply, assign(socket, filter: Map.merge(defaults, params))}
end

In apply mode the ticks do not reach the form's phx-change; the staged state is the browser's until Apply. icon takes a Hugeicons name; the default is the :filter glyph (icon="huge-filter" is the funnel).

A custom period

A single group takes custom: true (or the row's text, custom: "Outro período…") and ends with a separator and a row with a calendar icon, "Personalizado…" in pt_BR, that opens a panel to its side with an inline range calendar (date_picker/1). Picking the second day stages the period: the row shows it (13/11/2026 – 20/11/2026 in pt_BR, 2026-11-13 – 2026-11-20 otherwise), the group's presets uncheck and the panel closes. A preset chosen afterwards takes the period back. The group's value is then the text custom:FROM..TO with ISO days:

%{
  name: "filter[period]",
  label: "Período",
  caption: "Período",
  display: :section,
  type: :single,
  custom: true,
  value: @filter["period"],
  options: [{"Hoje", "today"}, {"7 dias", "7d"}, {"Este mês", "month"}]
}

The form posts filter[period]=custom:2026-11-01..2026-11-13 and the events carry the same text under the group's name; custom_range/1 turns it into {~D[2026-11-01], ~D[2026-11-13]} (nil for a preset). Hand the text back as the group's value to show the period as applied.

def handle_event("apply_filters", %{"filter" => %{"period" => "custom:" <> _ = period}}, socket) do
  {from, to} = LedgerUI.Components.FilterMenu.custom_range(period)
  {:noreply, assign(socket, from: from, to: to)}
end

The calendar's own two inputs never reach the form or the events. In the panel the keys are the calendar's (arrows, Page Up and Down, Enter picks); Esc closes the panel and gives the focus back to the row.

display: :submenu (the default) is a row that opens a panel; display: :section is the options laid flat in the menu under a caption, for settings such as a sort order. Only submenu groups are filters: sections do not count in the trigger, in a group's pill or in Apply. type: :multiple (the default) is checkboxes, type: :single radios.

One group, with the trigger of a toolbar:

<.filter_menu
  id="status-filter"
  label="Status"
  groups={[%{name: "status", label: "Status", value: @status, options: ~w(Paid Open Late) |> Enum.map(&{&1, &1})}]}
  on_apply="set_status"
/>

With on_apply (and on_change, on_clear) the events carry %{"id" => id, "values" => %{"status" => ["Paid"]}}, to target, so the form is optional. mode="live" has no Apply: every tick reaches the form's phx-change and on_change at once, and the footer is only Clear.

<.form for={@form} phx-change="filter">
  <.filter_menu id="live-filter" mode="live" groups={@groups} />
</.form>

A :group slot takes the same attributes as a group and your own content, any dropdown_checkbox or dropdown_radio (give each a name, and data-count for what Apply counts):

<.filter_menu id="custom">
  <:group name="tags[]" label="Tags" value={@tags}>
    <.dropdown_checkbox :for={tag <- @all_tags} name="tags[]" value={tag.id} checked={tag.id in @tags}>
      {tag.name}
    </.dropdown_checkbox>
  </:group>
</.filter_menu>

Ledger UI's tag input (the Tom Select page's Input Tags demos): what is typed becomes a chip on Enter, Tab or the delimiter, chips are removed with Backspace or their remove button.

<.tags_input label="Enter Tags:" placeholder="Enter tags" field={@form[:tags]} />

value is a list of strings or a comma separated string. The tags are submitted as name[] (plus an empty name[] so an empty list still reaches the server) through a hidden <select multiple>, and each change fires a bubbling input event for phx-change. suggestions are offered in the list while typing. The :option and :item slots draw an option in the list and a tag in the field, as in LedgerUI.Components.Select.

With max, the input is disabled at the limit, its placeholder becomes limit_placeholder and a 3 / 3 counter appears under the field (on the right of the help line when there is one); counter={false} leaves it out. A suggestion given as a map can carry a hint (%{label: "Priority", value: "Priority", hint: "12 uses"}), a dimmed note on the right of its row. A disabled field draws its tags without remove buttons. The row that creates a tag reads Enter Add “pri”: create_label and create_hint are its words.

Picking from a server-searched list

With create={false} only listed options can be chosen, and with on_search the server does the search: the typed text is pushed (debounced) and the LiveView answers by re-rendering options. Chips show the labels; the form gets the values as name[]. selected_options gives the labels of the chosen values that are not in the current options (after a search narrowed them).

  selected_options={@chosen_tags}
  create={false}

  target={@myself}
  removable
  placeholder="Search tags"
/>

Ledger UI's date pickers (flatpickr's calendar in Ledger UI's skin): one date, several dates or a range, with limits, disabled days, a custom text format, and a calendar that pops under the input or stays inline. For a date and a time in one panel see datetime_picker/1.

<.date_picker field={@form[:due_on]} placeholder="Choose date..." />
<.date_picker name="trip" mode="range" value={{~D[2026-10-10], ~D[2026-10-20]}} />
<.date_picker name="days" mode="multiple" disabled_weekdays={[0, 6]} week_start={1} />
<.date_picker name="due" display_format="M j, Y" show_icon={false} placeholder="Due date" />

The input shows the date in display_format (flatpickr tokens: Y-m-d, F j, Y, H:i...); the form gets ISO text through hidden inputs named like the field: 2026-10-23 (one date), and name[] per date for multiple and range (with an empty name[] first so an empty choice still reaches the server). A pick fires a bubbling input event, so phx-change runs; the server re-rendering the same value changes nothing, a different value replaces the one in the browser.

The calendar is an overlay: LedgerUI.open/close/toggle("id") work on it, and date_picker_clear/1 empties it.

A range in two fields

A range can submit its two ends as two fields instead of name[]: give start_field and end_field (or start_name and end_name) and the form gets start=2026-10-01 and end=2026-10-31 (empty text for an end not picked yet). presets adds quick choices under the calendar, computed on the server from today:

<.date_picker
  start_field={@form[:from]}
  end_field={@form[:to]}
  locale="pt_BR"
  week_start={1}
  placeholder="Período"
  presets={[
    {"Hoje", "today"},
    {"Últimos 7 dias", "last_7_days"},
    {"Este mês", "this_month"},
    {"Mês passado", "last_month"}
  ]}
/>

locale="pt_BR" names the months and weekdays in Portuguese, shows dd/mm/aaaa and joins a range with "até"; months, weekdays, display_format and range_separator still override it one by one.

Keyboard and screen readers

The popup is a dialog named "Choose date" ("Choose period" for a range); the month buttons are real buttons with a name, and the days are a grid of rows and cells with aria-selected, aria-disabled, aria-current="date" for today and a long name ("Friday, October 23, 2026", in the locale). The labels attribute changes any of these texts.

↓ or Enter on the input opens the calendar with the focus on the chosen day. In the calendar the arrows move a day or a week, Home/End the start and end of the week, Page Up/Page Down a month (with Shift a year) and Enter or Space picks. Esc closes the calendar and gives the focus back to the input; leaving it with Tab closes it.

A date and a time chosen in one panel: a calendar with a list of times beside it, or, for a range, two months side by side with a start and an end time.

<.datetime_picker field={@form[:starts_at]} label="Starts at" />
<.datetime_picker name="meeting" interval={15} min="now" min_time="08:00" max_time="18:00" />
<.datetime_picker name="slot" time="input" unavailable="12:00-13:00, 2026-10-14, 2026-10-15T10:00" />
<.datetime_picker name="shift" mode="range" default_time="09:00/17:00" locale="pt_BR" />

The value is wall-clock text, like a native datetime-local input: 2026-10-14T10:30, with no time zone and no conversion. The form gets it through a hidden input named like the field (a range gets name[] twice, start then end, with an empty name[] first so an empty choice still reaches the server; start_field/end_field or start_name/end_name submit the two ends as two fields instead). value takes a NaiveDateTime, a DateTime (its clock, not converted), "2026-10-14T10:30" or "2026-10-14 10:30"; a range takes {from, to} or a list of two. A bubbling input event fires on every change, so phx-change runs; the server re-rendering the same value changes nothing, a different value replaces the one in the browser.

One date and time

The default mode="single" opens a calendar with the times of the day beside it, the chosen time highlighted. Changing only the day updates the value at once, keeping the time (or taking the default one when that time is closed on the new day); choosing a time updates it and closes the panel. On a narrow screen the time list becomes a dropdown under the calendar and a "Select" button confirms (with a "Cancel" beside it): a tap alone does not change the value. A time that is closed is struck through and dimmed; today is marked with a dot under its number.

A range

mode="range" shows two months and, under them, the day and a time control for the start and for the end. The first click on a day starts the range, the next one closes it (a click before the start restarts it); nothing is applied until "Select range" is pressed, and "Cancel" (the datetime_cancel label) closes the panel without applying. default_time takes "start/end" ("09:00/17:00"); the end of a range cannot be before its start.

Times

interval is the step of the suggested times in minutes. With time="input" the person types an exact time (9:30, 930, 9:30 pm, 21:15) and the suggested times drop down as they type. time_format is the 12 or 24-hour clock, by default the one of the locale.

Restrictions

min and max bound the days ("now", "today", a Date, a NaiveDateTime or ISO text; "now" also closes the earlier times of today). min_time and max_time bound the times of every day. unavailable closes whole days ("2026-10-14"), a time range every day ("12:00-13:00", from the first time up to but not including the second; "22:00-02:00" crosses midnight) or one date-time ("2026-10-14T10:00"), as a comma separated text or a list. A day with no time left cannot be picked.

Your own trigger

The trigger slot replaces the input: any button opens the panel, and the picker shows no text of its own. The panel is an overlay, so LedgerUI.open/close/toggle("id") work on it.

<.datetime_picker id="when" name="when">
  <:trigger>
    <.button variant="outline">Pick a date and time</.button>
  </:trigger>
</.datetime_picker>

Month and year

The header of a month has two buttons beside the arrows, the month ("October") and the year ("2026"). The month opens a grid of the twelve months and the year a page of twelve years; picking one goes back to the days of that month. While a grid is open the arrows turn the year (or the page of years), months and years that min and max close are dimmed, and Esc goes back to the days with the focus on the button. The buttons are named by :datetime_choose_month and :datetime_choose_year in labels.

Keyboard

↓ or Enter on the input opens the panel with the focus on the chosen day. In the calendar the arrows move a day or a week, Home/End the start and end of the week, Page Up/Page Down a month (with Shift a year) and Enter or Space picks. In the time list ↑/↓/Home/End move and Enter picks; in the time field ↓/↑ walk the suggestions. Esc closes the panel and gives the focus back; leaving the panel with Tab closes it. In the month and year grids the arrows move over the three columns, Home/End to the first and the last, Enter or Space picks.

A calendar for dates that matter (due dates, appointments, deadlines): a month grid or a week grid of hours, with colored event chips, month and week switching and keyboard navigation.

<.calendar
  id="due"
  view={@view}
  date={@date}
  events={@events}
  locale="pt_BR"
  on_navigate="calendar_navigate"
  on_view="calendar_view"
  on_select="calendar_select"
  on_event="calendar_event"
/>

The server owns what the calendar shows, because the events of another period have to be loaded: view and date come from your assigns, and the toolbar (previous, next, today, month and week) and the keyboard push the events below with the date and view to show next. Update the assigns and load that period's events with calendar_range/3:

def handle_event("calendar_navigate", %{"date" => date, "view" => view}, socket) do
  {:noreply, assign(socket, date: Date.from_iso8601!(date), view: view)}
end

An event is a map with :date (a Date or ISO text) and :title, and optionally :id, :subtitle, :color (neutral primary secondary info success warning error), and :start and :end ("09:00" or a Time). In the week view an event with a :start is a block in its hour; the others sit in an all-day row.

%{id: 1, title: "Coelba", date: ~D[2026-10-15], color: "error"}
%{id: 2, title: "Visit", subtitle: "Santa Mônica", date: ~D[2026-10-19], start: "10:00", end: "11:00"}

Mini month

variant="mini" is the canvas's compact month in a card: one-letter weekdays, the days in round cells, a dot under the days that have events, the selected day in solid ink, a range painted in the accent tint and today ringed. months_shown={2} puts two months side by side (for long periods), each in its own card titled with the month's name. on_select makes the days buttons; on_navigate (single month with header) gives the title its arrows. marks="tint" paints the days with events in their color instead of a dot (a due calendar: to receive and to pay), and legend is then drawn over the grid with square keys.

<.calendar id="due" variant="mini" header={false} date={~D[2026-11-01]} locale="pt_BR"
           events={for d <- [5, 10], do: %{title: "Vencimento", date: Date.new!(2026, 11, d)}} />
<.calendar id="range" variant="mini" months_shown={2} header={false} locale="pt_BR"
           date={~D[2026-11-01]} range={{~D[2026-11-20], ~D[2026-12-06]}} />

The grid is role="grid": Tab lands on one day, the arrows move between days (past the first or the last day they go to the previous or the next period), Home and End go to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down change period, and Enter or Space selects the day. locale="pt_BR" names months and weekdays in Portuguese, like date_picker, and writes the labels of the toolbar in Portuguese.

<.calendar>

Renders the calendar.

Events pushed to the LiveView, or to the LiveComponent in target:

  • on_navigate: %{"id" => id, "date" => "2026-11-01", "view" => "month"}, the period to show next (the toolbar's arrows and Today, Page Up and Page Down, and the arrows at the edge of the grid).
  • on_view: %{"id" => id, "date" => "2026-10-24", "view" => "week"}, from the month and week buttons.
  • on_select: %{"id" => id, "date" => "2026-10-24"}, when a day is clicked or chosen with Enter, and from the "more" chip of a crowded day.
  • on_event: %{"id" => id, "event" => event_id, "date" => "2026-10-24"}, when an event is clicked.

A button whose event is not set does not render as a button (the chips) or is disabled (the toolbar).

A color picker that outputs hex text: a saturation and brightness area to drag, a hue slider, an optional opacity slider, a hex field and a row of preset swatches.

<.color_picker field={@form[:color]} label="Stage color" />
<.color_picker name="tag" value="#4C3FE0" presets={~w(#EB3B2F #F5A214 #18996E)} />
<.color_picker field={@form[:overlay]} alpha locale="pt_BR" />

The form gets #6366F1 (upper case, #RRGGBB; with alpha, a color that is not fully opaque is #RRGGBBAA) through a hidden input named like the field. Every change fires a bubbling input event from it, so phx-change runs; the server re-rendering the same color changes nothing, a different color replaces the one in the browser. phx-debounce and phx-throttle go to the hidden input.

The area is a slider: drag it, or use the arrow keys (Shift moves ten points). The hex field takes #RGB, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA and applies it as soon as it is a color. locale="pt_BR" names the controls in Portuguese; labels overrides single texts.

variant="swatches" is the canvas's brand palette: only the row of presets, the chosen one ringed in ink; hex_field adds the hex field under it (captioned hex_label):

<.color_picker name="brand" value="#8A5CD6" variant="swatches"
               presets={~w(#0D8F91 #2F5FD0 #8A5CD6)} />
<.color_picker name="stage" value="#0D8F91" variant="swatches" hex_field swatch_size="md"
               presets={~w(#0D8F91 #2F5FD0 #8A5CD6)} />

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.ColorPicker hook, so the picker needs a stable id.

A signature field: sign with a finger, a pen or the mouse (pointer events), or type a name that is set in a handwriting font. The signature leaves as SVG text.

<.signature_pad field={@form[:signature]} label="Signature" />
<.signature_pad name="receipt" mode="type" text="Marcos Oliveira" locale="pt_BR" />
<.signature_pad name="sign" modes={["draw"]} height={220} />

The form gets the SVG (<svg xmlns=... viewBox="0 0 300 170"><path .../></svg>, "" while the pad is empty) through a hidden input named like the field. Every stroke, typed letter or Clear fires a bubbling input event from it, so phx-change runs. Give the field a stored SVG as value and the pad shows it; the server sending another value (or an empty one) replaces what is in the pad, re-rendering the same one changes nothing. Show a saved signature elsewhere as an image, never as raw markup:

<img src={"data:image/svg+xml;base64," <> Base.encode64(@signature)} alt="Signature" />

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="classic" is the old Ledger UI pad) draws the design canvas's pad (a card with the dashed line and the hint under it, at the left), and footer={false} drops the status and Clear line under the pad:

<.signature_pad name="sign" modes={["draw"]} variant="canvas" footer={false} height={150} />

Drawing needs a pointer, so the type mode is the keyboard and screen reader way to sign; keep both modes unless the signature must be drawn. The pad is a white surface in the light theme and a navy one in the dark theme (the ink and the typed name are inverted to stay readable there); the SVG it exports always has dark ink on a transparent background.

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.SignaturePad hook, so the pad needs a stable id.

A tag that only labels (inside a link or a table row) is not interactive: as="span" or static renders a <span> with the same classes, so no button is nested in a link:

kit CSS's card (card card-border on base-100, card-body, card-title): the panel, soft, a link row, and the gradient-outlined card, with optional composable parts (header, body, footer).

<.card>
  <:title>Simple Card</:title>
  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
</.card>
<.card variant="bordered" shape="xl">…</.card>
<.card variant="flat">No shadow</.card>
<.card variant="solid" color="primary"><:title>Primary Card</:title>…</.card>
<.card variant="gradient" gradient="purple-indigo">…</.card>
<.card variant="gradient_outline" gradient="sky-blue">…</.card>

navigate, patch or href make the whole card a link, laid out as a row that ends in an arrow:

<.card navigate={~p"/banks/1"}>
  <div class="grow">Banco do Brasil</div>
</.card>

Without :title the content fills the card as is, padded evenly like a bordered div; padded={false} drops the default padding, for cards laid out by hand (<.card padded={false} class="px-4 pb-4 sm:px-5">).

Parts

A card is made of optional parts; use the ones you need. Anything placed directly in the card keeps the card's padding.

<.card variant="soft" body="inset" size="lg">
  <.card_header>
    <.card_heading>Profile</.card_heading>
    <.card_subheading>Make yourself at home</.card_subheading>
    <.card_actions><.button icon size="sm" variant="flat" aria-label="More">…</.button></.card_actions>
  </.card_header>
  <.card_body class="space-y-6">
    <.input name="name" label="Name" value="Olivia Martin" />
  </.card_body>
  <.card_footer>
    <span class="text-xs">All changes saved</span>
    <.card_actions><.button size="sm">Save</.button></.card_actions>
  </.card_footer>
</.card>
  • card_header/1 holds card_heading/1, card_subheading/1 and card_actions/1. Actions sit in the corner, centered on the heading; written before the heading they go to the leading side. Small buttons hang in the header's padding without making it taller.
  • card_body/1 is the main content. It may hold its own card_header/1 and card_footer/1 as sub-sections, spaced and padded by the body.
  • card_footer/1 holds supporting text and actions, or a heading, subheading and actions exactly like a header.
  • card_header/1 and card_footer/1 also work outside a card; give them the size of the card they stand with.

  • card_bleed/1 makes media fill the card's sides, reach the top or bottom when it is the first or last thing in the body, and round only the corners it touches.

    <.card body="inset"> <.card_body><.card_bleed></.card_bleed></.card_body> <.card_footer> <.card_heading>Morning hike</.card_heading> <.card_subheading>Sept 12</.card_subheading> </.card_footer> </.card>

  • A table/1 with bleed inside a card runs its rows edge to edge while its content stays aligned with the card's, and reaches the top and bottom of the body when it is the only thing in it.

Surfaces and treatments

variant is the surface: default (soft shadow in light, elevation in dark, a faint highlight along the inside top edge in light mode unless highlight={false}), flat, bordered, outline (border only), muted and soft (quiet tints that adapt to the color behind them, in light and dark), filled (a tint without border) and the colored solid, glow, gradient, gradient_outline.

body is how the parts are told apart: seamless (one surface, parts spaced by the card's padding), divided (hairlines between parts, divider="inset" stops them at the content edges), separated (tinted bands for header and footer), inset (the body is a panel inside the card, with corners concentric to the card's: raised on a tinted card, recessed on a plain one) and flush (the same panel running to the card's sides). With padded={false} the parts pad themselves and body has no effect.

size (xs, sm, md, lg) sets padding, type, corners and the spacing between parts. The card publishes these as CSS variables (--card-p, --card-r, --card-i, and per treatment --card-hx, --card-hy, --card-bx, --card-by, --card-bleed-x...), which the parts and the bleed of table/1 read; the rules live in assets/css/parts/card.css.

<.card>

Renders a card, with an optional :title above the content, or composed of card_header/1, card_body/1 and card_footer/1.

<.card variant="glow" color="info">
  <:title>Revenue</:title>
  <p>$12,400 this month.</p>
</.card>

A framed card for processes in steps (a build, a deploy, issuing an invoice, an import).

The header sits on the frame with the overall status, the title, the duration and a button that collapses the card; inside, a raised panel lists the steps, each with a status, a result in mono type and a chevron that opens its log.

<.step_group id="deploy" title="Deploy logs" status={:running} duration="1m 04s">
  <:step title="Preparing environment" status={:ok} result="12s" />
  <:step title="Updating the stack" status={:running} result="Running…" open>
    <.step_group_line n={1} at="09:41:02" tone="dim">Connecting</.step_group_line>
    <.step_group_line n={2} at="09:41:04" tone="err">Rejected</.step_group_line>

  <:step title="Routing traffic" status={:waiting} result="Waiting" />
</.step_group>

status is one of :ok, :running, :waiting, :failed, :skipped and :canceled.

The content of a :step is its log (step_group_line/1 lines). A step with a log is a <button> that opens and closes the log; a step without one is a plain row, with no chevron. A canceled step has no status icon, as in the canvas.

Collapsing the card and opening a log happen in the browser (Phoenix.LiveView.JS), with no round trip. The browser owns that state: collapsed and open set where it starts, and a patch does not undo what the user toggled.

Ledger UI's tree view: a hierarchical list whose branches expand and collapse.

<.treeview id="files">
  <.tree_item id="app" label="Application" expanded>
    <.tree_item label="Chrome" />
    <.tree_item label="VS Code" />
  </.tree_item>
  <.tree_item id="docs" label="Document">
    <.tree_item label="React App" />
  </.tree_item>
</.treeview>

An item with children is a branch (a native <details>), one without is a leaf. Give an item an :icon slot and it takes Ledger UI's "advanced" look (folder icons, darker text):

<.tree_item label="Design">
  <:icon><svg class="size-6 text-warning">…</svg></:icon>
  <.tree_item label="Web Apps"><:icon>…</:icon></.tree_item>
</.tree_item>

State

A branch opens from its expanded attr, or from the treeview's expanded list of item ids, and toggles in the browser without a round trip. A branch the person toggled stays that way across patches; when the server changes expanded for it, the server wins.

Events

on_toggle runs when the person opens or closes a branch, on_select when they click a leaf (or press Enter on it). See treeview/1 for the payloads.

The canvas look

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="lineone" is the old Ledger UI tree) draws the Signetum canvas tree: rows padded 6px 8px (8px corners, 2px apart; 36px with a boxed icon) in regular weight and the ink, the top level in 550, a 14px chevron, the selected row tinted with the accent from the row's start (the depth is a left padding inside the row) and boxed icons:

<.treeview id="notas" variant="canvas">
  <.tree_item id="2026" label="Notas 2026" expanded>
    <:icon><.icon name="huge-layers-01" boxed box_size="sm" class="size-3.5" /></:icon>
    <.tree_item id="out" label="Outubro" branch />
    <.tree_item id="nfe" label="NF-e 48.211.xml" selected />
  </.tree_item>
</.treeview>

branch draws an item as a closed branch before its children are there (loaded when it opens). checked (true, false or "mixed") puts a checkbox before the label and sets aria-checked; a click on it pushes the treeview's on_check. chevrons={false} leaves the chevrons out, for a checklist of categories.

Streams

<.treeview id="files" rows={@streams.files}>
  <:row :let={{_dom_id, file}}>
    <.tree_item tag="div" id={"file-#{file.id}"} label={file.name} />
  </:row>
</.treeview>

<.treeview>

Renders the tree's root list.

on_toggle (an event name or a %JS{}) is pushed with %{"id" => item_id, "expanded" => boolean} when the person opens or closes a branch. on_select is pushed with %{"id" => item_id} when a leaf is clicked or gets Enter. Both go to target when given; a %JS{} is executed instead.

<.treeview id="files" expanded={@open_ids} on_toggle="toggled" on_select="opened">
  <.tree_item id="src" label="src">
    <.tree_item id="src/app.ex" label="app.ex" />
  </.tree_item>
</.treeview>

def handle_event("toggled", %{"id" => id, "expanded" => open?}, socket), do: ...
def handle_event("opened", %{"id" => id}, socket), do: ...

Renders one item: a branch when it has children, a leaf when it does not.

id names the item in events and in the treeview's expanded list. Ledger UI's Swiper carousels, without Swiper: slides on a CSS scroll-snap track, and the LedgerUI.Carousel hook for arrows, pagination, autoplay, keyboard, swipe and effects.

<.carousel id="gallery" navigation class="rounded-lg">
  <.carousel_slide><img class="h-full w-full object-cover" src="/a.jpg" alt="" /></.carousel_slide>
  <.carousel_slide><img class="h-full w-full object-cover" src="/b.jpg" alt="" /></.carousel_slide>
</.carousel>

<.carousel id="beside" navigation="outside">…</.carousel>
<.carousel id="promo" pagination="bullets" autoplay={2000} loop>…</.carousel>
<.carousel id="tall" direction="vertical" pagination="bullets" class="h-64">…</.carousel>
<.carousel id="flip" effect="flip" navigation pagination="bullets">…</.carousel>
<.carousel id="peek" gap={30} pagination="bullets">
  <.carousel_slide class="w-10/12">…</.carousel_slide>
</.carousel>

effect is one of Ledger UI's: slide (the scrolling track), fade, flip, cube, cards, coverflow and creative (slides stacked and moved with CSS transforms). pagination is bullets (clickable), fraction, progress (the bar on top) or scrollbar (a draggable bar at the bottom). zoom={4} zooms a slide on double click. A :background slot with data-carousel-parallax="-23%" on it, and elements inside slides with data-carousel-parallax="-300", move at their own pace while the track scrolls.

The previous arrow comes before the next one in the DOM (the tab order), and both point to the track with aria-controls.

Canvas look and thumbnails

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="classic" is the old Ledger UI carousel) is the design canvas carousel: a 16px rounded track, round white arrows (the canvas lu-ib), the fraction as a small mono 1/3 at the top right, and bullets under the track (the active one a long ink pill). :thumb slots draw a row of 64px thumbnails under the track, one per slide, that pick the slide and ring the active one:

<.carousel id="photos" variant="canvas" label="Fotos do produto" class="h-[200px]">
  <.carousel_slide :for={src <- @photos}><img src={src} alt="" class="size-full object-cover" /></.carousel_slide>
  <:thumb :for={src <- @photos}><img src={src} alt="" class="size-full object-cover" /></:thumb>
</.carousel>

The bullets and the thumbnails hang below the carousel's box (the box keeps the slide height) and the carousel reserves their room with a bottom margin.

State

index is the server's slide. The person can move freely in the browser, and their slide survives patches; when the server changes index, the carousel goes there.

Events

on_change (an event name or %JS{}) runs when the active slide changes; an event name is pushed with %{"id" => id, "index" => index} (zero-based) to target, or to the LiveView.

From the server, push_event(socket, "linea:carousel", %{id: "gallery", index: 2}) moves it.

<.carousel>

Renders the carousel. Its children are carousel_slide/1s.

on_change is pushed with %{"id" => id, "index" => index} (zero-based) when the active slide changes; a %JS{} is executed instead. The server moves it by changing index, or with push_event(socket, "linea:carousel", %{id: id, index: n}).

<.carousel id="gallery" index={@slide} on_change="slid" navigation pagination="bullets">
  <.carousel_slide :for={src <- @images}>
    <img class="h-full w-full object-cover" src={src} alt="" />
  </.carousel_slide>
</.carousel>

A metric card made of kit CSS's pieces (card card-border with a stat): the label and the change (a soft badge) on top, the figure with its unit and a sparkline beside it.

<:icon> puts an icon chip before the label, icon_tone colors it. caption is a faint line under the figure, with or without progress. value_id is the id of the figure:

</.kpi_card>

bar_list/1 (a ranking over full-width tracks) and heatmap/1 (dots in five levels) are the canvas's two simpler charts, drawn on the server.

<.chart
  id="sales"
  options={%{
    chart: %{type: "area", height: 350, toolbar: %{show: false}},
    colors: ["#34d399", "#ffba1a"],
    series: [%{name: "Series1", data: [31, 40, 28, 51]}],
    xaxis: %{categories: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"]}
  }}
/>

options is an ApexCharts-shaped options object, as a map or a JSON string (the supported subset is listed below; anything else is ignored). The chart fills the width of its element and redraws when the element resizes. When options changes on the server the chart is redrawn in place. To stream data without re-sending the whole options, push an event:

push_event(socket, "linea:chart", %{id: "sales", series: [%{data: [1, 2, 3]}]})

series is laid over the current series by position (an entry that is a map keeps the name and the settings it does not repeat) and options is merged into the current options.

JSON has no functions, so formatters are named and resolved in the browser. formatters maps an options path to a built-in formatter, and a bare formatter: "name" string inside the options works too:

<.chart
  id="sales"
  formatters={%{"yaxis.labels.formatter" => "thousands", "tooltip.y.formatter" => "dollars"}}
  options={%{series: [...], plotOptions: %{radialBar: %{dataLabels: %{total: %{formatter: "total"}}}}}}
/>
name value becomes
thousands 2500 -> 2.5k (value / 1000, no rounding)
thousands_round 2500 -> 3k
thousands_fixed 2500 -> 2.50k, values under 1000 unchanged
kilo 1499 -> 1k, values under 1000 unchanged
dollars 5 -> $5
dollars_thousands 5000 -> $5k
brl 1284.9 -> R$ 1.284,9 (pt-BR grouping)
brl_thousands 6000 -> R$ 6 mil, 31500 -> R$ 31,5 mil, values under 1000 as brl
brl_kilo 20000 -> R$ 20k, 0 -> 0
brl_kilo_zero as brl_kilo, but 0 -> R$ 0 (every label of the axis carries the currency)
number_br 1248 -> 1.248
total_br for gauges and the donut total: the sum of the series as number_br (takes ApexCharts' w)
total_brl_thousands the donut total as R$ 248 mil (takes ApexCharts' w)
percent 12.5 -> 12.5%
percent_round 12.5 -> 13%
round 2.6 -> 3
hours 3 -> 3h
minutes 45 -> 45 min
none hides the label (empty text)
total for gauges: the sum of the series (takes ApexCharts' w, not a value)

Names not in the table are left as they are. For anything else, before rendering, the chart element dispatches a bubbling linea:chart:options event whose detail.options may be changed.

window.addEventListener("linea:chart:options", ({target, detail}) => {
  target.id === "sales" && (detail.options.yaxis = {labels: {formatter: (v) => "$" + v}})
})

Cursor

The chart tells the page where its cursor is, as the pointer or the arrow keys move it. Three ways, each off unless asked for:

  • the linea:chart:cursor event, always: bubbling, on the chart element, with detail as {index, label, values: [{name, color, value}]} (the values are the ones the tooltip shows, so formatters apply) and a null detail when the cursor leaves.
  • summary: a line above the plot with the label as a chip and one name value per series. It follows the cursor and, when the cursor is gone, shows the last point that has a value. It is not a live region (aria-live="off"): the tooltip and the hidden data table are what assistive technology reads.

  • on_cursor="event": pushes event to the LiveView (to phx-target when the chart has one) with %{"id" => id, "index" => i, "label" => l, "values" => [%{"name" => ..., "color" => ..., "value" => ...}]}, at most every 100 ms, and with "index" => nil and "values" => [] on leave.

    window.addEventListener("linea:chart:cursor", ({target, detail}) => console.log(target.id, detail))

A chart whose tooltip lists one series at a time (bars with tooltip.shared off) reports that series only.

Supported options

The engine reads this subset of the ApexCharts options. Everything else is ignored, never an error. Colors that belong to the theme (axis text, grid, tooltip card, gauge tracks, radar rings) follow Ledger UI's light and dark skin and cannot be set from the options.

Types (chart.type): line, area, bar (columns, or rows with plotOptions.bar.horizontal), rangeBar, candlestick, donut, pie, radialBar and radar. polarArea is drawn as a pie and any other type as a line.

chart: height (a number, "200px", a share of the width such as "50%", or "auto"), width (a number or text such as "120px" that sizes the element; otherwise the chart fills it), stacked, stackType (normal or 100%), sparkline.enabled, dropShadow (enabled, top, left, blur, color, opacity), animations.enabled, parentHeightOffset, defaultLocale (a locale such as "pt-BR": the month and day names of date labels and tooltips, Fev 2026, come from it; English without). The entry animation is short and is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

Data: series ([%{name, data}] where data is numbers, null for a gap, %{x, y} or [x, y]; candlestick y is [open, high, low, close], range bar y is [start, end]; donut, pie and radial bar take a list of numbers), labels (slice names), colors, xaxis.categories. Per-series chart types (combo charts) and several y axes are not supported; the first yaxis entry is the axis.

Lines and areas: stroke (show, curve smooth, straight or stepline, width, colors, dashArray, lineCap; each may be a list per series), markers (size, colors, hover.size, hover.sizeOffset), fill (type solid or gradient, colors, opacity, and gradient with type vertical, horizontal, diagonal1 or diagonal2, shade, shadeIntensity, opacityFrom, opacityTo, stops, inverseColors, gradientToColors). A gradient on a line chart paints the stroke left to right.

Bars: plotOptions.bar with horizontal, columnWidth and barHeight (a share such as "55%", a number meaning the same percentage, or pixels as "24px"), borderRadius, borderRadiusApplication, distributed, rangeBarOverlap and dataLabels.position (center or top; end on rows writes the value just past the end of each bar, in room kept at the right of the plot). A stacked bar rounds the ends of the whole pile. plotOptions.candlestick.colors takes upward and downward.

Axes: xaxis (type category, datetime or numeric, categories, min, max, tickAmount (on a line or area chart of categories: that many gaps, so tickAmount + 1 labels spread evenly), position top, show, labels with show, formatter, format for dates such as "dd MMM", hideOverlappingLabels, offsetX, offsetY, style.fontSize, axisBorder.show, axisTicks.show, crosshairs.show, tooltip.enabled) and yaxis (show, min, max, tickAmount, labels with the same keys plus align ("left" on a vertical chart: the labels start at the left edge of the widest one, as a column of values; the default is right-aligned), axisBorder.show, axisTicks.show, tooltip.enabled). For a horizontal bar the yaxis options drive the category labels and the xaxis ones the value labels. Labels never rotate; the ones that would overlap are thinned out.

Grid: grid.show, grid.strokeDashArray, grid.xaxis.lines.show, grid.yaxis.lines.show and grid.padding (top, right, bottom, left, negative values allowed, as in ApexCharts).

Text: dataLabels (enabled, formatter, offsetX, offsetY, style.fontSize), legend (show, showForSingleSeries, position, layout (table: one row per entry with the name, the value and the share in aligned columns), horizontalAlign, fontSize, markers.size, markers.shape, itemMargin, onItemClick.toggleDataSeries; clicking an entry hides its series; pointing at or tabbing to one puts its series in front: the others dim and a slice or ring grows), tooltip (enabled, shared, intersect, theme light or dark, fillSeriesColor, x.show, x.format, x.formatter, y.formatter, y.title.formatter) and title.text, which names the chart for assistive technology. Each chart also carries a hidden table with its data; the table_toggle attribute of chart/1 adds a Chart / Table switch that shows that table in place of the drawing.

Legend figures: for the parts of a whole (donut, pie, radial bar, and stacked bar or area charts), legend.showValue and legend.showPercent write 524 · 42% after each name: the slice value or the series total, and its share of the entries still shown (a hidden entry keeps its value only). Shape them with legend.value.formatter (any built-in name, such as number_br or brl) and legend.percent.formatter (receives 0 to 100; the default is the rounded number plus %). The percent of a radial bar is not shown, since its values already are percentages.

legend: %{position: "right", showValue: true, showPercent: true, value: %{formatter: "number_br"}}

Keyboard: a chart that can be walked is a tab stop. On a line, area or bar chart the arrow keys, Home and End move the cursor between the points (the tooltip, crosshair and markers follow); on a pie or donut they move between the slices (the tooltip, the highlighted slice and the middle text follow); on a radar between the spokes (the tooltip lists every series on the spoke). Escape or leaving the chart clears it.

Circular charts: plotOptions.pie (startAngle, endAngle, offsetX, offsetY, customScale, donut.size, donut.labels with show, name (name.show: false centers the value alone; value.fontFamily sets its font), value (value.showPercent writes 524 · 42% for the hovered slice), total and layout: "figure", the total large over its label and the hovered slice name over its value, dataLabels.offset), plotOptions.radialBar (startAngle, endAngle, hollow.size, track.show, track.margin, track.strokeWidth, track.opacity, dataLabels with show, name, value and total, each taking show, fontSize, fontWeight, color, offsetY and formatter) and stroke.lineCap. Hovering a donut slice shows its name and value in the middle.

Radar: plotOptions.radar (size, offsetX, offsetY), xaxis.categories for the spokes (their labels are #a8a8a8 unless xaxis.labels.style.colors says otherwise) and yaxis for the ring labels.

Annotations: annotations.yaxis, a list of lines at a value (y) across the plot, with borderColor, borderWidth, strokeDashArray, opacity and a label badge (text, position left or right, offsetX, offsetY, borderRadius, style with background, color, fontSize, fontWeight): a target ("Meta · 60").

Emphasis: xaxis.labels.style.colors and xaxis.labels.style.fontWeight take one value or one per category, to bring one label forward; on bars, stroke.width above zero outlines them, with stroke.colors per bar when distributed. Colors may be CSS variables ("var(--accent)"), which follow the theme.

responsive: rules apply while the window is narrower than their breakpoint, the smaller breakpoints last, as in ApexCharts.

Formatter functions receive the same arguments they do in ApexCharts: (value, opts) for data labels and the tooltip's y, (value, timestamp, opts) for x labels and (w) for the gauge total, with w.config and w.globals.seriesTotals.

<.chart>

Renders a chart. The LedgerUI.Chart hook draws it into an inner element LiveView leaves alone, and redraws it in place whenever the options assign changes.

<.chart
  id="revenue"
  class="max-w-xl"
  options={%{
    chart: %{type: "bar", height: 350, toolbar: %{show: false}},
    colors: ["#ff9800", "#6366f1"],
    plotOptions: %{bar: %{horizontal: true, borderRadius: 5}},
    series: [%{name: "Net Profit", data: @profit}, %{name: "Revenue", data: @revenue}],
    xaxis: %{categories: @months}
  }}
/>

Server push (no re-render), from handle_event/3 or handle_info/2; payload %{id: chart_id, series: [...]} and/or options: %{...}, id with or without #:

push_event(socket, "linea:chart", %{id: "revenue", series: [%{data: [1, 2, 3]}]})

Browser events, bubbling on the chart element: linea:chart:options fires before each draw with detail.options, the place to add JavaScript formatters, and linea:chart:cursor fires as the cursor moves (see Cursor in the module doc).

Attr Type Default Values / notes
id (required) :string DOM id; also what push_event payloads target.
options (required) :any ApexCharts-shaped options, a map (encoded to JSON) or an already encoded JSON string.
formatters :map %{} Options path to built-in formatter name, e.g. %{"yaxis.labels.formatter" => "thousands"}; see the table in the module doc. Applied before every draw.
table_toggle :any false true adds a Chart / Table switch above the chart (a segmented control, answered in the browser) that shows the data table in place of the drawing. A map renames the texts: %{chart: "Gráfico", table: "Tabela", label: "Visualização"}, and its class goes on the row of the switch, to place it elsewhere (for instance "absolute top-4 right-5" with the chart element static, to sit in the header of a card).
summary :boolean false Writes a line above the plot with the label and the value of each series at the cursor, falling back to the last point with data. Not a live region.
on_cursor :string nil Name of a LiveView event pushed (at most every 100 ms) with id, index, label and values as the cursor moves, and with an empty one when it leaves. Off by default.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

A ranking drawn as the canvas does it: each row has its label and its value above a full-width track, filled in proportion to the largest amount. No JavaScript.

<.bar_list label="Maiores clientes por compras">

  <:item label="Mercadinho Bom Preço" value="R$ 31,8 mil" amount={31_800} />
</.bar_list>
Attr Type Default Values / notes
label :string nil The list's aria-label.
max :any nil The amount of a full track; the largest amount when nil.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

Slots:

  • <:item> (required) — attrs: label, value, amount

<.heatmap>

The canvas heat map: a grid of dots in five levels of the accent (--heat0 to --heat4, light and dark), with a "less ... more" scale under it.

<.heatmap levels={@levels} columns={20} label="Vendas por dia" less="Menos" more="Mais" />
Attr Type Default Values / notes
levels (required) :list One level per cell, 0 to 4, row by row.
columns :integer 20
size :integer 12 The cell size in pixels.
shape :string "round" round, square
label (required) :string What the map shows, for assistive technology.
titles :list nil A title per cell (the day and the value).
less :string nil The text before the scale; no scale without it.
more :string nil The text after the scale.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

The chart tells the page where its cursor is, as the pointer or the arrow keys move it. Three ways, each off unless asked for:
