Ledger UI's tables: basic, bordered, hoverable, zebra and the grid look, with :col slots the way Phoenix's generated CoreComponents.table/1 takes them.

<.table id="users" rows={@users}>
  <:col :let={user} label="Name">{user.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={user} label="Job">{user.job}</:col>
</.table>

<.table id="users" rows={@streams.users} variant="hoverable" row_click={&JS.navigate(~p"/users/#{elem(&1, 1)}")}>
  <:col :let={{_id, user}} label="Name">{user.name}</:col>
  <:action :let={{_id, user}}><.button size="xs">Edit</.button></:action>
</.table>

variant="hoverable" and "zebra" draw the filled header; rounded picks its corners: row rounds both ends of the header row (a table inside a padded card), top only the top corners (a table that is the top of a card) and none keeps it square (full width).

Sortable headers: give a column sort_key and the table on_sort; the header becomes a button that sends on_sort with %{"column" => sort_key, "direction" => "asc" | "desc"}, the direction being the one to sort by next. sort_by and sort_dir mark the current order.

<.table id="t" rows={@rows} on_sort="sort" sort_by={@sort_by} sort_dir={@sort_dir}>
  <:col :let={row} label="Name" sort_key="name">{row.name}</:col>
</.table>

Row selection: on_select adds a checkbox column. Each checkbox sends on_select with %{"id" => key, "selected" => "true" | "false"} (the new state of that row); the header one sends on_select_all with %{"selected" => "true" | "false"}. selected is the list of keys checked. The key is row_key.(row), or the row's DOM id when row_key is not given; keys are compared as given, so pass strings or convert the "id" back.

Density and chrome: compact tightens the cell padding, borderless drops the row rules (and the cell borders of bordered), headless leaves out the <thead> altogether. A column's align (left, center, right) aligns its header and cells.

<.table id="stats" rows={@rows} compact borderless headless>
  <:col :let={row}>{row.label}</:col>
  <:col :let={row} align="right">{row.count}</:col>
</.table>

Every event attr takes an event name or a %JS{}; target sets phx-target.

Expandable rows: an :expand slot adds a last column with a chevron that shows a detail row under each row (expand_label names that column). The slot receives %{row: row, toggle: js}, toggle being the JS that opens and closes it. Expandable rows render one <tbody> per row, so they take a list, not a stream.

Per-row markup: row_class and row_attrs are functions of the row giving extra classes and attributes (phx-click, data-*) of its <tr>; :foot cells make a totals row in a <tfoot>; sticky_header pins the header inside a height-bound wrapper.

Columns leave by priority

A :col takes a priority: 0 (default) always stays; 1, 2 and 3 leave, in this order, when the table's own box (a container query, not the window) gets narrower than 720px, 560px and 420px. The header, the cells and the :foot cell of the same priority go together, so a wide table fits a narrow column without a horizontal scroll. Mark the :foot cells like the columns they sit under (a colspan is the app's own, so give it the span of what stays). Tables without a priority are not touched.

<.table id="people" rows={@people}>
  <:col :let={p} label="Name">{p.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={p} label="Owner" priority={2}>{p.owner}</:col>
  <:col :let={p} label="Status" priority={1}>{p.status}</:col>
  <:col :let={p} label="Team"><.avatar src={p.photo} class="table-narrow-hide" /> {p.team}</:col>
</.table>

The class table-narrow-hide hides what carries it (an avatar, an icon) when the box is narrower than 420px. The wrapper becomes the container only when some column has a priority; a hand-written table sets container and marks its :col and :cell entries (and table_cell/1) with priority itself. What left is not shown anywhere else: use expand or a row_click to open the record, or turn on peek.

Peek at what left

peek makes a row show a small panel with label: value of each column the box has hidden, while the row is hovered or has the keyboard focus (the row gets tabindex="0"; on touch, the first tap focuses it). The values come from the same :col render, so custom cell content works, and the label is the caption. The panel is in the DOM next to the first column that always stays, is a role="group" named by peek_label, and is drawn only while some column is actually hidden, so a wide table shows none. It opens upward for the last rows. Nothing changes without peek, or when no :col has a priority. Hand-written tables have no peek.

<.table id="people" rows={@people} peek peek_label="More about this person">
  <:col :let={p} label="Name">{p.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={p} label="Owner" priority={2}>{p.owner}</:col>
</.table>

Hand-written tables

Without rows, the table renders its inner block and its cells take the look of variant, rounded, compact, borderless and sticky_header from it, so rows can carry any markup: per-row attributes, colspans, detail rows, a totals footer.

<.table id="orders" variant="hoverable" rounded="top" class="min-w-[760px]">
  <.table_head on_sort="sort" sort_by={@sort_by} sort_dir={@sort_dir}
    on_select_all="select_all" all_selected={@all?} some_selected={@some?}>
    <:col sort_key="number">Number</:col>
    <:col align="right">Total</:col>
  </.table_head>
  <.table_body id="orders-body" phx-update="stream">
    <.table_row :for={{id, o} <- @streams.orders} id={id} on_click="open" phx-value-id={o.id}
      selected={o.id in @selected} on_select="select" select_value={o.id}>
      <:cell>{o.number}</:cell>
      <:cell align="right">{o.total}</:cell>
    </.table_row>
    <.table_empty id="orders-empty">No orders.</.table_empty>
  </.table_body>
  <.table_foot><:cell>Total</:cell><:cell align="right">{@sum}</:cell></.table_foot>
</.table>

table_cell/1, table_checkbox/1, table_expand_toggle/1 and table_detail_row/1 cover free cells, custom checkboxes and expandable rows; table_skeleton/1 is the loading state. A class given to a cell always wins over the table's look (the look lives in the CSS components layer).

Inside a card, bleed runs the table edge to edge: the wrapper cancels the padding of the card's body (or of the card) as a negative margin and the first and last cells get it back as their own padding, so the rows (hover, zebra, rules) reach the card's sides while the content stays aligned with the rest of the card. As the only thing in a body it also reaches the body's top and bottom and follows its rounded corners. The bordered frame is dropped.

<.card>
  <.card_header><.card_heading>Team</.card_heading></.card_header>
  <.table id="team" rows={@team} bleed>
    <:col :let={person} label="Name">{person.name}</:col>
  </.table>
</.card>

<.table>

Renders a table of rows (a list or a stream), one column per :col slot.

  <:col :let={{_id, person}} label="Name">{person.name}</:col>

  <:action :let={{_id, person}}>

  • on_select — a row checkbox: %{"id" => key, "selected" => "true" | "false"}.
  • on_select_all — the header checkbox: %{"selected" => "true" | "false"}.

With a stream, selected only reaches the rows the server re-renders: stream_insert the rows whose selection changed, and give all_selected for the header checkbox.

A table with a search box, sortable headers, a pagination footer and row selection, in the two looks Ledger UI shows: advanced (the Table Advanced page: a title bar with a search that slides open, the table as a card, "Show 10 entries" and a pager underneath) and grid (the Grid Table page: a search box on the right, sort arrows, "Showing 1 to 10 of 15 results" and Previous/Next).

The LiveView owns the state: it filters, sorts and slices the rows and gives the component the current page; the component only renders it and sends events back.

<.data_table
  id="users"
  rows={@users}
  search={@search}
  on_search="search"
  sort_by={@sort_by}
  sort_dir={@sort_dir}
  on_sort="sort"
  page={@page}
  page_size={10}
  total={@total}
  on_page="paginate"
>
  <:title>Users Table</:title>
  <:col :let={user} label="Name" sort_key="name">{user.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={user} label="Email">{user.email}</:col>
</.data_table>

def handle_event("search", %{"search" => q}, socket), do: ...
def handle_event("sort", %{"column" => col, "direction" => dir}, socket), do: ...
def handle_event("paginate", %{"page" => page}, socket), do: ...

Rows may be a stream (rows={@streams.users}); the body then renders with phx-update="stream" and total drives the footer. :col, :action, :expand, :empty, row_id, row_key, row_item, row_click and selection work as in LedgerUI.Components.Table.table/1, and so do the columns that leave by priority when the box gets narrow, and peek to read them in a panel.

<.data_table>

Renders a data table. The LiveView passes the rows of the current page and handles the events below.

<.data_table
  id="contacts"
  variant="grid"
  rows={@rows}
  total={@total}
  page={@page}
  on_page="paginate"
  search={@search}
  on_search="search"
  sort_by={@sort_by}
  sort_dir={@sort_dir}
  on_sort="sort"
  row_key={& &1.id}
  selected={@selected}
  on_select="select"
  on_select_all="select_all"
>
  <:col :let={c} label="Name" sort_key="name">{c.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={c} label="Email" sort_key="email">{c.email}</:col>
</.data_table>

Events, each an event name or a %JS{} (sent to target when given):

  • on_search — the search input changed or was submitted: %{"search" => query}.
  • on_sort — a sortable header was clicked: %{"column" => sort_key, "direction" => "asc" | "desc"}, the direction to sort by next.
  • on_page — a page was chosen: %{"page" => "3"} (a string, as every phx-value-*). With page_path (a function of the page number) the pager renders patch links instead.
  • on_page_size — the "Show N entries" select changed: %{"page_size" => "30"}.
  • on_select — a row checkbox: %{"id" => key, "selected" => "true" | "false"}.
  • on_select_all — the header checkbox: %{"selected" => "true" | "false"}.

The footer shows when on_page or page_path is given (unless footer={false}); the search when on_search is. The advanced title bar shows only when there is something in it (a :title, the search, :filters or :actions). pager="canvas" is the design canvas footer and loading draws skeleton rows for the first load.

api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

A compact table: one row per record, in a card with a header row and a thin status bar at the left of each row. It is for long lists (orders, invoices, clients) that must stay readable from a wide screen down to a phone, without a horizontal scroll.

<.card_table id="orders" rows={@streams.orders} on_select="select" on_select_all="select_all" selected={@selected}
  status={&order_status/1}>
  <:col :let={o} label="Order" role="head" width="max-content">{o.number}</:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Client" role="title" width="minmax(120px,1.3fr)">{o.client}</:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Issuer" priority={2}>{o.issuer}</:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Value" role="value" align="end">{o.total}</:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Status" role="status"><.badge variant="soft" dot>{o.status}</.badge></:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Balance" priority={1}>{o.balance}</:col>
  <:action :let={o}><.dropdown id={"actions-" <> o.id}>...</.dropdown></:action>
  <:empty>No orders.</:empty>
</.card_table>

Heading

title, description and <:actions> draw a heading above the table, so a list needs no card around it to say what it is and how to add to it:

<.card_table id="portal" rows={@users} title="Portal access" description="Who can see the orders." ...>
  <:actions><.button size="sm">Invite</.button></:actions>
  ...
</.card_table>

<.card_table id="orders" title="Pedidos" meta="128 no período" rows={@orders} ...>
  <:actions><.link navigate={~p"/orders"}>Ver todos</.link></:actions>
  ...
</.card_table>

meta is a small muted text on the same line as the title, right after it. A plain link (or any <a> with no class) in <:actions> is drawn quiet, in the same muted style, pushed to the right: the line reads Pedidos 128 no período ........................ Ver todos. A <.button> keeps its own look.

Footer

<:foot> is a line inside the card, under the rows, set off by a hairline: the place for the pager or a total. Its content is laid out in a wrapping row with the parts spread to the two ends:

<.card_table id="orders" rows={@orders} ...>
  <:col ...>...</:col>
  <:foot>
    <span>Mostrando 1–6 de 128 · 25 / página</span>
    <.pagination ... />
  </:foot>
</.card_table>

Columns leave by priority

The table answers to the width of its own box, not of the window (a container query), so it behaves the same in a narrow column or beside a sidebar. A column has a priority: 0 (default) always stays; 1, 2 and 3 leave, in this order, when the box gets narrower than 1180px, 960px and 720px. What left is not lost: hovering a row (or tabbing to it) opens a panel under it with the label and the value of every column that is hidden.

breakpoints changes those widths: one integer (px) per priority level, in descending order, and the width of the card layout last. The default is [1180, 960, 720, 520]. A table with four priority levels, whose card layout starts under 560px:

<.card_table id="orders" breakpoints={[1180, 980, 760, 640, 560]} ...>
  <:col :let={o} label="Issuer" priority={4}>{o.issuer}</:col>

gives 1 under 1180px, 2 under 980px, 3 under 760px, 4 under 640px and the cards under 560px. Between 2 and 5 integers (1 to 4 priority levels), strictly descending; anything else raises ArgumentError. Container queries cannot read CSS variables, so a table with other widths than the default renders a small <style> scoped to its own id (the same every render, so nothing is sent again over the socket). A priority above the levels of the list never leaves.

Below 520px (the last of breakpoints) the table is one card with a compact two-line grid per row, a hairline between rows, and the role of a column says where it goes: head (first line, left; drawn in mono), status (first line, right), title (second line, left, up to two lines: a name and a sub line) and value (second line, right). The checkbox, if any, sits at the left of both lines. A column with no role and meta are not drawn in the card (the board has no third line) unless it asks to stay (card, see below). The action column stays: it is drawn at the right of both lines, spanning them, so a row can still be edited or deleted on a phone (<:action card={false}> hides it). The header row and the panel are not drawn; "select all" is kept for screen readers and the keyboard only (a visually hidden checkbox that shows when it has focus).

Staying in the card

card on a column keeps it in the card when it has no role (or has meta): it is drawn in a line of its own under the two lines, so a copyable address does not vanish. <:action card={false}> removes the action column from the card.

<:col :let={a} label="Address" role="meta" card copy={& &1.address}>{a.address}</:col>

Expanded and edited rows

<:expand :let={row}> is a full-width line under a row (lots of an item, the items of a contract), drawn inside the row's <li> under the cells. row_expanded is a function of the row that says which rows show it (default: all, when the slot is given). A click inside it also toggles the details panel of the row, so a table that uses expand usually has no hidden columns (no priority) and no detail.

row_editing is a function of the row; when it returns true the row carries data-editing="true" and the <:edit :let={row}> slot (an inline form) takes the place of its cells, across the full width. The checkbox stays; the action cell and the panel are not drawn.

<.card_table id="tasks" rows={@tasks} row_editing={&(&1.id == @editing)} row_expanded={&(&1.id in @open)}>
  <:col :let={t} label="Task" role="title">{t.name}</:col>
  <:edit :let={t}><.form for={@form} phx-submit="save">...</.form></:edit>
  <:expand :let={t}>{t.notes}</:expand>
</.card_table>

row_action is a function of the row; a row for which it returns false has no action cell at all (the track stays empty, the layout does not move).

The details panel

Clicking a row (or tapping it) opens a panel under it with more than the row shows: a list of label and value, one line each. Hovering never opens it. The panel's left edge sits at the click (16px to its left), kept 8px inside both sides of the row, and it does not follow the pointer afterwards. The text of the panel can be selected and copied, and a click inside it keeps it open. It closes on a second click on the row, on Esc (the focus goes back to the row), on a click outside the table, and on a click on any control of the row (link, button, check box, copy button, action menu), which does its own thing. A click on another row moves the panel there. From the keyboard, Enter or Space on a focused row toggles it, at a fixed anchor (96px from the left of the row, 72px under 720px) since there is no pointer. The row carries aria-expanded and data-open (which the CSS uses). The last two rows open it upwards. The CardTable hook (LedgerUI.CardTable, on the rows' list) does this; without it the panel never opens. Give detail slots (<:detail :let={o} label="Due date">{o.due}</:detail>) and the panel lists them first, in the order given, at every width above 520px, then the columns that left at the current width (each shows only once its priority has left; a column with the same label as a detail is not listed again). With no detail, the panel only has the columns that left. Below 520px there is no panel: the card shows what the roles place.

A column may have an empty label (a number or copy column with no header text), and <:action priority={3}> makes the action column leave like a column of that priority.

Copy button

copy on a column (a function of the row that returns the text) turns its cell into a copy button, as in the order number of the design. Its tooltip shows the text it copies and, for two seconds after a copy, copied_label (copy_label is the button's accessible name). The column's own content stays visible only in the card, where there is no tooltip. The button shows a check while it says copied_label (two seconds).

copy_show="inline" keeps the column's own content visible before the button at every width, 8px apart (ORD-2041 [copy]), instead of only in the card:

<:col :let={o} label="Pedido" role="head" copy={& &1.number} copy_show="inline"
  copy_label="Copiar número">{o.number}</:col>

copy_tip="value_label" changes the tooltip to the value in bold mono, a dot, and the label in the text font: ORD-2041 · Copiar número, and after the copy ORD-2041 · Número copiado:

<:col :let={o} label="Pedido" role="head" copy={& &1.number} copy_tip="value_label"
  copy_label="Copiar número" copied_label="Número copiado">{o.number}</:col>

Sub lines

<.ctable_sub> is a second line inside a cell (12px, faint) that leaves by its own priority, with the same widths as the columns (default or custom breakpoints), while the cell stays. No priority: always shown. The panel of a row lists whole columns, so a sub line inside a column that left is shown there.

<:col :let={o} label="Cliente" role="title" width="minmax(120px,1.3fr)">
  {o.client}
  <.ctable_sub priority={2}>{o.issuer}</.ctable_sub>
</:col>
<:col :let={o} label="Valor" role="value" align="end">
  {o.total}
  <.ctable_sub priority={1}>saldo {o.balance} · {o.pending} pend.</.ctable_sub>
</:col>

when_hidden="p2" is the inverse: the sub line shows only once the columns of priority 2 have left, so the data is not shown twice on a wide screen (p1 to p4). A ctable_sub inside a role="head" column is not drawn in mono in the card.

<:col :let={o} label="Cliente" role="title">
  {o.client}
  <.ctable_sub when_hidden="p2">{o.issuer}</.ctable_sub>
</:col>
<:col :let={o} label="Emissor" priority={2}>{o.issuer}</:col>

Columns

width is the CSS track of the column (max-content by default; minmax(120px,1.3fr) to let it take what is left). align is start (default) or end (numbers). Text is cut with an ellipsis; truncate={false} lets it wrap (in the card too: a role="title" is not cut at two lines then; with the default, even a lu-cellx of avatar and text ends in an ellipsis). sort_key with the table's on_sort makes the header a button, as in table/1.

Rows

rows is a list or a stream. status is a function of the row that returns a color (success, info, warning, error, primary...) for the thin bar at the left of the row, or nil for the neutral (input border) bar. on_select adds a checkbox column (the events and keys work as in table/1: selected, row_key, on_select_all). row_attrs gives extra attributes of a row (phx-click, data-*).

<:foot> and <:empty> receive a map (:let={ctx}) with id, rows, selected and title of the table, so they can show a total or a message that depends on it: <:foot :let={ctx}>{length(ctx.rows)} rows</:foot> (the rows of a stream are not enumerable; use your own assign there). Without :let the argument is ignored.

bordered={false} draws the table with no border, shadow or background of its own, to nest it in a card that has other blocks (a chart and a table) without a double border.

Flat

variant="flat" is the canvas card table: a plain table in a card (a kit CSS card and table), for short lists on a dashboard ("Últimos pedidos", "Maiores clientes"). The title and <:actions> (a "Ver todos" link, drawn quiet) head the card; <:top> takes the place of the heading (tabs that filter the table). Columns keep label, align and class, and also take priority, role and card: a column leaves at the default widths (1180, 960 and 720px, breakpoints is not read), and under 520px, when some column has a role, each row becomes a card as in the default variant (meta too, and the action cell stays). The panel, the selection, expand and edit belong to the default variant. description goes under the title and <:foot> under the table (a "Total" line), as in the default variant.

<.card_table id="last" variant="flat" title="Últimos pedidos" rows={@orders}>
  <:actions><.link navigate={~p"/orders"}>Ver todos</.link></:actions>
  <:col :let={o} label="Pedido">{o.number}</:col>
  <:col :let={o} label="Total" align="end">{o.total}</:col>
</.card_table>

The filters above the table and the pager under it are not part of it: build them with input, select, button and pagination, inside the same card.

A table with a search box, sortable headers, a pagination footer and row selection, in the two looks Ledger UI shows: advanced (the Table Advanced page: a title bar with a search that slides open, the table as a card, "Show 10 entries" and a pager underneath) and grid (the Grid Table page: a search box on the right, sort arrows, "Showing 1 to 10 of 15 results" and Previous/Next).

The LiveView owns the state: it filters, sorts and slices the rows and gives the component the current page; the component only renders it and sends events back.

  rows={@users}
  search={@search}
  on_search="search"

  sort_dir={@sort_dir}
  on_sort="sort"
  page={@page}
  page_size={10}
  total={@total}
  on_page="paginate"
>

  <:col :let={user} label="Name" sort_key="name">{user.name}</:col>

</.data_table>

def handle_event("sort", %{"column" => col, "direction" => dir}, socket), do: ...

A floating bar of bulk actions for a table with selection: the count of what is selected in a badge, a field to change one attribute (a status, an owner, a label), buttons for the actions and a close that clears the selection. It appears only while count is above zero.

<.bulk_bar
  id="orders-bulk"
  count={@count}
  label="order selected"
  label_plural="orders selected"
  total={@total}
  on_select_all="select_all"
  on_clear="clear_selection"
>
  <:field>
    <.select name="status" options={@statuses} value={@status} search="none" placeholder="Change status" />
  </:field>
  <:action variant="primary" disabled={is_nil(@status)} phx-click="apply">Apply to {@count}</:action>
  <:action variant="danger" icon="huge-delete-02" phx-click="delete">Delete</:action>
</.bulk_bar>

The texts come from outside: label and label_plural (the part after the badge), select_all_label (%{total} is replaced) and clear_label. Nothing is pluralized here, so any language works.

Looks

variant="inverse" (default) is the opposite of the page: a dark bar on a light page, a light one on a dark page. soft is the page's own surface with a ring, for when the inverted bar weighs too much. solid is the canvas bar: the --solid surface, the count written in bold ("3 selecionados") instead of a badge, no separators, rounded sm buttons (soft, ghost, danger...), and a close button only when there is an on_clear. floating (default) pins the bar to the bottom center of the viewport above the page; floating={false} lays it out where it is, for a bar inside a card or a toolbar.

Slots

:field holds a control (a select, an input); it is skinned as a quiet field the height of the buttons, and a listbox inside it opens upwards when the bar is floating. :action is a button: variant is default, primary (the one main action, disabled until there is something to apply) or danger (last, in red; it only looks the part, so confirm in your handler or with data-confirm); icon is a Hugeicons name; every other attribute (phx-click, phx-value-*, data-*) goes to the button. A disabled action keeps the focus (it is aria-disabled, not a native disabled) and does nothing: its phx-* attributes are not rendered.

Progress

While a bulk action runs, progress (done) and progress_max (all) turn the bar into a progress bar: the label in bold as it is given (no count before it), a meter and the "5/12" fraction.

<.bulk_bar id="emit" count={12} variant="solid" label="Emitindo 12 notas…" progress={5} progress_max={12} />

Confirm

An :action with confirm (a title) asks first: the button opens a small card under the bar (above it when floating) with confirm_text, a cancel and a confirm button; only the confirm button runs the action's phx-click.

<:action variant="danger" icon="huge-delete-02" phx-click="delete" confirm="Excluir 3 pedidos?"
  confirm_text="Os rascunhos somem para todos." confirm_label="Excluir" cancel_label="Cancelar">
  Excluir
</:action>

Keyboard

Esc clears the selection (it presses the close button), unless it was meant for an open list or another control. show_esc writes the key as a chip in the close button. The bar is a labelled region and announces the count as it changes.

The board is a role="group"; give it an aria-label (aria-label="Sales funnel") so it is announced. A column with a limit (a work in progress limit) turns the pill and the bar red when the count goes over it (data-wip="exceeded"); the text of the stats line is yours (meta="limit of 3 in progress" total="4 of 3"). A disabled column is drawn at 60% opacity.

The board is one LedgerUI.Sortable hook: every column is a list (data-list), every card an item (data-id), and all the columns of the board are in one group, so a card can be dropped on any of them or reordered inside its own. Dropping pushes event (to target when given, else the LiveView) with the card's and the columns' ids and the index the card takes there:

def handle_event("move", %{"id" => id, "from" => from, "to" => to, "index" => index}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, update(socket, :orders, &Orders.move(&1, id, from, to, index))}

Nothing is moved in the browser, the server's render is the new order. While a card is dragged the original stays as a quiet dashed placeholder (data-dragging), a lifted copy of the card follows the pointer (tilting a little towards the movement, with a big soft shadow) and, on a drop, glides into its slot or flies back when the drop is cancelled. The cards of the column under the pointer (data-over, which only tints the column) slide out of the way as the copy crosses them, opening a gap with a dashed placeholder, and the board and the columns scroll when the pointer is near their edges. A drop where the card already was pushes nothing. A mouse, a pen and a finger share this: a mouse or a pen drags after moving a few pixels (a click on the card, a link or a button in it still works), a finger holds the card for a moment first. Escape cancels. A button in the card that pushes the same event with the next column (phx-click) is the alternative for the keyboard and for screens where dragging is awkward.

Another board

The old kanban of an admin template (columns that are reordered by a handle, free-form cards) needs no column: put phx-hook="LedgerUI.Sortable" on your own list and the data attributes of the hook on it.

<div id="columns" phx-hook="LedgerUI.Sortable" data-event="move_column" data-list="columns" data-handle=".grip" data-axis="x">
  <div :for={col <- @columns} data-id={col.id}>...</div>
</div>

A list that holds the cards of a column in its own group does the same for the cards:

<div id={"cards-#{col.id}"} phx-hook="LedgerUI.Sortable" data-group="cards" data-list={col.id} data-event="move_card">
  <.card :for={card <- col.cards} data-id={card.id}>...</.card>
</div>

A single list with no group is a sortable list, e.g. a to-do list:

<div id="todos" phx-hook="LedgerUI.Sortable" data-list="todos" data-event="reorder">
  <div :for={todo <- @todos} data-id={todo.id}>{todo.title}</div>
</div>

The attributes of the hook, on a list or on the element that holds the lists (a list's own wins):

  • data-event - the server event to push on a drop.
  • data-target - its phx-target; without it the LiveView of the hook gets the event.
  • data-group - lists with the same group exchange items; without one an item stays in its list.
  • data-list - the list's id, sent as from and to.
  • data-handle - a CSS selector inside the item; only a drag that starts on it moves the item.
  • data-axis - x for items laid in a row, y (default) for items stacked.
  • data-disabled - the list neither gives nor takes items (any value but false).

Items carry data-id, the id the server gets as id. The default look comes from parts/sortable.css: a quiet [data-dragging] item, the lifted .linea-drag-ghost and the dashed .linea-drop-slot, all zero-specificity and easy to override with utilities.

Layout

The server lays the steps out (no JavaScript, no measuring): edges is a list of maps with from and to (node ids) and, optionally, label and status. A node's row is its depth along the edges; a parent is centred over its children, the children stand side by side and every connection is an SVG path drawn in the gap above its target, with the label on it. A gap with a branch or a label is taller than a plain one. Edges are expected to join one row to the next; an edge that skips rows is drawn in the gap above its target, from the column of its source. A flow with no edges is a free grid: the nodes in the order given, four to a row.

status: "done" paints a traversed edge green and "error" red; an edge into the selected node takes the accent colour. An edge with no status is the neutral line, which is how the branch not taken of a run reads.

Nodes

A :node has a kind tab (text in kind, glyph in kind_icon) joined to a card with the title, the icon, the sections (flow_section/1, the content of the slot) and a footer of metrics. status is running, done, waiting, error or skipped and the tab gets its dot; selected takes the accent colour and renders the :actions slot beside the card (with the node id as the slot argument). With on_add set, the nodes with no outgoing edge get the + button under them; it pushes on_add (an event name or a %JS{}) with phx-value-id of the node.

The :hint slot is a floating note on the board (<:hint title="Comece pelo gatilho">Depois use o +…</:hint>): the title in bold above the text, placed at left/top (372 and 92 px of the stage, to the right of a first node) and width (240).

The :toolbar slot is the bar at the bottom of the board. The :panel slot is the aside on the right, composed with flow_panel_head/1, flow_panel_tabs/1, flow_panel_body/1 and flow_panel_foot/1 and the rest of the kit (tabs, input, select, button...); without it the board takes the whole width. Give the board a height (class="h-[640px]") and an aria-label.

The server owns what the calendar shows, because the events of another period have to be loaded: view and date come from your assigns, and the toolbar (previous, next, today, month and week) and the keyboard push the events below with the date and view to show next. Update the assigns and load that period's events with calendar_range/3:

def handle_event("calendar_navigate", %{"date" => date, "view" => view}, socket) do
  {:noreply, assign(socket, date: Date.from_iso8601!(date), view: view)}
end

An event is a map with :date (a Date or ISO text) and :title, and optionally :id, :subtitle, :color (neutral primary secondary info success warning error), and :start and :end ("09:00" or a Time). In the week view an event with a :start is a block in its hour; the others sit in an all-day row.

%{id: 1, title: "Coelba", date: ~D[2026-10-15], color: "error"}
%{id: 2, title: "Visit", subtitle: "Santa Mônica", date: ~D[2026-10-19], start: "10:00", end: "11:00"}

Mini month

variant="mini" is the canvas's compact month in a card: one-letter weekdays, the days in round cells, a dot under the days that have events, the selected day in solid ink, a range painted in the accent tint and today ringed. months_shown={2} puts two months side by side (for long periods), each in its own card titled with the month's name. on_select makes the days buttons; on_navigate (single month with header) gives the title its arrows. marks="tint" paints the days with events in their color instead of a dot (a due calendar: to receive and to pay), and legend is then drawn over the grid with square keys.

<.calendar id="due" variant="mini" header={false} date={~D[2026-11-01]} locale="pt_BR"
           events={for d <- [5, 10], do: %{title: "Vencimento", date: Date.new!(2026, 11, d)}} />
<.calendar id="range" variant="mini" months_shown={2} header={false} locale="pt_BR"
           date={~D[2026-11-01]} range={{~D[2026-11-20], ~D[2026-12-06]}} />

The grid is role="grid": Tab lands on one day, the arrows move between days (past the first or the last day they go to the previous or the next period), Home and End go to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down change period, and Enter or Space selects the day. locale="pt_BR" names months and weekdays in Portuguese, like date_picker, and writes the labels of the toolbar in Portuguese.

The canvas variant is the default (below); card is the old Ledger UI centered block for a whole area; the inline one is a compact notice for inside tables, lists and search results, in a neutral, success or error color.

api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

The canvas's error screens: the whole page an ErrorHTML renders (404, 500, 403, 401/419, 429, 503 and offline) and the error inside the app, under the shell.

<.error_page code={404} request_id={@request_id}>
  <:brand><img src={~p"/images/logo.svg"} class="size-8.5" /> <b>Acme</b></:brand>
  <:status href="https://status.acme.com">All systems operational</:status>
  <:actions>
    <.button navigate={~p"/"} color="primary" size="lg">Back home</.button>
  </:actions>
  <.error_links title="Maybe you were looking for">
    <:link navigate={~p"/orders"} icon="huge-invoice-01" description="Every order">Orders</:link>
  </.error_links>
  <:card>Orders with a similar number…</:card>
  <:footer><a href="/help">Help center</a></:footer>
</.error_page>

<.error_state code={404} title="Order #2499 not found">
  It may have been deleted or belong to another branch.
  <:actions><.button navigate={~p"/orders"} color="primary">See every order</.button></:actions>
</.error_state>

code is the HTTP status (an integer or text, "OFF" for offline). It picks the color of the big code (tone: neutral for 404, error for 5xx, warning for 403, 429 and offline, accent for 401, 419 and 503) and the English defaults of label (error_page), title and description (and of the error_state icon), all of which you pass translated.

The page

On the left, the code and its label, the title, the description, the actions and the inner block (the canvas puts error_links/1 or an alert there). On the right, the dotted panel with rings, the code in 230px mono fading down and the card slot floating over it (a search with similar records, the log line of a 500, the permissions of a 403...). On top, the brand and the status link (a dot in the color of status: ok, warning or down); at the bottom the request_id with a copy button, the timestamp and the footer (help links). Under 1100px the panel goes below the text; on a phone it is hidden.

It is a whole page: render it as the ErrorHTML template, with the root layout that loads the CSS (render_errors: [formats: [html: MyAppWeb.ErrorHTML], root_layout: {MyAppWeb.Layouts, :root}]). The styles are canvas-error-page.css (lu-err).

<.error_page>

Renders the whole error page.

tone :string nil `,neutral,error,warning,accent— The color of the code; bycodewhennil`.
label :string nil The words after the code chip (Page not found).
title :string nil
description :string nil
request_id :string nil Shown in the footer with a copy button.
request_id_label :string "Request ID"
copy_label :string "Copy request ID"

It copies with an inline onclick (navigator.clipboard) and sets data-copied for two seconds, so it works on a plain ErrorHTML page with no LiveView or hook; a CSP that forbids inline handlers needs unsafe-inline for it, and the click on the id still selects it whole.

api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

Ledger UI's tabs: underlined (line), on a gray track (boxed), rounded (pill), plain text (text) and the design canvas segmented control (segmented), laid out horizontally or vertically, with or without icons. A tab's count draws the canvas count badge after its label.

<.tabs id="profile-tabs" selected="home">
  <:tab name="home">Home</:tab>
  <:tab name="profile">Profile</:tab>
  <:panel name="home">…</:panel>
  <:panel name="profile">…</:panel>
</.tabs>

<.tabs id="boxed" variant="boxed">
  <:tab name="home"><svg class="size-4.5">…</svg><span>Home</span></:tab>
  <:panel name="home">…</:panel>
</.tabs>

The selected tab comes from selected and switching happens in the browser (click, ←/→ or ↑/↓, Home and End) without a round trip. A choice made in the browser survives patches; when the server changes selected, the server wins.

on_change tells the server what was chosen:

<.tabs id="server-tabs" selected={@tab} on_change="select_tab">…</.tabs>
<.tabs id="period" variant="boxed" size="sm"><:tab name="month">Last month</:tab></.tabs>
<.tabs id="range" variant="text"><:tab name="week">Last 7 days</:tab><:tab name="all">All time</:tab></.tabs>
<.tabs id="view" variant="segmented"><:tab name="summary">Summary</:tab><:tab name="items">Items</:tab></.tabs>
<.tabs id="status"><:tab name="all" count={128}>All</:tab><:tab name="late" count={4}>Late</:tab></.tabs>

def handle_event("select_tab", %{"id" => "server-tabs", "value" => tab}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, tab: tab)}

Every selection also dispatches a bubbling linea:change DOM event with detail: %{id: id, value: name, tab: name}.

Navigation tabs

Tabs without :panels switch routes instead of panels: give each :tab a patch, navigate or href and it renders as a <.link>, so the browser goes there with no handle_event round trip, and selected (the current route's tab) carries aria-current="page":

<.tabs id="customer-tabs" variant="line" bordered selected={@live_action |> to_string()}>
  <:tab name="show" patch={~p"/customers/#{@customer}"}>Details</:tab>
  <:tab name="orders" patch={~p"/customers/#{@customer}/orders"}>Orders</:tab>
  <:tab name="history" navigate={~p"/customers/#{@customer}/history"}>History</:tab>
</.tabs>

variant="nav" renders the canvas navigation tabs, a kit CSS tabs tabs-border of links (<nav class="tabs tabs-border"><a class="tab tab-active">…</a></nav>) (14px links, a 2px underline on the current one). It is for routes only: no hook, no roles, no panels, and on_change is never pushed. selected may be nil (none is current). A :tab without patch, navigate or href (or with them nil/false) is never current: with phx-click (and phx-target, phx-value-*) it is a clickable <a role="button">, with soon or disabled it is a dimmed, non-clickable <a aria-disabled="true"> titled with soon_label.

<.tabs id="system-tabs" variant="nav" selected={@section}>
  <:tab name="overview" navigate={~p"/system"}>Overview</:tab>
  <:tab name="tasks" navigate={~p"/system/tasks"} count={12}>Tasks</:tab>
  <:tab name="finance" phx-click="soon">Finance</:tab>
  <:tab name="contracts" soon>Contracts</:tab>
</.tabs>

A tab only points at a panel (aria-controls) when a :panel with its name exists, so navigation tabs carry no dangling references. The arrow keys move the focus between link tabs; Enter follows the focused one.

<.tabs>

Renders a tab list and its panels. Each :tab is matched to the :panel with the same name.

<.tabs id="settings" selected={@tab} variant="boxed" on_change="tab_changed">
  <:tab name="general">General</:tab>
  <:tab name="billing" disabled>Billing</:tab>
  <:panel name="general">…</:panel>
  <:panel name="billing">…</:panel>
</.tabs>

Events: with on_change="tab_changed" the hook pushes "tab_changed" with %{"id" => "settings", "value" => "general", "tab" => "general"} (to target or the closest LiveComponent) after the browser switched; with on_change={%JS{}} the commands run on the tabs element. Either way a bubbling linea:change DOM event carries detail: %{id, value, tab}; tab repeats value.

Attr Type Default Values / notes
id (required) :string Needed by the hook and for the tab/panel ids.
selected :string nil The name of the selected tab; the first one when not given.
variant :string "line" line, boxed, pill, text, segmented, nav — line underlines the selected tab, boxed lifts it off a gray track, pill fills a rounded tab, text is plain text that only changes color (no border or background; spacing comes from list_class, space-x-4 by default), segmented is the segmented control (kit CSS tabs-box: the selected tab raised on the track), nav is a tabs-border nav of links (see Navigation tabs).
size :string "md" xs, sm, md — For boxed: md is px-3 py-1.5, sm is Ledger UI's compact px-3 py-1 text-xs-plus, xs is px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs.
color :string "primary" primary, neutral — The fill of the selected pill tab and the text color of the selected text tab.
orientation :string "horizontal" horizontal, vertical
bordered :boolean false For line: draws the gray rule the tabs sit on.
overlap :boolean false For a bordered line: the selected tab's line covers the gray rule instead of sitting on it.

Views

views are the tabs: maps with :label and :value, and optionally :icon (a huge-* name), :count and :disabled. The tab whose value is value is the chosen one. A tab is a button that sends on_change with %{"view" => value}; a view with :patch, :navigate or :href is a link instead, and the chosen one carries aria-current="page":

views={[
  %{label: "List", value: "list", patch: ~p"/invoices?view=list"},
  %{label: "Board", value: "board", patch: ~p"/invoices?view=board"}
]}

The menu

options are the views on offer: maps with :label and :value, and optionally :icon, :description, :added (a check at the end, for a view that is already a tab) and :disabled. Choosing one sends on_add with %{"view" => value} and closes the menu. Without options there is no button. add_label and menu_title are its texts and columns is 2 or 1.

The menu is a dropdown/1 (id is "#{id}-add"): it floats in the top layer, flips when there is no room, works with ↑ ↓ Home End, letters and Esc, and closes with LedgerUI.close(socket, "invoice-views-add").

Ledger UI's breadcrumb: the links to the pages above the current one, then the current page.

<.breadcrumb>
  <:item navigate={~p"/"}>Home</:item>
  <:item navigate={~p"/elements"}>Elements</:item>
  <:item>Breadcrumb</:item>
</.breadcrumb>

An item with href, navigate or patch is a link; one with phx-click is a button that looks like a link, so a crumb can navigate through a server event; the others are plain text (the current page is the last one). Any other attribute of the item (phx-target, phx-value-*, id, data-*, aria-*) is passed on to the link or button.

<.breadcrumb>
  <:item :for={folder <- @path} phx-click="open_folder" phx-value-id={folder.id}>
    {folder.name}
  </:item>
</.breadcrumb>

href, navigate and patch that are nil or false count as absent, so a step built with <:item :for={step <- @steps} navigate={step.to}> is plain text when it has no destination.

The current page is in the soft text color and a long label is cut with an ellipsis; give the item a title for the full label.

A long trail collapses with max_items: it keeps the first step and the last ones, and the steps in between become a single "…" button that opens them in a dropdown (links and phx-click steps keep working there). max_items counts the "…" as a step, so max_items={4} shows the first step, "…" and the last two. Give the breadcrumb an id: the dropdown's is "<id>-more".

<.breadcrumb id="path" max_items={4}>
  <:item navigate={~p"/finance"}>Finance</:item>
  <:item navigate={~p"/finance/reconciliation"}>Reconciliation</:item>
  <:item navigate={~p"/finance/reconciliation/statements"}>Statements</:item>
  <:item>October</:item>
</.breadcrumb>

It is kit CSS's breadcrumbs, whose own separator goes between the steps unless a :separator is given:

<.breadcrumb variant="bordered">
  <:separator><span class="text-xs font-light">/</span></:separator>
  <:item href="/"><svg>…</svg></:item>
  <:item>Calendar</:item>
</.breadcrumb>

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="plain" is the old Ledger UI trail) is the design canvas trail: muted 13px links, faint / separators and the current page in the ink, inside a <b> with aria-current="page" on its wrapper.

<.breadcrumb>
  <:item navigate={~p"/customers"}>Customers</:item>
  <:item>Casa das Tintas</:item>
</.breadcrumb>

The pagination: the design canvas pager by default (shape="canvas"), or Ledger UI's joined bar or divided buttons, rounded or pill (shape="rounded" is the old default), in three sizes.

<.pagination page={@page} total_pages={10} patch={&"/orders?page=#{&1}"} />
<.pagination page={@page} total_pages={10} navigate={&"/orders?page=#{&1}"} divided shape="rounded" />
<.pagination page={@page} total_pages={10} on_change="paginate" shape="pill" />

Each page is a link when patch, navigate or href is given: a function from the page number to the path. Otherwise it is a button pushing on_change with %{"page" => "3"} (to target when given). Pages far from the current one collapse into an ellipsis: siblings pages are kept on each side of the current one and boundaries at each end.

A list footer: total_entries and page_size add the "Showing 1–15 of 128" summary on the left (and work out total_pages), page_sizes a rows-per-page select pushing on_page_size.

<.pagination
  page={@page}
  page_size={@per_page}
  total_entries={@total}
  page_sizes={[15, 30, 50]}
  on_change="paginate"
  on_page_size="per_page"
  summary="Mostrando %{first}–%{last} de %{total}"
  page_size_label="%{size} / página"
/>

%{shown} is the rows on the current page (6 of 14 charges), and an :aside slot puts content at the right of the pages, or in place of them when there is a single page. With class="lu-pager" the footer takes the canvas pager look:

<.pagination class="lu-pager" page={@page} page_size={10} total_entries={14}
  summary="%{shown} de %{total} cobranças" on_change="paginate">
  <:aside>Webhook recebido há 2 min</:aside>
</.pagination>

<.pagination>

Renders the page links between a previous and a next arrow.

<.pagination page={@page} total_pages={@total} patch={&"/orders?page=#{&1}"} />
<.pagination page={@page} total_pages={@total} on_change="paginate" target={@myself} />

With on_change="paginate" every page and arrow is a button pushing "paginate" with %{"page" => "3"} (the page as a string):

def handle_event("paginate", %{"page" => page}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, page: String.to_integer(page))}

The arrow at either end and the ellipsis (…) are inert <span>s.

With total_entries or page_sizes the bar becomes a footer row: the summary (role="status") on the left, the select and the pages on the right. The select sits in its own <form> and pushes on_page_size with %{"page_size" => "30"} (to target), so do not put the pagination inside another form.

def handle_event("per_page", %{"page_size" => size}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, per_page: String.to_integer(size), page: 1)}

page (required) :integer The current page, from 1.
total_pages :integer nil How many pages there are. Worked out from total_entries and page_size when not given.
total_entries :integer nil Rows across every page; shows the summary.
page_size :integer nil Rows per page; the select's current value.
page_sizes :list [] Options of the rows-per-page select.
on_page_size :any nil Event name or %JS{} of the select's form, pushed with %{"page_size" => "30"}.
summary :string "Showing %{first}–%{last} of %{total}" The summary text; %{first}, %{last}, %{shown} (the rows on the current page) and %{total} are replaced.
page_size_label :string "%{size} / page" Text of each select option; %{size} is replaced.
page_size_aria :string "Rows per page" aria-label of the select.
siblings :integer 1 Pages kept on each side of the current one.
boundaries :integer 1 Pages kept at each end.

navigate :any nil A function from a page number to a path to navigate to.
href :any nil A function from a page number to a URL.
on_change :any nil Used when no link function is given: an event name pushed with %{"page" => "3"}, or a %JS{} run on click (its JS.push carries the same page value).
target :any nil The phx-target of on_change.

color paints every point and the line between them; a step's own color paints only its point. The content of a step is what its point shows (a number, an icon or nothing). A step's state (done, current, error, todo) picks its color and marks the current one.

stepper/1 is the progress version for wizards and checklists: states drawn as a bar and a numbered, checked or flagged dot, with a sub line and room for an action.

<.stepper>

Renders a stepper: the steps of a wizard or a checklist, each done, current, error or todo.

Give current (the index of the step being worked on, from 0) and the others follow: the ones before are done, the ones after are to do, and with error the current one is flagged. A :step can also carry its own state. The current step (and a flagged one) has aria-current="step"; every step has its state as hidden text for screen readers.

<.stepper current={@step} error={@failed}>

  <:step label="Certificate" sub="File and password" />
</.stepper>

A dropdown_submenu nests a menu that opens to the side, on hover, on click, or with → (← or Esc goes back to its parent):

<.dropdown id="row" toggle_icon="dots">
  <.dropdown_item phx-click="edit">Edit</.dropdown_item>
  <.dropdown_submenu label="Move to">
    <.dropdown_item phx-click="move" phx-value-to="archive">Archive</.dropdown_item>
    <.dropdown_item phx-click="move" phx-value-to="trash">Trash</.dropdown_item>
  </.dropdown_submenu>
</.dropdown>

The menu floats above the page: opened, it sits in the browser's top layer (popover="manual", position: fixed, placed from the trigger's rectangle), so a table's horizontal scroll area, a drawer's scrolling body or an ancestor's z-index / transform neither cut it off nor cover it, and the "…" menu in the last column of a table opens whole. It follows the page and any box around the trigger as they scroll, flips to the other side when there is no room, and closes when its trigger scrolls out of sight. It stays in the LiveView's DOM where it was rendered, so patches and phx-click on items work as usual. Without the Popover API (old browsers) it is a fixed box on --ledger-z-popover.

A filter menu

dropdown_checkbox and dropdown_radio are items that keep the menu open while they are toggled (menuitemcheckbox and menuitemradio); a dropdown_submenu groups them and shows how many are checked; dropdown_footer ends the menu with Clear / Apply. keep_submenus leaves an open submenu open while the pointer moves elsewhere. Inside a form, an item with a name is a real (hidden) input, so the form's phx-change hears every tick and phx-submit gets the checked ones:

<.form for={@form} phx-change="filter" phx-submit="apply">
  <.dropdown id="filters" label="Filter" keep_submenus close_on_select={false}>
    <.dropdown_submenu label="Status">
      <.dropdown_checkbox
        :for={status <- @statuses}
        name="filter[status][]"
        value={status}
        checked={status in @filter.status}
        count={@counts[status]}
      >
        {status}
      </.dropdown_checkbox>
    </.dropdown_submenu>
    <.dropdown_separator />
    <.dropdown_label>Sort by</.dropdown_label>
    <.dropdown_radio name="filter[sort]" value="recent" checked={@filter.sort == "recent"}>
      Most recent
    </.dropdown_radio>
    <.dropdown_radio name="filter[sort]" value="value" checked={@filter.sort == "value"}>
      Highest value
    </.dropdown_radio>
    <.dropdown_footer locale="pt_BR" />
  </.dropdown>
</.form>

Without a form, give an item phx-click and phx-value-*; the checked state is the item's checked (the server wins when it changes it, a patch that did not change it keeps what was ticked in the browser).

A long menu scrolls inside a scroll_area (LedgerUI.Components.ScrollArea); keep submenus out of a scrolling box inside the menu, which would clip them.

The keyboard works as in a menu (↑ ↓ Home End, letters, Esc, Tab). It opens and closes from the browser (LedgerUI.toggle("actions")), from the server (LedgerUI.close(socket, "actions")) or from open; on_open / on_close run whoever opened or closed it.

Ledger UI's menu lists: a vertical list of links with one active entry.

<.menu_list variant="solid">
  <:item navigate={~p"/start"} active>Getting start</:item>

An icon is the first child of an item; Ledger UI's icon colors (muted, darker on hover, current color when active) come with it:

<:item href="#"><svg class="size-5">…</svg><span>Payments</span></:item>

A trailing count (a badge, a number) goes in the :count slot of a menu_item, or in the count attr of an :item; it is pushed to the end of the row:

<.menu_item navigate="/inbox" variant="solid">
  <:icon><svg class="size-5">…</svg></:icon>
  Inbox
  <:count><.badge size="sm" shape="pill">12</.badge></:count>
</.menu_item>

variant follows Ledger UI's examples: link (text only), solid (filled; color picks primary or neutral), pill (rounded with a tinted hover), gradient and bordered.

Items that are not links take on_select (an event name or %JS{}), pushed with %{"value" => item_value}:

<.menu_list on_select="pick">
  <:item value="shipping">Shipping</:item>
</.menu_list>

variant="static" is the canvas lu-list: plain rows (menu_row) with an icon, a title over a sub line, a value at the right and an unread dot; see menu_row.

Streams render one menu_item per row:

<.menu_list id="pages" rows={@streams.pages}>
  <:row :let={{_id, page}}>
    <.menu_item navigate={page.path} active={page.id == @current}>{page.title}</.menu_item>
  </:row>
</.menu_list>

Unlike the generic LedgerUI.Components.Dropdown it has a look of its own so it is not mistaken for the content behind it: a raised background, a stronger outline and a shadow, in the dark theme too. While it is open the button looks pressed and the item's row is tinted, so it is clear whose actions these are.

label is the accessible name of the button. The optional :title slot is the header with the item's name. An item with href, navigate or patch is a link, any other is a button (phx-click...). disabled items stay in the menu and say why in their hint; the keys skip them and they carry aria-disabled. danger paints an item in the error color (put it last).

It uses the Dropdown's machinery (hook LedgerUI.ActionMenu, a Dropdown hook with the row marking): the menu sits in the top layer under the button, aligned to its right edge (placement="bottom-end"), flips upwards when there is no room below, follows scrolling, and closes with Esc (the focus goes back to the button), Tab or a click outside; ↑ ↓ Home End and letters move among the items. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle work with its id.

One action only

A menu for a single item is heavy: use action_button/1, a direct button (or link) that sits where the "⋯" would be.

<.action_button label={"Delete " <> c.name} icon="huge-delete-02" danger phx-click="delete" phx-value-id={c.id} />
<.action_button label="Open" icon="huge-view" navigate={~p"/companies/#{c.id}"} />

The hook sets data-am-open on the nearest [data-am-row], tr or card-table row (.linea-ctable-row) above the button, and the CSS tints it (color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, var(--panel))). Inside a card_table the row is marked with no work of yours. For any other item (a list entry, a message) give its element data-am-row; a card with no data-am-row is simply not marked. The button is pressed through aria-expanded="true".

A modal in kit CSS's look: a centered base-100 box with the theme's rounded-box corners over a dark backdrop, with its enter and leave animations.

<.button phx-click={LedgerUI.open("edit-pin")}>Edit</.button>

<.modal id="edit-pin" animation="scale" origin="top">
  <:header>Edit Pin</:header>
  <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>

    <.button phx-click={LedgerUI.close("edit-pin")}>Cancel</.button>
  </:footer>
</.modal>

It opens and closes in the browser (LedgerUI.open/close/toggle("id")), from the server (LedgerUI.open(socket, "id")) or from an assign:

<.modal id="confirm" open={@confirming} on_close="cancel-confirm">…</.modal>

on_close runs however the modal closed (Esc, the backdrop, the close button, a command), so the server can keep @confirming in sync. With an event name the LiveView (or target) gets handle_event("cancel-confirm", %{"id" => "confirm"}, socket); a %JS{} is run as is. Without a :header the close × sits in the card's corner above the content; give wide content (an image) a close_variant="chip" so the button keeps a backdrop.

title (with description) gives it the header of a sheet instead (the design canvas modal): the 19px title over a muted line with the round × at the end, the body under it, and the :footer buttons aligned to the end over a line, like a LedgerUI.Components.Drawer sheet:

<.modal id="delete-customer" title="Delete customer?" description="Casa das Tintas" class="max-w-[440px]">
  <p>The orders stay in the history.</p>
  <:footer>
    <.button variant="ghost" phx-click={LedgerUI.close("delete-customer")}>Cancel</.button>
    <.button color="error">Delete customer</.button>
  </:footer>
</.modal>

prevent_close keeps Esc and the backdrop from closing it.

A modal opened from a drawer (or from another modal) is drawn above it, and Esc closes only the one on top; render it next to the drawer, not inside its markup. Its layer is the CSS custom property --ledger-z-modal (see the README).

Ledger UI's drawer: a full-height panel that slides in from the left or the right over a dark backdrop. Bare, it is a sliding frame for a menu; with a title (or a :header) and a :footer it is a sheet, the panel a form or a detail opens in: a header with the title, its description and the close ×, a body that scrolls, and a footer with the buttons.

<.button phx-click={LedgerUI.toggle("menu")}>Menu</.button>

<.drawer id="menu" side="right">
  <nav class="p-5">…</nav>
</.drawer>

<.drawer id="customer" placement="right" size="md" title="New customer"
  description="Who buys from you." on_close="cancel">
  <.form for={@form} id="customer-form" phx-submit="save">…</.form>
  <:footer>
    <.button variant="outline" phx-click={LedgerUI.close("customer")}>Cancel</.button>
    <.button type="submit" form="customer-form" color="primary">Save</.button>
  </:footer>
</.drawer>

size sets the sheet's width (sm 400px, md 520px, lg 640px, wide 800px, xl 1080px), never wider than the screen, so it is full width on a phone. Buttons in the header go in :actions, a back arrow (a sheet opened from another) in :back.

A sheet is variant="float" by default: 12px from the screen's edges, 16px corners, always the whole height, the footer fixed under the body. variant="flush" is the panel glued to the edge, as Ledger UI draws it. placement is left, right or bottom; the bottom one is the phone's sheet, a rounded panel with a grab handle, 78% of the screen's height and the full width.

The header, the body and the footer are also components of their own, for a sheet laid out by hand (variant makes a bare drawer a sheet):

  <.sheet_header title="Edit customer" description="Since March 2025" />
  <.sheet_body>
    <.input field={@form[:legal_name]} label="Legal name" />
  </.sheet_body>
  <.sheet_footer>
    <.button variant="outline" phx-click={LedgerUI.close("edit-customer")}>Cancel</.button>
    <.button color="primary">Save</.button>
  </.sheet_footer>
</.drawer>

Like the modal it opens from the browser (LedgerUI.open/close/toggle("id")), from the server (LedgerUI.open(socket, "id")) or from open; on_close runs however it closed (Esc, the backdrop, the ×, a command), so the server can follow. By default a drawer does not lock the page's scroll, as in Ledger UI (lock_scroll locks it).

Drawers and modals stack in the order they open: a drawer opened from another (a detail, then its edit form), or a modal opened from a drawer, is drawn above it; Esc and the backdrop close only the one on top. The second overlay may sit next to the first or inside its markup (a confirm rendered in the sheet's body or footer): the open drawer carries no CSS transform (the slide is an animation that only runs while it enters and leaves, with no fill), so it is not a containing block for position: fixed and a modal inside it still covers the whole viewport, above the drawer. Keep panel_class and class free of transform, filter, backdrop-filter, perspective and contain for the same reason. Nothing is moved out of the LiveView's DOM, so patches reach the nested modal as usual. The layers come from the CSS custom properties --ledger-z-overlay (drawers) and --ledger-z-modal (modals), see the README.

Ledger UI's popover: a white card with an arrow next to its trigger, for more than a tooltip holds (text, tags, people, a small form).

<.popover id="lesson">
  <:trigger><.button color="primary">Lessons</.button></:trigger>
  <:title>Group Lesson</:title>
  <p class="mt-2">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>
</.popover>

<.popover id="john" trigger_on="hover" placement="top" class="w-48 px-4 py-5 text-center">
  <:trigger><div class="lu-avatar size-8">…</div></:trigger>
  …
</.popover>

The default placement is Ledger UI's right-start, falling back to the bottom and the top when there is no room. It opens and closes from the browser (LedgerUI.toggle("lesson")), from the server (LedgerUI.close(socket, "lesson")) or from open; a click outside and Esc close it and on_close runs however it closed.

The card floats above the page: opened, it sits in the browser's top layer (popover="manual", position: fixed, placed from the trigger's rectangle), so a scroll area, a drawer's body or an ancestor's z-index / transform neither clip nor cover it. It follows scrolling, flips when there is no room and closes when its trigger scrolls out of sight; it stays in the LiveView's DOM, so patches and events inside it work as usual.

The card is 272px wide (w-68, at most 90% of the viewport) so text wraps instead of running on one line; class changes it (w-48, w-96, w-max). The panel is a role="dialog" named by its :title (aria-labelledby), or by label when there is no title.

A tooltip is an overlay: LedgerUI.open/close/toggle show and hide it by id, and open drives it from the server (when the assign changes, the server wins).

The hint is shown in the browser's top layer (popover="manual"), so a table's scroll area, a drawer's body or an ancestor's z-index / transform neither clip nor cover it; it follows scrolling and hides when its trigger scrolls out of sight.

<.tooltip>

Renders a trigger and its tooltip.

on_open and on_close take an event name or a JS command; an event's payload is %{"id" => id} and it goes to target when given.

</.tooltip>

A command palette: a dialog opened with Ctrl K (or LedgerUI.open/1) where the person types, narrows the results by scope and jumps to a page or runs an action from the keyboard.

<.command_palette
  id="palette"
  scopes={[{"All", "all"}, {"Pages", "pages"}, {"Actions", "actions"}, {"Recent", "recent"}]}
  items={[
    %{group: "Go to", scope: "pages", label: "Orders", sub: "Sales", icon: "huge-shopping-cart-01",
      navigate: ~p"/orders", keys: ["G", "O"]},
    %{group: "Actions", scope: "actions", label: "New order", sub: "Opens the order form",
      icon: "huge-add-01", value: "new-order", keys: ["N"]}
  ]}
  assistant={%{label: "Ask the assistant: “%{query}”", sub: "Answers with your company's data"}}
  on_select="palette-select"
  on_assistant="ask"
/>

<.button phx-click={LedgerUI.open("palette")}>Search</.button>

Item and assistant icons are Hugeicons names (huge-*), which need the Tailwind plugin of the Icons section of the README; without icon, the item shows no icon and the assistant row a sparkle.

The palette is a modal, so LedgerUI.open/close/toggle (in the browser or from the server) and the open, on_open and on_close attrs work as they do for modal. shortcut (Ctrl K / ⌘ K by default) toggles it from anywhere in the page.

The input is a role="combobox" over a role="listbox"; the arrows move the active row (aria-activedescendant), Enter presses it, Ctrl Enter opens it in a new tab and Esc closes the palette. The scope chips are toggle buttons (aria-pressed): the first scope starts selected, the scope "all" keeps every item and any other keeps the items whose scope is the same. Every time the palette opens it starts empty on its first scope.

The items are filtered in the browser, by label, sub and keywords ignoring case and accents. With on_search the server filters instead: the query is pushed (debounced) and the palette shows the items it renders, still narrowed by scope.

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="classic" is the old Ledger UI palette) is the design canvas look (the canvas menu: a 14px panel, 34px rows with muted icons, small faint group headings, mono keys); hints={false} drops the keys footer and highlight="typed" leaves the rows unmarked until something is typed (or an arrow or the mouse picks one), as the canvas shows its "recent" list. An item's avatar (the attrs of LedgerUI.Components.Avatar.avatar/1) takes the place of its icon:

<.command_palette
  id="search"
  variant="canvas"
  hints={false}
  highlight="typed"
  items={[%{group: "Clientes", label: "Casa das Tintas", avatar: %{initials: "CD", tint: "#d97a1e"}}]}
/>

Your own icons

An item that has neither icon nor avatar can draw its own icon (an SVG of the design) through the :item_icon slot, which receives each item's map as you gave it (so it can branch on a kind key of yours):

<.command_palette id="search" items={@entries}>
  <:item_icon :let={item}>
    <.design_icon name={item.kind} />
  </:item_icon>
</.command_palette>

Filtering on the server

By default the palette filters its items in the browser. With on_search it does not filter at all: the query (and the scope) is pushed to the server after debounce milliseconds, the server answers by assigning its own entries to items, and the palette only narrows them by scope. This is the mode for a registry of entries that lives in the app:

<.command_palette id="search" items={@results} on_search="search" on_select="go" />

def handle_event("search", %{"query" => query}, socket) do
  {:noreply, assign(socket, :results, Registry.search(query))}
end

Choosing an item closes the palette and runs on_select. An item with navigate, patch or href is a real link (so Ctrl Enter opens its address in a new window) and the navigation happens as for any link.

<.command_palette>

Renders the palette, closed unless open.

Each of items is a map with label (required) and optionally value (what on_select receives, the label by default), sub (the line under the label), icon (a LedgerUI.Components.Icon.icon/1 name), avatar (a map of LedgerUI.Components.Avatar.avatar/1 attrs, drawn 24px and square in place of the icon), keys (a list of key names shown on the right), group (the heading it is listed under; items without one are listed first, without a heading), scope, keywords (more text the query matches) and one of navigate, patch or href.

assistant is a map with label (%{query} is replaced by what was typed), sub and icon: the row that offers to ask the assistant. It shows when the query has no match, or whenever something is typed with assistant_mode="always".

Events (an event name or a %JS{}; a %JS{} push receives the same payload):

  • on_select - %{"id" => palette id, "value" => item value, "new_tab" => boolean}; new_tab is true after Ctrl Enter or a Ctrl/⌘ click.
  • on_assistant - %{"id" => palette id, "query" => text typed}.
  • on_search - an event name only; %{"id" => palette id, "query" => text typed, "scope" => scope value}, after debounce milliseconds.
  • on_open / on_close - %{"id" => palette id}, as for modal.

All go to target when given.

A notification center: a bell with a dot when something is unread, and, under it, a panel with a title and the count of unread, tabs, the notifications grouped by day, a footer and an empty state.

<.notification_center
  id="notifications"
  items={@notifications}
  tabs={[
    %{id: "all", label: "Todas"},
    %{id: "unread", label: "Não lidas"},
    %{id: "orders", label: "Pedidos", empty: "Nenhum pedido novo"}
  ]}
  on_read_all="read_all"
  on_read="read"
  all_href={~p"/notifications"}
  preferences_href={~p"/settings/notifications"}
/>

Each item is a map:

%{
  id: 41,
  title: "Pedido aguardando aprovação",
  body: "Pedido 2483, Clínica Vida Plena",
  at: "há 4 min",
  group: "Hoje",
  type: "warning",
  category: "orders",
  read: false,
  navigate: "/orders/2483"
}

title is the only required key. group is the heading of the day (items with the same group in a row share it, so keep the list in order); type is one of info success warning error primary and gives the icon and the tone (icon, a Hugeicons name, replaces the icon); category is the id of a tab and is shown after at; navigate, patch or href turn the item into a link.

The tabs are filtered in the browser, without a round trip: all shows everything, unread the items that are not read, and any other id the items with that category. The number beside a tab is how many unread items it holds. Without tabs the panel has no tab bar.

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="classic" is the old Ledger UI panel with title bar, tabs and footer) is the compact panel of the design canvas: no title bar, tabs or footer, only the list grouped by day, each row with its icon tile, the title, the body and the time at the right, the unread ones on the accent tint; its empty state is an icon tile (empty_icon, empty_tone) over the text.

<.notification_center id="notifications" variant="canvas" items={@notifications} on_read="read" />

The panel is a LedgerUI.Components.Popover: it closes on a click outside and on Esc, and opens from the server with LedgerUI.open(socket, "notifications"). Marking as read is up to the server: change read and the dot, the count and the bell follow.

A section that opens and closes under its trigger, with Ledger UI's 200ms height animation. It is the piece Ledger UI's Collapse and Accordion pages are built from (see LedgerUI.Components.Accordion).

<.collapse id="details">
  <:trigger class="flex items-center justify-between py-4 font-medium">Shipping details</:trigger>

chevron adds the rotating chevron Ledger UI's panels use at the end of the trigger:

<.collapse id="files" open chevron="down">
  <:trigger class="px-4 text-xs font-medium uppercase">My files</:trigger>
  …
</.collapse>

variant is the design canvas section by default (see below); classic (or nil) is the old bare look, and variant gives it one of three more looks without writing the trigger's classes: framed (a card with a 12px radius and an inset 1px border, a hover fill, 16/14px padding), flat (only a rule under it) and section (a small uppercase label):

<.collapse id="filters" variant="section" chevron="down" open>
  <:trigger>Filters</:trigger>
  …
</.collapse>

canvas is the design canvas section (the look of the canvas accordion): a 14px frame with an inset line, the title in the ink at 14px 16px, a muted 13.5/21 body.

The app top bar of the canvas "Navbar" board: one container, navbar/1, and small pieces to put in it. The right side is always the same vocabulary (search, notifications, theme, language and the user); the variants change what goes on the left and the visual weight.

<.navbar>
  <.navbar_crumbs items={[%{label: "Início", navigate: ~p"/"}, %{label: "Projetos", navigate: ~p"/projetos"}, %{label: "Site novo"}]} />
  <:end>
    <.navbar_search placeholder="Buscar ou ir para…" phx-click={JS.exec("data-show", to: "#palette")} />
    <.navbar_bell dot />
    <.theme_switch id="theme" variant="icons" size="sm" />
    <.navbar_lang locales={["PT", "EN"]} current="PT" />
    <.navbar_sep />
    <.navbar_user id="me" user={@user}>
      <:menu>
        <.navbar_menu_head user={@user}><:badge><.badge color="primary">Admin</.badge></:badge></.navbar_menu_head>
        <.navbar_menu_item icon="huge-user" navigate={~p"/perfil"}>Perfil</.navbar_menu_item>
        <hr />
        <.navbar_menu_item icon="huge-logout-01" danger href={~p"/sair"} method="delete">Sair</.navbar_menu_item>
      </:menu>
    </.navbar_user>
  </:end>
</.navbar>

variant is "default" (60px, a line under it), "float" (a frosted pill detached from the top, for apps with no side menu), "clear" (transparent, over a hero or a cover; the icon buttons get a glass background), "dense" (44px) or "mobile" (56px: menu, title, bell and user). The slots are inner_block (the left side), :center (between the two, such as navbar_links/1 or a wide navbar_search/1), :end (the right side) and :tabs, which makes the bar two rows: the content on top and the tabs (navbar_tabs/1) under it.

Your own components in the bar

The pieces are optional: :center and :end take any markup, in the same .lu-nb-end wrapper, so an app can put a live_component (the ⌘K palette, the notifications bell, the account menu) in place of navbar_search/1, navbar_bell/1 and navbar_user/1 and the bar keeps the same markup around it:

<.navbar>
  <.navbar_crumbs items={@crumbs} />
  <:center><.live_component module={MyAppWeb.PaletteTrigger} id="palette" /></:center>
  <:end>
    <.live_component module={MyAppWeb.BellLive} id="bell" user={@user} />
    <.live_component module={MyAppWeb.AccountMenu} id="me" user={@user} />
  </:end>
</.navbar>

Inside the :topbar slot of shell/1 it is the top of the page:

<.shell nav={...} user={@user} footer="version">
  <:topbar><.navbar>...</.navbar></:topbar>
</.shell>

The pieces

  • navbar_brand/1, navbar_workspace/1, navbar_chip/1, navbar_slash/1 and navbar_crumbs/1 are the left side.
  • navbar_links/1, navbar_tabs/1 and navbar_title/1 are the middle (and the tabs row).
  • navbar_search/1, navbar_bell/1, navbar_icon/1, navbar_lang/1, navbar_sep/1, navbar_env/1, navbar_sync/1 and navbar_avatars/1 are the right side. The theme choice is theme_switch/1 (variant="icons" size="sm"), a button is button/1.
  • navbar_user/1 is the avatar and, with the :menu slot, the account menu; navbar_menu_head/1, navbar_menu_status/1, navbar_menu_row/1 and navbar_menu_item/1 are what goes in it.

Icons are Hugeicons: write each name in full (huge-search-01) so Tailwind sees it. The bar is a kit CSS navbar; its pieces are kit CSS too (menu-horizontal links, tabs-border tabs, breadcrumbs, btn, join, indicator, badge, status, kbd), painted by the theme. canvas-navbar.css (lu-nb) only lays them out.
