api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

The side menu of the Shell, in three formats that read the same data (the canvas "Sidebar" board):

  • sections (the default): the brand with a company switcher, groups with an uppercase mono label, "settings and help" at the foot and the plan card.
  • rail: a 58px rail of icons (logo, home, the person, one icon per group, extra apps in coloured circles, the foot items) beside the raised panel of the active module: its title, a create button, its items, a coloured tree, the "try" shortcuts and the trial card.

  • tree: the brand with a collapse button, groups with a label and a chevron, children joined by a line, square coloured icons, a notice dot and the user card at the foot (see "The foot" for the version line instead).

    <.sidebar format="rail" nav={MyAppWeb.Nav.items(assigns)} current={@current_path} brand={%{name: "Linea", logo: "S"}} user={%{name: "Marina Costa", email: "marina@linea.com"}} />

Put it inside a .sg root (the framed shell/1 is one). Changing format changes how the menu is drawn, never the items.

The nested format

format="nested" is the shadcn/ui sidebar: the brand as a team switcher (logo tile, brand.name and brand.plan, ↕), groups under a quiet label, items whose children open under a thin line with a chevron that turns, and the user at the foot (avatar, name, e-mail, ↕). With brand.menu and user.menu both rows open a menu beside the sidebar (dropdown/1, ids "#{id}-team" and "#{id}-user"); the user menu starts with the avatar, name and e-mail. A menu is a list of maps (label, icon, navigate / patch / href with an optional method, click for a phx-click, hint at the end, danger: true in red, heading: true for a label) and :separator for a line:

user={%{name: "Marina Costa", email: "marina@linea.com", menu: [
  %{label: "Upgrade to Pro", icon: "spark", navigate: ~p"/billing/upgrade"},
  :separator,
  %{label: "Account", icon: "user", navigate: ~p"/account"},
  %{label: "Billing", icon: "card", navigate: ~p"/billing"},
  :separator,
  %{label: "Log out", icon: "huge-logout-03", href: ~p"/users/log-out", method: "delete"}
]}}

Put <.rail_toggle for="sidebar" /> at the top of the main area for the panel button of the shadcn layout; collapsed, the menu keeps its icons, the switcher's logo and the avatar, with tooltips.

Variants

variant="floating" (the default) is the card with corners and a shadow; "sidebar" sits flush, on the page background with a line at its edge; "inset" drops the card too, for a main area drawn as a card beside it.

The menu data

nav is a list of maps, in the order of the menu. A map with group is a group, any other is an item.

Item keys:

  • label: the text (also the tooltip of the collapsed menu and the accessible name of an icon).
  • icon: see "Icons" below.
  • navigate, patch or href: where it goes (# when none).
  • count: a number at the right, in mono. A dot when the menu is collapsed.
  • badge: a notice dot at the right (the bell of the rail). A string is its accessible name.
  • color: a colour for the icon: a round chip in the rail's tree (children), a square chip in the tree format (items). A name (blue, green, rose, violet, orange, ink) or any CSS colour.
  • children: items under it, joined by a line (tree), a coloured tree (rail) or a plain tree.
  • collapsible: in the tree format an item with children gets a chevron at the right that closes and opens them, and the row itself toggles too when it has no destination (navigate, patch or href); with a destination, clicking the link also opens them. false takes it away. It is true when left out. It starts open only when it holds the active item (itself or a child), closed otherwise.
  • open: true or false forces a collapsible item open or closed at first, whatever the route.
  • active: marks it active; current marks the item whose navigate/patch/href is the current path (path and query are compared). The active item has aria-current="page".
  • match: "exact" (the default, or the match of the component) or "prefix": the item is also active on a path under its own (navigate: "/app/tasks" lights up on /app/tasks/NXP-1; only the path is compared, and / is always exact).
  • disabled: a "coming soon" item: a span (not a link) with aria-disabled="true" and class="lu-sb-item dis" inside an li.menu-disabled, never active and never toggling. title is its tooltip (a string disabled works as the title too).
  • formats: a list of formats that show it (["rail"]: only the rail); every format when left out.

Group keys:

  • group: the label.
  • icon: the icon of the group in the rail.
  • items: its items (and, in the rail panel, nested groups with a collapsible header).
  • collapsible: the whole header row is the toggle (not just the chevron); false takes the chevron (and the toggle) away and the group is always shown; it is true when left out. A collapsible group starts open only when it holds the active item.
  • open: true or false forces a collapsible group open or closed at first, whatever the route.
  • navigate, patch, href: where the group's icon goes in the rail (the first item's when left out).
  • footer: true: the group is the foot of the menu ("settings and help"): in sections under its label, in tree without it, in the rail as icons at the bottom.
  • action: %{label, navigate, icon}, the create button at the top of the rail panel.
  • try: %{label, items}, the shortcuts at the foot of the rail panel ("Try").

The first item that is not in a group is the home of the rail (above the person); the other items without a group come after the group icons. The module open in the rail panel is the group that holds the active item (the first group when none does).

Configuration

config :ledger_ui, :shell, sidebar: :sections, nav: {MyAppWeb.Nav, :items}

sidebar (an atom or a string) is the format when format is left out and nav is {module, function}, called with the assigns of the component, when nav is left out. footer: :version and version: "v1.4.2" (or a map) are the foot (see "The foot"). What you pass always wins.

The foot

The foot of the menu is a choice (footer, in the three formats):

  • "user": the person. The user card in the tree and in sections (the same .lu-sb-user card, in place of the plan card), the avatar in the rail.
  • "version": the version line of the canvas (a status dot, v1.4.2, the build and the "What's new" link) in place of the user (tree, rail) or of the plan card (sections). The line is at the foot of the panel in the rail, so a rail collapsed to icons (which hides the panel) does not show it.
  • "none": nothing, for an app that already shows the user in its topbar.
  • left out: each format as it was, the user card in the tree, the plan card in sections, the avatar in the rail.

version is a string or a map; only version is required:

version="v1.4.2"
version=%{version: "v1.4.2", build: "2a9f1c3", navigate: "/changelog", label: "Novidades",
          title: "Updated today", status: :ok}
  • build: the short hash after the version.
  • navigate, patch or href: where the link goes; without one there is no link.
  • label: the text of the link ("What's new" when left out). title: its tooltip.
  • status: :ok (default, green dot), :warning or :down.

footer: :version without a version draws nothing. A version without footer shows the version line (as in 0.15). show_user={false} is deprecated: it is footer="none", or "version" when there is a version. Collapsed to icons the line is the dot, centred, with the version and the build in its title and aria-label ("Version v1.4.2 (2a9f1c3)").

The kit does not read the version of your app: pass it, from Application.spec/2, in the layout.

<.shell footer="version" version={%{version: "v" <> to_string(Application.spec(:my_app, :vsn)),
  build: "2a9f1c3", navigate: ~p"/changelog", label: "Novidades"}} …>

The canvas "Painel" menu

Every format draws its items as a kit CSS menu (ul.menu.menu-sm, li.menu-title for labels, menu-active on the active item, menu-disabled on a "soon" one), so the look follows the kit CSS theme. The tree format has collapsible groups with a chevron (aria-expanded, aria-controls), items with children in a nested ul (kit CSS's indent and line), disabled "soon" items and the mono count (a badge). Groups open and close in the browser; persist_groups keeps which ones are open in localStorage (linea-sidebar-groups:<id>), so the next visit restores them.

<.sidebar id="menu" format="tree" persist_groups match="prefix" current={@current_path}
  nav={[
    %{group: "Gestão", items: [
      %{label: "Tarefas", icon: "kanban", navigate: ~p"/app/tasks", count: 12,
        children: [%{label: "Minhas", navigate: ~p"/app/tasks/mine"}]},
      %{label: "Relatórios", icon: "chart", disabled: true, title: "Em breve"}
    ]}
  ]}>
  <:sidebar_footer>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm justify-start" data-rail-toggle="menu">Recolher menu</button>
  </:sidebar_footer>
  <:mobile_drawer>
    <.link navigate={~p"/settings"} class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm justify-start">Configurações</.link>
    <.link href={~p"/sair"} method="delete" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm justify-start">Sair</.link>
  </:mobile_drawer>
</.sidebar>

The :sidebar_footer slot is in the foot of the menu, above the version line (footer="version"), so a "Recolher menu" button (any element with data-rail-toggle="<id of the menu>") and the version live together. The :mobile_drawer slot (.lu-sb-drawer) is in the menu body and shows only below 768px, when the menu is the top bar with a hamburger: put the search, settings, theme and logout there.

Collapsing

In every format the menu collapses to icons (tooltips with the label, counts turn into dots). It uses the LedgerUI.ShellRail hook of the framed menu: collapsed is the start, on_collapse is pushed with %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}, the choice is kept in localStorage (persist) and <.rail_toggle for="sidebar" /> collapses it from anywhere, and so does Ctrl/⌘+B (shortcut, any key, or nil to turn it off; it is left to fields and editors, where Ctrl+B is bold). The tree button, the panel button of the rail (and a click on a module icon of a collapsed rail) do it by themselves; sections has no button of its own. Below 768px the menu is a top bar with a hamburger that opens it under the bar.

The state Ledger UI keeps in <body> classes lives on the shell's root element: is-sidebar-open, has-min-sidebar (layout="minimal"), navigation:sideblock and navigation:horizontal, is-header-blur and is-header-not-sticky.

LiveView

sidebar_open is the server's state; the browser toggles without a round trip and tells the server through on_toggle. A choice made in the browser survives patches and live navigation (navigate between LiveViews rendering the same shell id) unless the server changes sidebar_open; at xl and up it is also kept in localStorage["linea-sidebar"] (persist). Below xl the sidebar closes, as in Ledger UI. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(socket_or_js, "shell") drive it from the server or a JS pipeline.

Active items come from active on each item or from current (the current path, compared with the item's navigate, patch or href), so they follow live navigation.

Dark mode (<html class="dark">, localStorage["dark-mode"]) and monochrome mode (<body class="is-monochrome">, localStorage["monochrome-mode"]) are client state; put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has them.

Setup

The hooks (LedgerUI.AppShell, LedgerUI.SidebarGroup, LedgerUI.ShellPopper, LedgerUI.ShellTooltips, LedgerUI.RightSidebar, LedgerUI.ThemeToggle, LedgerUI.MonochromeToggle) come with Ledger UI's Hooks. Render the shell in the app layout of a live_session and give it the current path from an on_mount hook, so the active items follow navigate:

def on_mount(:current_path, _params, _session, socket) do
  {:cont,
   Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :current_path, :handle_params, fn _params, url, socket ->
     {:cont, assign(socket, :current_path, URI.parse(url).path)}
   end)}
end

Layouts

layout="sidebar" (the default) takes a main_sidebar/1 and a sidebar_panel/1; "minimal" adds a sidebar_panel_min/1; "sideblock" takes a sideblock/1; "horizontal" keeps the main sidebar and panel for phones and puts horizontal_nav_menu/1s in the :nav slot of header/1; "framed" is the app frame described below.

The framed shell

layout="framed" is an app in a frame: the menu sits on the grey frame, 10px from the edges, and the page is a rounded white panel beside it. The menu is framed_sidebar/1 with rail_link/1s and rail_module/1s (a module opens the pages under it; the module of the current page starts open). It collapses to a 60px rail of icons (tooltips on hover, badges turned into dots; a click on a module opens it again) and the choice is kept per person. Below 768px the menu becomes a top bar with a hamburger. The page's title block is page_header/1 with variant="page".

Rules the markup needs, each one a thing that renders wrong when missed:

  • The collapse button is rail_toggle/1 in the :leading slot of the page header (the corner of the panel), not inside the menu. It finds the menu by its id. on_collapse receives %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}; assign collapsed back so the server knows, or leave it out and let the browser keep the choice.
  • The children of :search are laid out as the direct children of the search box: the icon first, then the text and the shortcut. In the rail only the first child stays, centered. Do not wrap them in one element, and put class="rail-label" on anything else that must disappear in the rail (the workspace block does it by itself).
  • rail_module/1 is highlighted only when the current page is one of its items (pass current or mark one :item active); opening a module by hand only shows its pages. Give every link current={@current_path} or active so the right one is selected.
  • :bottom is for what stays at the foot of the menu: settings and the person.
  • Use layout="framed" on app_shell and put the page content after page_header/1; the panel is a flex column, so a child with flex-1 fills the rest.

A drawer with several panels (Ledger UI's floating tab bar in the :footer) switches them in the browser, with JS commands on its buttons. persist_tab makes the drawer remember the panel the person chose, for the session (sessionStorage), so it opens on it again after a live navigation replaces the page. Configuration

config :ledger_ui, :shell, sidebar: :sections, nav: {MyAppWeb.Nav, :items}

sidebar is the format and nav is {module, function}, called with the assigns of the shell, when the attributes are left out. The attributes always win.

footer is "user", "version" or "none" (see "The foot" in sidebar/1): the user, the version line of the canvas (version, a string or %{version, build, navigate, label, title, status}) or nothing, in the three formats. The state Ledger UI keeps in <body> classes lives on the shell's root element: is-sidebar-open, has-min-sidebar (layout="minimal"), navigation:sideblock and navigation:horizontal, is-header-blur and is-header-not-sticky.

LiveView

sidebar_open is the server's state; the browser toggles without a round trip and tells the server through on_toggle. A choice made in the browser survives patches and live navigation (navigate between LiveViews rendering the same shell id) unless the server changes sidebar_open; at xl and up it is also kept in localStorage["linea-sidebar"] (persist). Below xl the sidebar closes, as in Ledger UI. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(socket_or_js, "shell") drive it from the server or a JS pipeline.

Active items come from active on each item or from current (the current path, compared with the item's navigate, patch or href), so they follow live navigation.

Dark mode (<html class="dark">, localStorage["dark-mode"]) and monochrome mode (<body class="is-monochrome">, localStorage["monochrome-mode"]) are client state; put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has them.

Setup

The hooks (LedgerUI.AppShell, LedgerUI.SidebarGroup, LedgerUI.ShellPopper, LedgerUI.ShellTooltips, LedgerUI.RightSidebar, LedgerUI.ThemeToggle, LedgerUI.MonochromeToggle) come with Ledger UI's Hooks. Render the shell in the app layout of a live_session and give it the current path from an on_mount hook, so the active items follow navigate:

def on_mount(:current_path, _params, _session, socket) do
  {:cont,
   Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :current_path, :handle_params, fn _params, url, socket ->
     {:cont, assign(socket, :current_path, URI.parse(url).path)}
   end)}
end

Layouts

layout="sidebar" (the default) takes a main_sidebar/1 and a sidebar_panel/1; "minimal" adds a sidebar_panel_min/1; "sideblock" takes a sideblock/1; "horizontal" keeps the main sidebar and panel for phones and puts horizontal_nav_menu/1s in the :nav slot of header/1; "framed" is the app frame described below.

The framed shell

layout="framed" is an app in a frame: the menu sits on the grey frame, 10px from the edges, and the page is a rounded white panel beside it. The menu is framed_sidebar/1 with rail_link/1s and rail_module/1s (a module opens the pages under it; the module of the current page starts open). It collapses to a 60px rail of icons (tooltips on hover, badges turned into dots; a click on a module opens it again) and the choice is kept per person. Below 768px the menu becomes a top bar with a hamburger. The page's title block is page_header/1 with variant="page".

    <.framed_sidebar id="menu" collapsed={@collapsed} on_collapse="collapse" label="Main menu">

      <:wordmark>Signetum</:wordmark>

      </:search>
      <.rail_link navigate={~p"/today"} label="Today" current={@current_path}><.icon name="huge-home-01" /></.rail_link>
      <.rail_module id="sales" label="Sales" badge="3" current={@current_path}>
        <:icon><.icon name="huge-shopping-cart-01" /></:icon>
        <:item navigate={~p"/orders"}>Orders</:item>
        <:item navigate={~p"/products"}>Products</:item>
      </.rail_module>

Rules the markup needs, each one a thing that renders wrong when missed:

  • The collapse button is rail_toggle/1 in the :leading slot of the page header (the corner of the panel), not inside the menu. It finds the menu by its id. on_collapse receives %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}; assign collapsed back so the server knows, or leave it out and let the browser keep the choice.
  • The children of :search are laid out as the direct children of the search box: the icon first, then the text and the shortcut. In the rail only the first child stays, centered. Do not wrap them in one element, and put class="rail-label" on anything else that must disappear in the rail (the workspace block does it by itself).
  • rail_module/1 is highlighted only when the current page is one of its items (pass current or mark one :item active); opening a module by hand only shows its pages. Give every link current={@current_path} or active so the right one is selected.
  • :bottom is for what stays at the foot of the menu: settings and the person.
  • Use layout="framed" on app_shell and put the page content after page_header/1; the panel is a flex column, so a child with flex-1 fills the rest.

Opened with open, right_sidebar_toggle/1, or LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(id) (also from the server with a socket). Esc, the overlay and the close button close it. on_open and on_close take an event name, pushed with %{"id" => id}, or a %JS{}.

<.right_sidebar id="right-sidebar" open={@panel_open} on_close="panel-closed">
  <:title><span class="text-xs">25 May, 2022</span></:title>
  <div class="px-3">…</div>
</.right_sidebar>

Remembering the panel

A drawer with several panels (Ledger UI's floating tab bar in the :footer) switches them in the browser, with JS commands on its buttons. persist_tab makes the drawer remember the panel the person chose, for the session (sessionStorage), so it opens on it again after a live navigation replaces the page. Mark each control that selects a panel with data-tab="name"; clicking one saves name, and when the drawer mounts it clicks the saved control, which runs the control's own phx-click. The key is derived from the drawer's id, so two drawers do not share a choice.

<.right_sidebar id="right-sidebar" persist_tab>
  <.panel id="panel-home" />
  <.panel id="panel-activity" />
  <:footer>
    <button data-tab="home" phx-click={show_panel("home")}>Home</button>
    <button data-tab="activity" phx-click={show_panel("activity")}>Activity</button>
  </:footer>
</.right_sidebar>

label :string "Sidebar"

The state Ledger UI keeps in <body> classes lives on the shell's root element: is-sidebar-open, has-min-sidebar (layout="minimal"), navigation:sideblock and navigation:horizontal, is-header-blur and is-header-not-sticky.

LiveView

sidebar_open is the server's state; the browser toggles without a round trip and tells the server through on_toggle. A choice made in the browser survives patches and live navigation (navigate between LiveViews rendering the same shell id) unless the server changes sidebar_open; at xl and up it is also kept in localStorage["linea-sidebar"] (persist). Below xl the sidebar closes, as in Ledger UI. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(socket_or_js, "shell") drive it from the server or a JS pipeline.

Active items come from active on each item or from current (the current path, compared with the item's navigate, patch or href), so they follow live navigation.

Dark mode (<html class="dark">, localStorage["dark-mode"]) and monochrome mode (<body class="is-monochrome">, localStorage["monochrome-mode"]) are client state; put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has them.

Setup

The hooks (LedgerUI.AppShell, LedgerUI.SidebarGroup, LedgerUI.ShellPopper, LedgerUI.ShellTooltips, LedgerUI.RightSidebar, LedgerUI.ThemeToggle, LedgerUI.MonochromeToggle) come with Ledger UI's Hooks. Render the shell in the app layout of a live_session and give it the current path from an on_mount hook, so the active items follow navigate:

def on_mount(:current_path, _params, _session, socket) do
  {:cont,
   Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :current_path, :handle_params, fn _params, url, socket ->
     {:cont, assign(socket, :current_path, URI.parse(url).path)}
   end)}
end

Layouts

layout="sidebar" (the default) takes a main_sidebar/1 and a sidebar_panel/1; "minimal" adds a sidebar_panel_min/1; "sideblock" takes a sideblock/1; "horizontal" keeps the main sidebar and panel for phones and puts horizontal_nav_menu/1s in the :nav slot of header/1; "framed" is the app frame described below.

The framed shell

layout="framed" is an app in a frame: the menu sits on the grey frame, 10px from the edges, and the page is a rounded white panel beside it. The menu is framed_sidebar/1 with rail_link/1s and rail_module/1s (a module opens the pages under it; the module of the current page starts open). It collapses to a 60px rail of icons (tooltips on hover, badges turned into dots; a click on a module opens it again) and the choice is kept per person. Below 768px the menu becomes a top bar with a hamburger. The page's title block is page_header/1 with variant="page".

Rules the markup needs, each one a thing that renders wrong when missed:

  • The collapse button is rail_toggle/1 in the :leading slot of the page header (the corner of the panel), not inside the menu. It finds the menu by its id. on_collapse receives %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}; assign collapsed back so the server knows, or leave it out and let the browser keep the choice.
  • The children of :search are laid out as the direct children of the search box: the icon first, then the text and the shortcut. In the rail only the first child stays, centered. Do not wrap them in one element, and put class="rail-label" on anything else that must disappear in the rail (the workspace block does it by itself).
  • rail_module/1 is highlighted only when the current page is one of its items (pass current or mark one :item active); opening a module by hand only shows its pages. Give every link current={@current_path} or active so the right one is selected.
  • :bottom is for what stays at the foot of the menu: settings and the person.
  • Use layout="framed" on app_shell and put the page content after page_header/1; the panel is a flex column, so a child with flex-1 fills the rest.

<.app_shell>

The page frame: the sidebar, the header, the drawers and the <main> content, with Ledger UI's body classes.

on_toggle runs when the browser opens or closes the sidebar (a toggle button, a close button, a breakpoint change, or a remembered choice applied on mount). An event name is pushed with %{"id" => id, "open" => boolean}; a %JS{} is executed.

<.app_shell id="shell" layout="minimal" sidebar_open={@sidebar_open} on_toggle="sidebar">
  <:sidebar>…</:sidebar>
  <:header><.header /></:header>
  <.page_header title="Orders" />
</.app_shell>

def handle_event("sidebar", %{"open" => open}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, :sidebar_open, open)}
Attr Type Default Values / notes
id :string "app-shell"
layout :string "sidebar" sidebar, minimal, sideblock, horizontal, framed — sidebar is the main sidebar with its panel, minimal shows the minimized panel while the panel is closed, sideblock is one wide sidebar, horizontal puts the navigation in the header, framed is the grey frame with a framed_sidebar/1 and a rounded main panel.
sidebar_open :boolean nil Whether the sidebar is open; defaults to open for sidebar and sideblock.
header_blur :boolean true Ledger UI's is-header-blur.
header_sticky :boolean true false is Ledger UI's is-header-not-sticky.
persist :boolean true Keep the sidebar choice in localStorage.
preloader :boolean false Ledger UI's app preloader, faded out on mount.
on_toggle :any nil An event name or a %JS{}.
target :any nil The phx-target of on_toggle.
main_class :any nil Merged into the classes of <main class="main-content">.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

<.right_sidebar>

Ledger UI's right sidebar: a drawer from the right with an overlay, a top row (:title and the close button), the content and a :footer (Ledger UI's floating tab bar).

Opened with open, right_sidebar_toggle/1, or LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(id) (also from the server with a socket). Esc, the overlay and the close button close it. on_open and on_close take an event name, pushed with %{"id" => id}, or a %JS{}.

<.right_sidebar id="right-sidebar" open={@panel_open} on_close="panel-closed">
  <:title><span class="text-xs">25 May, 2022</span></:title>
  <div class="px-3">…</div>
</.right_sidebar>

Remembering the panel

A drawer with several panels (Ledger UI's floating tab bar in the :footer) switches them in the browser, with JS commands on its buttons. persist_tab makes the drawer remember the panel the person chose, for the session (sessionStorage), so it opens on it again after a live navigation replaces the page. Mark each control that selects a panel with data-tab="name"; clicking one saves name, and when the drawer mounts it clicks the saved control, which runs the control's own phx-click. The key is derived from the drawer's id, so two drawers do not share a choice.

<.right_sidebar id="right-sidebar" persist_tab>
  <.panel id="panel-home" />
  <.panel id="panel-activity" />
  <:footer>
    <button data-tab="home" phx-click={show_panel("home")}>Home</button>
    <button data-tab="activity" phx-click={show_panel("activity")}>Activity</button>
  </:footer>
</.right_sidebar>

open :boolean false
label :string "Sidebar"
persist_tab :boolean false Remembers, for the session, the control with data-tab that was clicked last, and clicks it again when the drawer mounts.
on_open :any nil
on_close :any nil
target :any nil
class :any nil

<.framed_sidebar>

The menu of the framed shell (<.app_shell layout="framed">): the brand, an optional workspace and search, the navigation (rail_link/1, rail_module/1) and the bottom items. It collapses to a 60px rail of icons: the labels (any element with the class rail-label) go away, badges become dots and a tooltip shows the label on hover. The choice is kept in localStorage (persist); a collapsed the server changes wins over it. Below 768px it is a top bar with a hamburger that opens the menu under it.

<.framed_sidebar id="menu" collapsed={@collapsed} on_collapse="collapse">
  <:brand><img src={~p"/images/mark.svg"} alt="" class="size-5" /></:brand>
  <:wordmark>Signetum</:wordmark>
  <.rail_link navigate={~p"/today"} label="Today"><svg>…</svg></.rail_link>
</.framed_sidebar>

def handle_event("collapse", %{"collapsed" => collapsed}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, :collapsed, collapsed)}

Put <.rail_toggle for="menu" /> anywhere (the header, the bottom of the menu) for the button that collapses it.

<.tab_bar>

A phone's bottom bar of tabs: one icon per section, the current one in the accent color. Put it in the :tab_bar slot of <.app_shell layout="framed">, or at the foot of any phone-sized frame.

<.tab_bar>
  <:tab navigate={~p"/today"} label="Today" active><.icon name="huge-home-01" /></:tab>
  <:tab navigate={~p"/orders"} label="Orders"><.icon name="huge-shopping-cart-01" /></:tab>
</.tab_bar>

variant="canvas" is the bar of the canvas "Celular" board, a kit CSS dock (dock-label, dock-active) placed inside the board: a bar with the icon and the label visible under it, the current tab highlighted (<nav class="dock"><a class="dock-active">…<span class="dock-label">…</span></a></nav>). The class of a tab is added to its link, so the app can mark its own states.

<.tab_bar variant="canvas" current={@current_path} match="prefix">
  <:tab navigate={~p"/app"} label="Início" match="exact"><.icon name="huge-home-01" /></:tab>
  <:tab navigate={~p"/app/tasks"} label="Tarefas" class="tasks"><.icon name="huge-task-01" /></:tab>
</.tab_bar>

The current tab is the one whose link is current (match="exact", the default, compares the path). With match="prefix" (on the bar for every tab, or on a tab to override it) /app/tasks/NXP-1 also lights the tab of /app/tasks: the tab path or any path under it. The home path / is always compared exactly. active on a tab forces it.

The state Ledger UI keeps in <body> classes lives on the shell's root element: is-sidebar-open, has-min-sidebar (layout="minimal"), navigation:sideblock and navigation:horizontal, is-header-blur and is-header-not-sticky.

LiveView

sidebar_open is the server's state; the browser toggles without a round trip and tells the server through on_toggle. A choice made in the browser survives patches and live navigation (navigate between LiveViews rendering the same shell id) unless the server changes sidebar_open; at xl and up it is also kept in localStorage["linea-sidebar"] (persist). Below xl the sidebar closes, as in Ledger UI. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(socket_or_js, "shell") drive it from the server or a JS pipeline.

Active items come from active on each item or from current (the current path, compared with the item's navigate, patch or href), so they follow live navigation.

Dark mode (<html class="dark">, localStorage["dark-mode"]) and monochrome mode (<body class="is-monochrome">, localStorage["monochrome-mode"]) are client state; put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has them.

Setup

The hooks (LedgerUI.AppShell, LedgerUI.SidebarGroup, LedgerUI.ShellPopper, LedgerUI.ShellTooltips, LedgerUI.RightSidebar, LedgerUI.ThemeToggle, LedgerUI.MonochromeToggle) come with Ledger UI's Hooks. Render the shell in the app layout of a live_session and give it the current path from an on_mount hook, so the active items follow navigate:

def on_mount(:current_path, _params, _session, socket) do
  {:cont,
   Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :current_path, :handle_params, fn _params, url, socket ->
     {:cont, assign(socket, :current_path, URI.parse(url).path)}
   end)}
end

Layouts

layout="sidebar" (the default) takes a main_sidebar/1 and a sidebar_panel/1; "minimal" adds a sidebar_panel_min/1; "sideblock" takes a sideblock/1; "horizontal" keeps the main sidebar and panel for phones and puts horizontal_nav_menu/1s in the :nav slot of header/1; "framed" is the app frame described below.

The framed shell

layout="framed" is an app in a frame: the menu sits on the grey frame, 10px from the edges, and the page is a rounded white panel beside it. The menu is framed_sidebar/1 with rail_link/1s and rail_module/1s (a module opens the pages under it; the module of the current page starts open). It collapses to a 60px rail of icons (tooltips on hover, badges turned into dots; a click on a module opens it again) and the choice is kept per person. Below 768px the menu becomes a top bar with a hamburger. The page's title block is page_header/1 with variant="page".

    <.framed_sidebar id="menu" collapsed={@collapsed} on_collapse="collapse" label="Main menu">

      </:search>

      <.rail_module id="sales" label="Sales" badge="3" current={@current_path}>
        <:icon><.icon name="huge-shopping-cart-01" /></:icon>
        <:item navigate={~p"/orders"}>Orders</:item>
        <:item navigate={~p"/products"}>Products</:item>
      </.rail_module>
      <.rail_link navigate={~p"/chat"} label="Chat" badge="2" current={@current_path}><.icon name="huge-message-01" /></.rail_link>
      <:bottom>
        <.rail_link navigate={~p"/settings"} label="Settings" current={@current_path}><.icon name="huge-settings-02" /></.rail_link>

Rules the markup needs, each one a thing that renders wrong when missed:

  • The collapse button is rail_toggle/1 in the :leading slot of the page header (the corner of the panel), not inside the menu. It finds the menu by its id. on_collapse receives %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}; assign collapsed back so the server knows, or leave it out and let the browser keep the choice.
  • The children of :search are laid out as the direct children of the search box: the icon first, then the text and the shortcut. In the rail only the first child stays, centered. Do not wrap them in one element, and put class="rail-label" on anything else that must disappear in the rail (the workspace block does it by itself).
  • rail_module/1 is highlighted only when the current page is one of its items (pass current or mark one :item active); opening a module by hand only shows its pages. Give every link current={@current_path} or active so the right one is selected.
  • :bottom is for what stays at the foot of the menu: settings and the person.
  • Use layout="framed" on app_shell and put the page content after page_header/1; the panel is a flex column, so a child with flex-1 fills the rest.

A drawer with several panels (Ledger UI's floating tab bar in the :footer) switches them in the browser, with JS commands on its buttons. persist_tab makes the drawer remember the panel the person chose, for the session (sessionStorage), so it opens on it again after a live navigation replaces the page.   </:footer>

The state Ledger UI keeps in <body> classes lives on the shell's root element: is-sidebar-open, has-min-sidebar (layout="minimal"), navigation:sideblock and navigation:horizontal, is-header-blur and is-header-not-sticky.

LiveView

sidebar_open is the server's state; the browser toggles without a round trip and tells the server through on_toggle. A choice made in the browser survives patches and live navigation (navigate between LiveViews rendering the same shell id) unless the server changes sidebar_open; at xl and up it is also kept in localStorage["linea-sidebar"] (persist). Below xl the sidebar closes, as in Ledger UI. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle(socket_or_js, "shell") drive it from the server or a JS pipeline.

Active items come from active on each item or from current (the current path, compared with the item's navigate, patch or href), so they follow live navigation.

Dark mode (<html class="dark">, localStorage["dark-mode"]) and monochrome mode (<body class="is-monochrome">, localStorage["monochrome-mode"]) are client state; put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has them.

Setup

The hooks (LedgerUI.AppShell, LedgerUI.SidebarGroup, LedgerUI.ShellPopper, LedgerUI.ShellTooltips, LedgerUI.RightSidebar, LedgerUI.ThemeToggle, LedgerUI.MonochromeToggle) come with Ledger UI's Hooks. Render the shell in the app layout of a live_session and give it the current path from an on_mount hook, so the active items follow navigate:

def on_mount(:current_path, _params, _session, socket) do
  {:cont,
   Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :current_path, :handle_params, fn _params, url, socket ->
     {:cont, assign(socket, :current_path, URI.parse(url).path)}
   end)}
end

Layouts

layout="sidebar" (the default) takes a main_sidebar/1 and a sidebar_panel/1; "minimal" adds a sidebar_panel_min/1; "sideblock" takes a sideblock/1; "horizontal" keeps the main sidebar and panel for phones and puts horizontal_nav_menu/1s in the :nav slot of header/1; "framed" is the app frame described below.

The framed shell

layout="framed" is an app in a frame: the menu sits on the grey frame, 10px from the edges, and the page is a rounded white panel beside it. The menu is framed_sidebar/1 with rail_link/1s and rail_module/1s (a module opens the pages under it; the module of the current page starts open). It collapses to a 60px rail of icons (tooltips on hover, badges turned into dots; a click on a module opens it again) and the choice is kept per person. Below 768px the menu becomes a top bar with a hamburger. The page's title block is page_header/1 with variant="page".

Rules the markup needs, each one a thing that renders wrong when missed:

  • The collapse button is rail_toggle/1 in the :leading slot of the page header (the corner of the panel), not inside the menu. It finds the menu by its id. on_collapse receives %{"id" => id, "collapsed" => boolean}; assign collapsed back so the server knows, or leave it out and let the browser keep the choice.
  • The children of :search are laid out as the direct children of the search box: the icon first, then the text and the shortcut. In the rail only the first child stays, centered. Do not wrap them in one element, and put class="rail-label" on anything else that must disappear in the rail (the workspace block does it by itself).

Ledger UI's transactional e-mail: one layout for the e-mails a system sends (a sign-in code, a reset link, an order update): the logo, a card with an icon badge, an eyebrow, a title, text, a block of code, facts or steps, a main button with its address spelled out, a note (with an optional 16px icon image) and a footer, set 16px under the card. 520px wide.

<.email_layout subject="Your code" preheader="Valid for 10 minutes" brand="Acme" logo_url="https://acme.com/logo.png"
               eyebrow="Confirm your access" title="Your verification code">
  <:badge><img src="https://acme.com/mail/envelope.png" width="24" height="24" alt="" /></:badge>
  <:body>
    <p>Hi <b>Ana</b>. Type this code on the sign-in screen. It is valid for 10 minutes.</p>
    <.email_code value="482913" />
  </:body>
  <:action href="https://app.acme.com/confirm?token=7f3a9c">Sign in</:action>
  <:note>Not you? Ignore this e-mail: nobody signs in without the code.</:note>
  <:footer>Acme Ltda · Main Street, 100</:footer>

It renders a whole HTML document built for mail clients: tables for the structure, every style inline, web-safe font stacks, no script and no stylesheet that matters. The only <style> carries the resets, the mobile padding and the dark mode: with theme={:auto} (the default) the e-mail follows the reader's prefers-color-scheme, :light and :dark fix it. Every color is also on a hook class (em-*) that the dark block overrides with !important.

Icons and logos are images (<img> with an absolute URL): mail clients do not draw SVG or icon fonts.

Helpers

  • email_code/1: a verification code, one box per character.
  • email_facts/1: label and value rows in a panel; a row can be :mono (a tracking number) or :total.
  • email_steps/1: a row of steps, done or to come (paid, shipped, delivered).

Use them inside the :body slot, with email_p/1 for the paragraphs. They draw the light palette and the dark block restyles them; when the layout has a fixed theme={:dark}, pass theme={:dark} to them too.

Deliver it as the html_body of your mailer (Phoenix.HTML.Safe.to_iodata/1 of the rendered component, or Phoenix.Template.render_to_string/4 with a template that calls it).

The canvas look of a short notice: button="ink" (a black pill with no arrow), footer_style="plain" (centered small print under the card), title_size={18} and compact (tighter padding).

The light / dark / system choice of the canvas "ThemeSwitch" board, wired to the kit's dark mode.

<.theme_switch id="theme" />
<.theme_switch id="theme" variant="icons" size="sm" />
<.theme_switch id="theme" variant="switch" />

variant is "segmented" (icon and label in kit CSS's tabs tabs-box: a grey track with the choice in white), "icons" (the same with the labels visually hidden, for a top bar) or "switch" (kit CSS's toggle with a sun and a moon: on is dark). size="sm" is the compact one; system={false} leaves only light and dark.

The segmented and icons variants are a radiogroup of radio buttons (arrow keys move the choice); the switch is one switch button. The labels are the accessible names (label names the group or the switch).

What it does

The LedgerUI.ThemeSwitch hook (register the kit's hooks) reads the stored choice, puts the dark class on <html> and keeps data-value / aria-checked in step. A click stores the choice in localStorage["theme"] ("light", "dark" or "system") and the dark mode it resolves to in localStorage["dark-mode"], the key theme_toggle/1 uses, so both agree. "System" follows prefers-color-scheme live. Every theme_switch and theme_toggle on the page listens to the same change:darkmode window event and follows. Put <.theme_script /> in the root layout's <head> so the first paint already has the theme.

The server renders the light choice; the hook owns data-value, aria-checked and tabindex, and phx-mounted={JS.ignore_attributes(...)} keeps a LiveView patch from resetting them.

Lets the user choose a named theme (LedgerUI.Theme), as kit CSS's theme controller does: a menu in the top bar or a grid of previews on a settings page. Each option previews its own palette (its swatches carry the theme's data-theme), in the light or dark mode the page is in.

The theme is a palette, apart from the mode: theme_switch/1 still picks light, dark or system, and the picker picks which palette is light or dark. So the two sit side by side.

What it does

The LedgerUI.ThemePicker hook puts the chosen id on <html data-theme>, keeps it in localStorage["linea-theme"], marks the option (aria-checked) and tells every picker on the page through the change:theme window event. on_change also sends the choice to the LiveView (%{"theme" => id}), to keep it on the user's profile, say. Put <.theme_script theme="..." /> in the root layout's <head> so the stored theme is on before the first paint; default (or config :ledger_ui, :theme) is the one shown when nothing is stored.

themes takes ids or maps (%{id, label}) and defaults to LedgerUI.Theme.all/0: the kit's twelve plus the app's (config :ledger_ui, :themes, extra: [%{id: "acme", label: "Acme"}], CSS from mix ledger_ui.gen.theme).

The assistant ("Assistente (IA)"): the conversation, its messages, the proposals the user approves, the queries the assistant shows it made, the field to ask, the list of conversations and the starting suggestions. The assistant proposes and the user approves; nothing changes without a confirmation.

Or piece by piece:

    <:change label="Linha 3" from="Cimento CP2 50" to="40011 · Cimento CP-II 50kg" />
  </.ai_proposal>
</.ai_message>

<.ai_composer field={@form[:pergunta]} context={[:pedidos]} phx-submit="send" />

<.conversation_list conversations={@conversas} active={@conversa.id} on_select="open" />

<.prompt_suggestions items={@sugestoes} on_pick="ask" />

A message of ai_chat is a map: :id, :role (:user or :assistant), :text (paragraphs separated by a blank line, **bold** is bold), :name (of the user, for the avatar), :trace (%{tools: [...], duration_ms: 3000, running: false}), :proposal (%{id:, title:, status:, changes: [%{label:, from:, to:, text:}], note:, editable:}), :streaming and :status.

<.ai_tool_trace>

What the assistant consulted: one chip per query, how many and how long. running shows the spinner and "em andamento"; a tool with failed: true is marked in red; expanded lists each query with its filters.

<.ai_tool_trace tools={[%{icon: "huge-invoice-01", label: "Pedidos", detail: "situação ≠ faturado · 14 linhas"}]} duration_ms={3000} />
Attr Type Default Values / notes
tools :list [] Maps %{icon, label, title, detail, failed}: the Hugeicons name, the name of the source (title is its name in the expanded list), what was asked and failed: true for a query that did not work.
running :boolean false The queries are still going on.
expanded :boolean false Lists each query with its filters under the chips.
duration_ms :integer nil The total time, shown in seconds.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

<.ai_message>

A message of the conversation. The user's is the dark bubble on the right with the avatar; the assistant's is a card with the spark, the queries it made (trace slot) and the content. variant="plain" drops the card: loose text beside the spark.

<.ai_message role="user" name="Marina Costa">Quanto tenho para receber até sexta?</.ai_message>
<.ai_message streaming><p>Os pedidos vencidos somam <b class="ink">R$ 12.300</b></p></.ai_message>
<.ai_message variant="plain"><p>Os pedidos vencidos somam <b class="ink">R$ 12.300</b></p></.ai_message>
Attr Type Default Values / notes
role :string "assistant" user, assistant
variant :string "card" card, plain — card frames the assistant's content (560px, border, padding); plain is loose text beside the spark. Not used by user.
streaming :boolean false Shows the cursor after the last paragraph.
status :string "ok" ok, error — error marks the message (data-status); the failed query itself is drawn by ai_tool_trace.
name :string nil The user's name: the avatar of a user message shows its initials.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

Slots:

  • <:inner_block> (required)
  • <:trace> — The queries the assistant made, above the content.

<.ai_proposal>

<.ai_proposal id="p1" title="Sugestão: trocar o produto da linha" status={:pending}
  on_approve="approve" on_reject="reject">
  <:change label="Pedido">#2491 · Mercadinho Bom Preço</:change>
  <:change label="Linha 3" from="Cimento CP2 50" to="40011 · Cimento CP-II 50kg" />
</.ai_proposal>

<.ai_proposal id="p2" title="Atualizar o pedido" layout="definition" pending_label="Pendente"
  pending_note="Cada ação aprovada entra no rastreamento do pedido" on_approve="approve" on_reject="reject">
  <:change label="Status" from="Aberto" to="Faturado" />
</.ai_proposal>

note :string nil The line under the rows once decided.

Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line.

The greeting of the assistant: the first line (the whole line) in a living gradient, whose colors drift across the text (6s, back and forth; 12s under prefers-reduced-motion), and the question under it. tone="warm" swaps the brand colors for pink, rose and orange.

size :string "lg" sm, md, lg — 30px, 36px or 40px.

class :any nil

<.conversation_list>

The conversations of the assistant, by day, with a button for a new one and a search. The open one is a card; a teal dot marks a conversation with an action waiting. Each item is a link (navigate, patch or href) or, with on_select, a button-like link that sends the id.

<.conversation_list conversations={@conversas} active={@conversa.id} on_new="new" on_search="search" />

A conversation is a map: :id, :title, :status (the line under the title), :day (the group, as "Hoje"), :pending (an action waits), :content (searched with the title) and the link.

Attr Type Default Values / notes
conversations (required) :list
active :any nil The id of the open conversation.
search :string "" The text of the search: filters by title and content.
group_by :atom :day day
variant :string "card" card, rail — rail is a full-height column with a divider.
title :string "Assistente"
shortcut :string "⌘ J" Shown on the new conversation button.
on_new :any nil The event (or JS) of Nova conversa.
on_search :any nil The phx-change event of the search field.
on_select :any nil The event (or JS) of an item without a link; payload %{id}.
target :any nil The phx-target of the events.
class :any nil

  • <:item> — attrs: conversation — The content of an item, in place of the title and status.

<.ai_chat>

  </:header>
  <:suggestion title="Resumo do dia">Faça um resumo do dia.</:suggestion>

Attr Type Default Values / notes
id (required) :string
messages :any [] A list of message maps or a stream of them.
user :any nil The current user (a name or a map with :name): greeting and avatar.
streaming :boolean false The answer is coming: the composer shows Parar.
context :list [] The initial context chips of the composer, as ai_composer.
variant :string "card" card, bare, page — card is framed with the header; bare is the content only; page fills a screen.
draft :string nil The text in the composer.
greeting :string nil Replaces the greeting line.
footnote :string nil A small line under the composer (a notice about approvals, for instance). None unless given.
composer :boolean true false leaves the composer out: a conversation shown as a record (an approved proposal).
placeholder :string "Pergunte sobre pedidos, estoque, fiscal ou financeiro"
on_send :any nil The phx-submit event of the composer.
on_change :any nil The phx-change event of the composer.
on_stop :any nil
on_approve :any nil
on_reject :any nil
on_undo :any nil
on_pick :any nil The event of a suggestion; payload %{value, title}.
target :any nil The phx-target of the events.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

Slots:

  • <:empty> — Shown above the messages in place of the greeting and suggestions.

A message of ai_chat is a map: :id, :role (:user or :assistant), :text (paragraphs separated by a blank line, **bold** is bold), :name (of the user, for the avatar), :trace (%{tools: [...], duration_ms: 3000, running: false}), :proposal (%{id:, title:, status:, changes: [%{label:, from:, to:, text:}], note:, editable:}), :streaming and :status.

<.ai_tool_trace>

What the assistant consulted: one chip per query, how many and how long. running shows the spinner and "em andamento"; a tool with failed: true is marked in red; expanded lists each query with its filters.

<.ai_tool_trace tools={[%{icon: "huge-invoice-01", label: "Pedidos", detail: "situação ≠ faturado · 14 linhas"}]} duration_ms={3000} />
Attr Type Default Values / notes
tools :list [] Maps %{icon, label, title, detail, failed}: the Hugeicons name, the name of the source (title is its name in the expanded list), what was asked and failed: true for a query that did not work.
running :boolean false The queries are still going on.
expanded :boolean false Lists each query with its filters under the chips.
duration_ms :integer nil The total time, shown in seconds.
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

<.ai_message>

A message of the conversation. The user's is the dark bubble on the right with the avatar; the assistant's is a card with the spark, the queries it made (trace slot) and the content. variant="plain" drops the card: loose text beside the spark.

<.conversation_list>

The conversations of the assistant, by day, with a button for a new one and a search. The open one is a card; a teal dot marks a conversation with an action waiting. Each item is a link (navigate, patch or href) or, with on_select, a button-like link that sends the id.

<.conversation_list conversations={@conversas} active={@conversa.id} on_new="new" on_search="search" />

A conversation is a map: :id, :title, :status (the line under the title), :day (the group, as "Hoje"), :pending (an action waits), :content (searched with the title) and the link.

Attr Type Default Values / notes

active :any nil The id of the open conversation.

group_by :atom :day day
variant :string "card" card, rail — rail is a full-height column with a divider.
title :string "Assistente"
shortcut :string "⌘ J" Shown on the new conversation button.
on_new :any nil The event (or JS) of Nova conversa.
on_search :any nil The phx-change event of the search field.
on_select :any nil The event (or JS) of an item without a link; payload %{id}.
target :any nil The phx-target of the events.
class :any nil

on_reject :any nil
on_undo :any nil

trace_line/1 takes the title as title or as its block (so it can hold <b> and <code>). status is nil (done), "running" (the title shimmers, still for readers who prefer reduced motion), "error" (red, with an alert icon in place of icon) or "pending" (faded). With href, navigate or patch the line is a link, and end_icon puts an icon after it (an arrow, say).

trace_step/1 is a native <details>: the line is its summary, with a chevron that turns when open, and the block is what shows under it, behind a thin line. Put a <pre class="linea-trace-code"> there for output, or another <.trace> to group steps (sources, a chain of thought, the files of a commit). open starts it open.

Code, terminal output, logs and diffs in a quiet card: an optional header with a title and a copy button, line numbers, wrapping, added, removed and highlighted lines, and a small size for tool output inside a trace/1. It is the canvas's CodeBlock, in the spirit of the shadcn/ui Code Block.

<.code_block id="install" title="Terminal" icon="huge-command-line" code={@output} line_numbers wrap />

The code

code is a string, split into lines. lines is a list instead, each a string or a map with :text and :variant ("added", "removed" or "highlighted"), for a diff:

<.code_block id="diff" title="mix.exs" lines={[
  "defp deps do",
  %{text: ~s(  {:phoenix, "~> 1.7"},), variant: "removed"},
  %{text: ~s(  {:phoenix, "~> 1.8"},), variant: "added"},
  "end"
]} />

highlight marks lines by number (highlight={[2, 3]}). A line's text is escaped; to show syntax colors pass safe HTML, such as Phoenix.HTML.raw(Makeup.highlight_inner_html(source)), as the block: the block is drawn as is, without line numbers.

Added and removed lines carry a + or − before the text, and line numbers sit in a gutter that grows with the largest number (start_line is the first one). Both are drawn by CSS, so a selection copies the code alone. The code itself always runs left to right.

Header and actions

title (with an optional icon) puts a header above the code; it truncates. copy adds a copy button (to the header, or floating at the top end on hover when there is no header) that copies the code without the markers. The :actions slot adds buttons next to it and the :footer slot a row under the code (a "Show more", say).

size="sm" is tighter and 12px, for tool output; variant="destructive" tints the card for errors and failed output. A long block caps its height with class="[&_pre]:max-h-64" or max_height.

A tool call an agent makes (running a command, reading a file), from input to output, as a line of a trace/1: a plain line while it runs, a step that opens on its output once it has one, red when it fails. A call that waits for the user is a tool_approval/1 card with Deny and Approve. It is the canvas's Tool, in the spirit of the shadcn/ui AI Elements Tool, built on trace/1 and code_block/1.

<.trace>
  <.tool id="t1" state="running" subject="pnpm install" />
  <.tool id="t2" state="done" subject="node --version" output="v24.18.0" />
  <.tool id="t3" state="error" subject="pnpm lint" output={@stderr} />
</.trace>

States

state is where the call stands; it picks the status of the line and the verb before subject:

state line title (en / pt_BR)
running running (shimmer) Running … / Rodando …
waiting pending (faded) Waiting to run … / Aguardando …
done plain Ran … / Rodou …
error error (red) Failed to run … / Falhou ao rodar …
denied plain Denied … / Negado …

verbs overrides them per state (verbs={%{done: "Read", running: "Reading"}} for a file tool) and title replaces the whole title. subject is drawn as code. Map an AI SDK part with its state: input-streaming and input-available are running while the chat streams (error once it stopped, or waiting for a tool that runs on the client), output-available is done, output-error is error and output-denied is denied.

Output

With output (or input, shown above it) the line opens on a small code_block/1 that wraps and caps at 256px; open starts it open. description sits after the title (a duration, say).

Approval

<.tool_approval id="a1" subject="rm -rf tmp" input={@args} on_approve="approve" on_deny="deny" value={@call_id} />

The card asks "Run rm -rf tmp?" (title replaces it), shows the input, and its buttons send on_approve and on_deny with %{"value" => value}.

With href, navigate or patch it renders a link that looks the same.

The classes are kit CSS's: btn, its color (btn-primary, btn-error…), style (btn-outline, btn-soft, btn-ghost), size (btn-xs to btn-xl) and shape (btn-square, btn-circle), so the theme (data-theme) paints it, and any other kit CSS or Tailwind class can be added.

While work runs, loading disables the button (no double submit), marks it aria-busy and puts kit CSS's spinner (loading loading-spinner) before the label; change the label to the gerund yourself:

A button and a field of the same size have the same height (kit CSS's --size-field), so control is no longer needed to line them up; it is kept so existing calls compile. A disabled button is faded. An icon button takes pip, the accent dot on its corner (indicator and status) that tells there is something new:

label is the accessible name of the button. The optional :title slot is the header with the item's name. An item with href, navigate or patch is a link, any other is a button (phx-click...). disabled items stay in the menu and say why in their hint; the keys skip them and they carry aria-disabled. danger paints an item in the error color (put it last).

It uses the Dropdown's machinery (hook LedgerUI.ActionMenu, a Dropdown hook with the row marking): the menu sits in the top layer under the button, aligned to its right edge (placement="bottom-end"), flips upwards when there is no room below, follows scrolling, and closes with Esc (the focus goes back to the button), Tab or a click outside; ↑ ↓ Home End and letters move among the items. LedgerUI.open/close/toggle work with its id.

A menu for a single item is heavy: use action_button/1, a direct button (or link) that sits where the "⋯" would be.

A floating action button that retracts: a navy pill holding a round icon tile and a label, which shrinks to just the round bubble when it is not in use.

<.fab id="ask" label="Ask the assistant" phx-click="open_assistant" />

The label is always in the DOM and is the button's aria-label. color picks the look (assistant is the indigo to purple tile on navy, primary, dark, light), position the corner, size md or lg. Extra offset goes in class (class="bottom-24"). With href, navigate or patch it renders a link.

Retracting

retract says when the pill shows its label. On a device without hover (touch) every mode but never is the bubble, and a tap runs the action directly.

hover (default) is the bubble at rest; it expands on pointer hover and keyboard focus:

<.fab id="ask" label="Ask the assistant" phx-click="open_assistant" />

auto starts expanded, retracts after retract_after ms (4000 by default) or as soon as the page scrolls, and expands again on hover or focus:

<.fab id="help" label="Need a hand?" retract="auto" retract_after={6000} navigate={~p"/help"} />

never is always expanded:

<.fab id="new" label="New invoice" retract="never" color="primary" patch={~p"/invoices/new"}>
  <:icon><.icon name="hero-plus" class="size-5" /></:icon>
</.fab>

always is always the bubble; the label is only the aria-label and the native tooltip:

<.fab id="chat" label="Chat with us" retract="always" color="light" position="bottom-left" badge={3} />

expanded lets the server force the pill open whatever retract says, for a hint or an onboarding step:

<.fab id="ask" label="Ask the assistant" expanded={@show_hint} phx-click="open_assistant" />

A button with several actions is a speed-dial, fab_dial/1.

The canvas look

variant="canvas" (the default; variant="pill" is the old retracting pill) is the design canvas's FAB: the solid ink button (kit CSS btn btn-neutral btn-lg) with 18px corners, the icon and the label always shown (retract, color, size and badge do not apply). offset moves it from the corner, in pixels, in either variant:

<.fab id="new" label="New order" variant="canvas" offset={18} phx-click="new_order">
  <:icon><.icon name="huge-add-01" class="size-4" /></:icon>
</.fab>

On fab_dial/1, variant="canvas" (the default; pill is the old one) is the 56px solid square (a btn btn-neutral btn-square) and its actions are a kit CSS surface of ghost btn rows (icon and label).

The button sits under modals and drawers and above the page (--ledger-z-fab, 90 by default; an app raises it in its own CSS like the other --ledger-z-* layers).

Renders the floating button, or a link when href, navigate or patch is given.

<.fab_dial>

A speed-dial: a round button that opens a column of mini actions, each with its label beside it. The button turns its plus into a cross while it is open.

<.fab_dial id="quick" label="Quick actions">
  <:action label="New contact" phx-click="new_contact"><.icon name="hero-user-plus" class="size-4.5" /></:action>
  <:action label="Upload a file" phx-click={JS.push("upload")}><.icon name="hero-arrow-up-tray" class="size-4.5" /></:action>
  <:action label="New proposal" navigate={~p"/proposals/new"}><.icon name="hero-document-plus" class="size-4.5" /></:action>
</.fab_dial>

Each :action takes label (the visible text and the item's name), the icon as its content, and one of phx-click (an event name or a %JS{}, with phx-target), href, navigate or patch (a link); disabled turns it off. The first action is the one nearest the button.

It opens and closes by click. Escape closes it and gives the focus back to the button; with the dial open the up and down arrows walk the actions (from the button, down is the first and up the last, both wrap; Home and End go to the ends), a click on an action, a click outside or the focus leaving close it, and the arrows on the closed button open it. The button has aria-expanded, aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-controls; the actions are the menuitems of a menu named after label. open sets the initial state only (the LedgerUI.FabDial hook owns data-state, so a server patch does not undo the person's choice). The motion is off under prefers-reduced-motion.

color, size and position are the ones of fab/1; class adds offset (class="bottom-24").

api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

Ledger UI's copy to clipboard: a button that copies a text, and a field with a copy button joined to it.

<.clipboard value="mix phx.new demo">Copy</.clipboard>
<.clipboard from="#invite-link" size="xs">Copy</.clipboard>
<.clipboard_input id="share" value={@url} />

from is a selector: a field gives its value, any other element its text. After a copy the toaster shows toast (by default "Text Copied", or "Texto copiado" with locale="pt_BR", in the success color, as Ledger UI does), the button keeps data-copied for two seconds (style it with data-copied:) and on_copy runs; a copy that fails shows error_toast. With copied_label the button says it ("Copiado") for those two seconds:

<.clipboard value="mix phx.new demo" copied_label="Copied">Copy</.clipboard>
<.clipboard value={@pix} locale="pt_BR" variant="soft" icon copied_label="Copiado">Copiar Pix</.clipboard>

icon puts a copy icon before the text (a check while copied) and icon_only makes the round canvas icon button (lu-ib) of it, for a value already on screen:

<.clipboard value="mix phx.new demo" icon copied_label="Copied">Copy</.clipboard>
<.clipboard from="#cmd" icon_only variant="flat" size="sm" aria-label="Copy command" />

copied renders the button already in its copied state (until the next copy ends), to show it.

With on_copy as an event name the LiveView (or target) gets handle_event(name, %{"id" => id}, socket).

<.clipboard>

A button that copies value, or what from points at.

Events: on_copy pushes %{"id" => id} when it is an event name.

Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

Ledger UI's notifications: a small colored note at a corner or an edge of the screen that leaves by itself after a few seconds.

Mount the toaster once, in the layout every LiveView renders (it reads the flash):

<.toaster flash={@flash} />

Then, from the server:

conn |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> redirect(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> push_navigate(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> send_toast("Copied", color: "info", position: "center-top")

put_toast/3 goes through the flash, so it survives a redirect; send_toast/3 pushes the toast to the page at once. From the browser, without a round trip:

<.button phx-click={show_toast("This is a simple notification", color: "primary")}>Primary</.button>

Options: color (neutral primary secondary info success warning error light dark), position (left-top left-bottom center-top center-bottom right-top right-bottom), duration in milliseconds (0 or :infinity keeps it until closed), close (a close button) and template, the id of a <template> on the page whose first element is shown instead of the message (an element with data-toast-dismiss inside it closes the toast; this is the way to put buttons of your own in a toast).

Kinds, descriptions and actions

kind (neutral info success warning error loading) draws the toast as a card (white, navy-700 in dark) with the icon in a tile tinted by the kind (or by color, dark makes the whole card dark) and a title; description adds a second line and actions put buttons on the right. A toast with none of kind, description, actions, aura or value stays Ledger UI's plain colored note (a color: :dark card with no kind leads with a dot with a halo where the icon would be):

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent",
  kind: :success,
  description: "NF-e 1234 was authorized.",
  actions: [
    [label: "Open", event: "open-invoice", value: %{id: 1234}],
    [label: "Undo", js: JS.push("undo")],
    [label: "See all", href: "/invoices"]
  ]
)

An action takes label and one of event (pushed to the LiveView with value merged with %{"toast_id" => id}, to target when given), js (a %JS{} run in the browser) or href (a link). It closes the toast unless dismiss: false; [label: "Close", dismiss: true] alone only closes it. variant (outline by default, solid, soft) and color (primary, error) set the look of the button: [label: "Review", variant: :solid], [label: "Retry", variant: :soft, color: :error].

The timer and the toasts that wait

Every toast leaves by itself after duration (5000 ms on the toaster by default), and a thin line at its bottom counts the time down; the pointer over the stack holds both. timer: false hides the line of one toast and timer={false} on the toaster of all.

A toast that depends on the person stays until it is closed, with a close button and no line: one with actions, one with a template of its own, one with aura: :glow, a loading one, and a progress one until it reaches 100. An explicit duration wins over all of this, so duration: 8000 makes a toast with buttons leave after 8 s and duration: :infinity keeps any toast until closed.

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent")
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]])
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]], duration: 8000)

Inverted toasts

invert reverses the colors of the cards: a dark card on a light page and a light one on a dark page, so the message stands out. The kind still tells the message (the green check of a success keeps its tint). Put it on the toaster for all of them, or on one toast; plain notes invert too, keeping their tint:

<.toaster flash={@flash} invert />

send_toast(socket, "Changes saved", kind: :success, invert: true)

Loading, then the answer

A toast with a fixed id is updated in place when another one comes with the same id:

socket = send_toast(socket, "Sending the invoice…", id: "nfe-42", kind: :loading)
# later, in handle_info/2
send_toast(socket, "Invoice authorized", id: "nfe-42", kind: :success)

A loading toast never leaves by itself and has no close button; once it becomes another kind it takes its duration again. update_toast/3 changes only the options it is given, keeping the rest (update_toast(socket, "nfe-42", description: "Waiting for SEFAZ…")); dismiss_toast/2 and clear_toasts/1 remove toasts. send_toast/2 also takes the message as title: (send_toast(socket, id: "x", kind: :loading, title: "Working…")). Errors stay until closed when the toaster has persist_errors.

Aura

aura runs a ring of light around the toast while the assistant (or the SEFAZ) works. true or :default rotates it, :dual rotates two lights (the assistant's and green, for a result that is ready) and :glow pulses red instead of rotating (for something that needs the user). aura_size (xs sm default lg, default when not given) sets the thickness of the ring and aura_color (assistant primary secondary info success warning error, assistant by default) the light:

send_toast(socket, "The assistant is reading NF 88.530",
  id: "ai-1", kind: :info, aura: true, description: "Suggesting product, CFOP and markup.")

send_toast(socket, "Manifestation is due today", kind: :warning, aura: :glow, aura_size: :lg)

The sizes are the canvas's: xs 0.75px, sm 1px, default 1.25px (what a toast without aura_size gets) and lg 2px. xs sm lg keep their names and now map to those thicknesses (before, the toast ring was 1, 1.5 and 2.5px, with sm as the default). Aura.aura/1's width takes the same four.

The same ring goes around any element with LedgerUI.Components.Aura.aura/1 (the canvas look, used by toast_card/1 below).

Progress

A toast with a value (0 to 100) is a progress toast: a fill grows behind it, a spinner turns and the percentage shows (bar: true draws a 3px bar at the bottom instead, without the percentage). At 100 it becomes a success and leaves by itself after 1.6 s (or its duration); below 100 it stays and has no close button unless close: true. Turning it into kind: :error makes it a failure: a red card that stays, with the reason in the description and, say, a retry action. Move it with update_toast/3:

socket = send_toast(socket, "Issuing the NF-e", id: "nfe-42", value: 0, description: "Validating…")
# later, in handle_info/2
update_toast(socket, "nfe-42", value: 64, description: "Sending to SEFAZ…")
update_toast(socket, "nfe-42", value: 100, title: "NF-e authorized", description: "Protocol 1292…")

Status

A long process (a deploy, a batch of invoices, an import, a backup) gets the compact, inverse toast: dark in both themes, with a circle at the left, the message and the buttons at the right. status is :run (the circle fills while it works, or shows the real percentage when there is a value), :queue (dashed circle), :ok (green dot) or :err (red dot). **name** in the message highlights the name. A status toast stays until it changes or is closed (a finished one without buttons leaves like any other), has no close button unless close: true, and variant: :ghost makes an action a plain text button. position: "center-bottom" or "center-top" puts it in the middle of the page as a process bar; its width follows the text, up to 440px.

send_toast(socket, "Deploy **f798c00** is building on **mavorax · master**",
  id: "deploy", status: :run, position: "center-bottom", actions: [[label: "Cancel", event: "cancel"]])
update_toast(socket, "deploy", status: :ok, message: "Deploy **f798c00** published in **38s**",
  actions: [[label: "Logs", variant: :ghost, href: "/logs"], [label: "Open", href: "/app"]])
send_toast(socket, "Importing **BB statement**, **412 of 980** lines", id: "imp", status: :run, value: 42)

status_toast/1 draws the same card in the page.

This is the default look. A plain toast (a message and, at most, a kind) is drawn as a status card: :success, :info and no kind are :ok, :error and :warning are :err, :loading is :run. A toast with a description, an aura, a value, steps or a template keeps its own card. To go back to the classic card for every plain toast:

config :ledger_ui, :toast_style, :card

Steps

A batch that goes in stages is a toast with steps (how many) and step (how many are done): a title with the step/steps counter, one segment per stage (done ones in the primary color, the one in course in purple, the rest empty) and the description below. The id makes the next call update it in place; no other toast is stacked. It stays until the last step (no timer, no close button unless close: true), then it turns green and leaves by itself after 1.6 s (or its duration). kind: :error turns it into a plain failure. It is still a toast: actions, invert, position and color: :dark work as in any other.

socket = send_toast(socket, "Issuing 5 invoices", id: "batch", steps: 5, step: 0, description: "Validating…")
# later, in handle_info/2
update_toast(socket, "batch", step: 2, description: "NF-e of PV-1286 at SEFAZ")
update_toast(socket, "batch", step: 5, title: "Batch issued", description: "5 NF-e authorized")

The toasts of a corner are stacked: the newest is shown in full and the older ones sit behind it, smaller, as slivers (three at most). With the pointer over the stack it opens, every toast in its own size, and their timers wait; when the pointer leaves they go on with the time they had left. Set stack={false} on the toaster to keep them always open, one above the other.

The toasts sit on the CSS layer --ledger-z-toast (see the README).

A toast in the page

toast_card/1 draws the design canvas's toast card (lu-toast, light or dark) where it is written, not in the toaster: for a notice that stays in a panel, or to show what a toast looks like.

<.toast_card kind="error" icon="huge-cancel-circle" title="Could not issue"
  description="SEFAZ is down. We will retry in 5 min." />

<.toaster>

The place the toasts are drawn. Mount it once per page, inside the LiveView (the layout that receives @flash).

kit CSS's alert (alert, alert-soft, alert-outline, alert-{color}): filled, outlined, soft and bordered, with an icon, an accent bar or a close button.

<.alert>This is simple alert</.alert>
<.alert color="primary" variant="soft" shape="pill">Saved</.alert>
<.alert color="secondary" variant="soft" accent="left">With a bar</.alert>
<.alert color="info" variant="outline">
  <:icon boxed><svg>…</svg></:icon>
  This is simple alert
</.alert>
<.alert id="notice" color="info" variant="outline" dismissible>Closable</.alert>

The canvas variant (the default) is a soft alert tinted by color (primary, warning, error, info, success; neutral is kit CSS's plain one), the icon at the top left, the content growing beside it (write it as <b> and <p>), the :action buttons in a row under the text and a ghost round close button (variant="solid", outline, soft and bordered give the other kit CSS styles):

<.alert variant="canvas" color="warning">
  <:icon><.icon name="huge-alert-02" class="size-4" /></:icon>
  <b>Certificate expires in 12 days</b>
  <p>Renew it to keep issuing invoices.</p>
  <:action><.button color="mono" size="sm">Renew now</.button></:action>
</.alert>

dismiss_alert/1 fades out and hides the alert around the element that runs it, for close buttons placed by hand:

<.button phx-click={dismiss_alert()}>Remind me later</.button>

<.alert>

Renders an alert.

With accent or a boxed :icon the alert is split into parts and its padding moves to the content; otherwise the content sits in the padded alert itself, after an inline icon.

<.alert id="saved" color="success" variant="soft" dismissible on_dismiss="hide_notice">
  <:icon><svg class="size-5">…</svg></:icon>
  Changes saved.
</.alert>

With on_dismiss="hide_notice" the server gets handle_event("hide_notice", %{"id" => "saved"}, socket).

The canvas's pixel card: a card to choose from (a model, a module, an integration) that, on hover or keyboard focus, lights up a matrix of pixels in its top right corner, in the card's colour. The pixels blink in frames (the pattern changes every 0.3s) and fade towards the centre, so the text stays readable.

<.pixel_card navigate={~p"/novo/loja"} color="red" icon="huge-shopping-cart-01"
  title="Loja" description="PDV, estoque, NFC-e" />

<div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-2.5">
  <.pixel_card navigate={~p"/novo/loja"} color="red" icon="huge-shopping-cart-01"
    title="Loja" description="PDV, estoque, NFC-e" />
  <.pixel_card phx-click="pick" phx-value-id="agenda" color="ink" icon="huge-calendar-03"
    title="Agenda" description="Horários e lembretes" />
</div>

With href, navigate or patch the card is a link (<a>); with none it is a <button type="button"> that takes phx-click and the other events through rest. Both are focusable, and the keyboard focus does what the hover does: the pixels, the stronger outline and the arrow (arrow={false} leaves the arrow out).

color takes a palette name (red, rose, green, teal, blue, violet, amber, ink); without it the card takes the accent. Any other colour goes through the --px custom property:

<.pixel_card title="Marca" description="--px: var(--accent)" style="--px: #f97316" />

The cards sit in a 3-column grid of the canvas with lu-px-grid, and lu-px-sec is the heading of a section of them (a bold name over a muted line); both are plain classes.

How the pixels blink

There is no JavaScript. The card's ::before is masked by a 60px tile of 2.6px squares (three tiles, --pxa, --pxb and --pxc, each with its own random pattern and opacities) intersected with a radial gradient from the top right corner. A stepped keyframe (lu-px-twinkle, .9s steps(1)) swaps the tile every 0.3s. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is off: the first tile stays drawn, lit on hover and focus.
