api:
Todos os function components, atributos, valores e slots que este componente cobre.

Ledger UI's notifications: a small colored note at a corner or an edge of the screen that leaves by itself after a few seconds.

Mount the toaster once, in the layout every LiveView renders (it reads the flash):

<.toaster flash={@flash} />

Then, from the server:

conn |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> redirect(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> push_navigate(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> send_toast("Copied", color: "info", position: "center-top")

put_toast/3 goes through the flash, so it survives a redirect; send_toast/3 pushes the toast to the page at once. From the browser, without a round trip:

<.button phx-click={show_toast("This is a simple notification", color: "primary")}>Primary</.button>

Options: color (neutral primary secondary info success warning error light dark), position (left-top left-bottom center-top center-bottom right-top right-bottom), duration in milliseconds (0 or :infinity keeps it until closed), close (a close button) and template, the id of a <template> on the page whose first element is shown instead of the message (an element with data-toast-dismiss inside it closes the toast; this is the way to put buttons of your own in a toast).

Kinds, descriptions and actions

kind (neutral info success warning error loading) draws the toast as a card (white, navy-700 in dark) with the icon in a tile tinted by the kind (or by color, dark makes the whole card dark) and a title; description adds a second line and actions put buttons on the right. A toast with none of kind, description, actions, aura or value stays Ledger UI's plain colored note (a color: :dark card with no kind leads with a dot with a halo where the icon would be):

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent",
  kind: :success,
  description: "NF-e 1234 was authorized.",
  actions: [
    [label: "Open", event: "open-invoice", value: %{id: 1234}],
    [label: "Undo", js: JS.push("undo")],
    [label: "See all", href: "/invoices"]
  ]
)

An action takes label and one of event (pushed to the LiveView with value merged with %{"toast_id" => id}, to target when given), js (a %JS{} run in the browser) or href (a link). It closes the toast unless dismiss: false; [label: "Close", dismiss: true] alone only closes it. variant (outline by default, solid, soft) and color (primary, error) set the look of the button: [label: "Review", variant: :solid], [label: "Retry", variant: :soft, color: :error].

The timer and the toasts that wait

Every toast leaves by itself after duration (5000 ms on the toaster by default), and a thin line at its bottom counts the time down; the pointer over the stack holds both. timer: false hides the line of one toast and timer={false} on the toaster of all.

A toast that depends on the person stays until it is closed, with a close button and no line: one with actions, one with a template of its own, one with aura: :glow, a loading one, and a progress one until it reaches 100. An explicit duration wins over all of this, so duration: 8000 makes a toast with buttons leave after 8 s and duration: :infinity keeps any toast until closed.

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent")
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]])
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]], duration: 8000)

Inverted toasts

invert reverses the colors of the cards: a dark card on a light page and a light one on a dark page, so the message stands out. The kind still tells the message (the green check of a success keeps its tint). Put it on the toaster for all of them, or on one toast; plain notes invert too, keeping their tint:

<.toaster flash={@flash} invert />

send_toast(socket, "Changes saved", kind: :success, invert: true)

Loading, then the answer

A toast with a fixed id is updated in place when another one comes with the same id:

socket = send_toast(socket, "Sending the invoice…", id: "nfe-42", kind: :loading)
# later, in handle_info/2
send_toast(socket, "Invoice authorized", id: "nfe-42", kind: :success)

A loading toast never leaves by itself and has no close button; once it becomes another kind it takes its duration again. update_toast/3 changes only the options it is given, keeping the rest (update_toast(socket, "nfe-42", description: "Waiting for SEFAZ…")); dismiss_toast/2 and clear_toasts/1 remove toasts. send_toast/2 also takes the message as title: (send_toast(socket, id: "x", kind: :loading, title: "Working…")). Errors stay until closed when the toaster has persist_errors.

Aura

aura runs a ring of light around the toast while the assistant (or the SEFAZ) works. true or :default rotates it, :dual rotates two lights (the assistant's and green, for a result that is ready) and :glow pulses red instead of rotating (for something that needs the user). aura_size (xs sm default lg, default when not given) sets the thickness of the ring and aura_color (assistant primary secondary info success warning error, assistant by default) the light:

send_toast(socket, "The assistant is reading NF 88.530",
  id: "ai-1", kind: :info, aura: true, description: "Suggesting product, CFOP and markup.")

send_toast(socket, "Manifestation is due today", kind: :warning, aura: :glow, aura_size: :lg)

The sizes are the canvas's: xs 0.75px, sm 1px, default 1.25px (what a toast without aura_size gets) and lg 2px. xs sm lg keep their names and now map to those thicknesses (before, the toast ring was 1, 1.5 and 2.5px, with sm as the default). Aura.aura/1's width takes the same four.

Ledger UI's notifications: a small colored note at a corner or an edge of the screen that leaves by itself after a few seconds.

Mount the toaster once, in the layout every LiveView renders (it reads the flash):

<.toaster flash={@flash} />

Then, from the server:

conn |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> redirect(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> put_toast("Saved", color: "success") |> push_navigate(to: ~p"/orders")
socket |> send_toast("Copied", color: "info", position: "center-top")

put_toast/3 goes through the flash, so it survives a redirect; send_toast/3 pushes the toast to the page at once. From the browser, without a round trip:

<.button phx-click={show_toast("This is a simple notification", color: "primary")}>Primary</.button>

Options: color (neutral primary secondary info success warning error light dark), position (left-top left-bottom center-top center-bottom right-top right-bottom), duration in milliseconds (0 or :infinity keeps it until closed), close (a close button) and template, the id of a <template> on the page whose first element is shown instead of the message (an element with data-toast-dismiss inside it closes the toast; this is the way to put buttons of your own in a toast).

Kinds, descriptions and actions

kind (neutral info success warning error loading) draws the toast as a card (white, navy-700 in dark) with the icon in a tile tinted by the kind (or by color, dark makes the whole card dark) and a title; description adds a second line and actions put buttons on the right. A toast with none of kind, description, actions, aura or value stays Ledger UI's plain colored note (a color: :dark card with no kind leads with a dot with a halo where the icon would be):

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent",
  kind: :success,
  description: "NF-e 1234 was authorized.",
  actions: [
    [label: "Open", event: "open-invoice", value: %{id: 1234}],
    [label: "Undo", js: JS.push("undo")],
    [label: "See all", href: "/invoices"]
  ]
)

An action takes label and one of event (pushed to the LiveView with value merged with %{"toast_id" => id}, to target when given), js (a %JS{} run in the browser) or href (a link). It closes the toast unless dismiss: false; [label: "Close", dismiss: true] alone only closes it. variant (outline by default, solid, soft) and color (primary, error) set the look of the button: [label: "Review", variant: :solid], [label: "Retry", variant: :soft, color: :error].

The timer and the toasts that wait

Every toast leaves by itself after duration (5000 ms on the toaster by default), and a thin line at its bottom counts the time down; the pointer over the stack holds both. timer: false hides the line of one toast and timer={false} on the toaster of all.

A toast that depends on the person stays until it is closed, with a close button and no line: one with actions, one with a template of its own, one with aura: :glow, a loading one, and a progress one until it reaches 100. An explicit duration wins over all of this, so duration: 8000 makes a toast with buttons leave after 8 s and duration: :infinity keeps any toast until closed.

send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent")
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]])
send_toast(socket, "Invoice sent", actions: [[label: "Undo", event: "undo"]], duration: 8000)

Inverted toasts

invert reverses the colors of the cards: a dark card on a light page and a light one on a dark page, so the message stands out. The kind still tells the message (the green check of a success keeps its tint). Put it on the toaster for all of them, or on one toast; plain notes invert too, keeping their tint:

<.toaster flash={@flash} invert />

send_toast(socket, "Changes saved", kind: :success, invert: true)

# later, in handle_info/2

Without a caption, help or errors it renders the bare <input> (wrapped in a positioning span when it has icons), so it can sit inside an input_group.

Masks

mask formats what is typed, as Ledger UI's Cleave.js examples do. mask_options tunes it:

<.input name="card" mask="credit_card" placeholder="xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx" />
<.input name="date" mask="date" mask_options={%{pattern: ~w(m d Y), delimiter: "-"}} />
<.input name="time" mask="time" mask_options={%{pattern: ~w(h m s)}} />
<.input name="phone" mask="phone" />
<.input name="document" mask="cpf_cnpj" label="CPF ou CNPJ" mask_submit="raw" />
<.input name="amount" mask="numeral" mask_options={%{thousands: "lakh"}} />
<.input name="code" mask="blocks" mask_options={%{blocks: [3, 2, 3, 3], delimiters: [".", "_", "-"], uppercase: true}} />
<.input name="ref" mask="blocks" mask_options={%{prefix: "Prefix", delimiter: "-", blocks: [6, 4, 4, 7]}} />
mask options
blocks blocks, delimiter, delimiters, prefix, uppercase, lowercase, numeric
credit_card delimiter (" "); blocks follow the card brand (Amex 4-6-5, Diners 4-6-4)
date pattern of d m y Y (~w(d m Y)), delimiter ("/")
time pattern of h m s (~w(h m s)), delimiter (":")
phone blocks ([3, 3, 4]), delimiter (" ")
cpf_cnpj none. Brazilian document: CPF (000.000.000-00) up to 11 digits, CNPJ (00.000.000/0000-00) beyond, switching by itself while typing, deleting and pasting; at most 14 digits. Sets inputmode="numeric" (override it with inputmode)
numeral thousands (thousand lakh wan none), decimals (2), delimiter (","), decimal_mark ("."), positive, prefix ("R$ ", shown before the figure and left out of the raw value)

The input submits the masked text. mask_submit="raw" submits the unmasked value instead (digits, or a plain number like 1234.5 for numeral) through a hidden input that carries the field's name; phx-debounce/phx-throttle are copied onto it.

<.input field={@form[:amount]} mask="numeral" mask_submit="raw" phx-debounce="300" />

Clearing a focused input

clear_on_submit makes the field take the server's value after its form is submitted even while it has focus:

<.form for={@form} phx-submit="add">
  <.input id="todo" name="title" value={@title} clear_on_submit />
</.form>

Buttons inside the input

:prefix and :suffix hold icons and let clicks fall through to the input. Mark one interactive to put a button there (send, clear, show the password):

<.input name="message" value={@message} placeholder="Message">
  <:suffix interactive>
    <.button variant="flat" class="size-7 rounded-[var(--pill-in,8px)] p-0" type="submit" aria-label="Send">
      <.icon name="huge-sent" class="size-4" />
    </.button>
  </:suffix>
</.input>

A suffix that holds text (a unit, a count) takes text: the box sizes to its content and the input's right padding follows it (the LedgerUI.InputSuffix hook publishes the width, 2.25rem until it runs, as for an icon). Icon suffixes are unchanged.

<.input name="guests" type="number">
  <:suffix text>4 pessoas</:suffix>
</.input>

Beside the caption and under the box

:label_aside puts content at the right of the caption (a "Forgot?" link, the word of a strength meter) and :below puts it between the box and the help line (the meter's bars). Both need the caption block, so they go with label (below also works without one).

<.input field={@form[:password]} type="password" label="Senha" help="Mínimo de 8 caracteres">
  <:label_aside><.link navigate={~p"/forgot"}>Esqueci</.link></:label_aside>
  <:below><div class="lu-meter">…</div></:below>
</.input>

The mask runs in the LedgerUI.InputMask hook, so a masked input needs a stable id (it gets one from field; pass one otherwise when the input re-renders).

A one-time code made of single-character boxes, for the second step of a sign-in, a phone or email confirmation, a recovery PIN.

<.otp_input field={@form[:code]} label="6-digit code" />
<.otp_input name="pin" length={4} mask autofocus />

Typing fills a box and moves to the next, Backspace on an empty box goes back and empties the previous one, the arrows, Home and End move between boxes, and a paste or an autofill spreads its characters over the boxes (a text as long as the whole code always starts at the first box). Characters the mode does not allow are dropped.

The boxes have no name: a hidden input named like the field carries the joined code, and a bubbling input event fires from it whenever the code changes, so a surrounding phx-change receives %{"name" => "482913"} (a partial code while it is typed). phx-debounce and phx-throttle go in rest of a form, not here. value may be an integer or a string; the server renders it into the boxes, a value the server sends later wins over the one in the browser (render value="" to clear a rejected code), and re-rendering what the browser sent does nothing.

A filled box keeps the border of the others (it only carries data-filled); with errors it keeps the error border and with state="success" the success one. The error line has role="alert"; a help line under state="success" starts with a check-circle icon.

<.otp_input field={@form[:code]} state="success" help="Code confirmed" />

Accessibility

The boxes are a role="group" named by the label (or by aria_label); each box is named digit_label plus its number (Digit 1), has autocomplete="one-time-code" so the keyboard offers the code from an SMS, and a numeric keypad on touch devices in numeric mode. The separator is hidden from assistive technology.

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.Otp hook, so the component needs a stable id (it gets one from field or name).

<.otp_input>

Renders the boxes, with their caption, help and errors when given.

Events: no event of its own besides on_complete. The hidden input dispatches a bubbling input event when the code changes. on_complete is an event name or a %JS{}, sent to target when there is one, each time the code changes while every box is filled, with %{"id" => id, "name" => name, "value" => code}.

kit CSS's radios (radio, radio-primary, radio-sm…), in a group that shares one name: plain or filled box, circle or squircle, in every theme color.

<.radio_group field={@form[:plan]} options={[{"Free", "free"}, {"Pro", "pro"}]} color="primary" />

  <:radio value="error" color="error" disabled>Error</:radio>

The sizes are kit CSS's (radio-xs, radio-sm, radio-lg; md is its default).

variant="segmented" renders the look of segmented: a row of toggle buttons on one track, where exactly one is chosen. The buttons are real radios (visually hidden), so the form submits the choice, field and its errors work, the arrow keys move the choice and the chosen segment is the one the radio checks, with a focus ring around the segment that has the focus. count shows a small number after the label and disabled dims a segment; color and filled do not apply. size follows segmented (xs and sm are its sm). Unlike segmented, the choice is a form value, so the server learns of it with the form's phx-change.

  %{label: "Day", value: "day"},
  %{label: "Week", value: "week", count: 3},
  %{label: "Month", value: "month", disabled: true}
]} />

variant="tile" draws each option as a 52px square with a 1px border that turns to a 2px ink border when chosen, dimmed to 35% when disabled; the content of the option is free (an SVG, an emoji) and, having no text, each option takes an aria_label.

A numeric field for money and quantities that shows the number the way the person's locale writes it (1.234,56 in pt-BR, 1,234.56 in en) and submits the plain machine value (1234.56).

<.number_input field={@form[:price]} label="Price" prefix="R$" decimals={2} min={0} />
<.number_input field={@form[:quantity]} label="Quantity" steppers min={1} step={1} suffix="un" />
<.number_input name="discount" value={Decimal.new("12.5")} suffix="%" max_decimals={2} max={100} />
<.number_input field={@form[:amount]} locale="en" align="right" />

The visible input has no name: a hidden input named like the field carries the machine value, and a bubbling input event fires from it whenever that value changes, so a surrounding phx-change runs. phx-debounce/phx-throttle go to the hidden input.

value may be an integer, a float, a numeric string or a Decimal. The server formats it for the first paint; a value the server sends later wins over the one in the browser, and re-rendering the same value does nothing.

Typing keeps what the person writes (digits, the decimal separator, the grouping separator and a leading - when negatives are allowed); leaving the field clamps it to min/max, rounds it to decimals/max_decimals and writes it grouped. Arrow up and down (and the steppers) move by step, Page up and down by ten steps.

With steppers the field is 40px high at md (sm 32px, lg 48px) and its value is set in mono. The suffix then sits at the right edge, or, with align="center", right after the value (the hook keeps its distance in --nlen, the number of characters shown). A stepper is disabled at min and max.

stepper_style picks how the steppers look: inset (the default, the canvas stepper) is one field with plain − and + icon buttons inside its ends; round is the canvas's compact one for cart rows, two round outlined buttons with the bare number between them; joined is Ledger UI's, the buttons as boxes joined to the input.

<.number_input name="qty" value={3} steppers stepper_style="round" min={0} />

The behavior lives in the LedgerUI.NumberInput hook, so the field needs a stable id (it gets one from field or name).

<.number_input>

Renders the number input.

Events: none of its own. The hidden input dispatches a bubbling input event when the machine value changes, so the form's phx-change receives %{"name" => "1234.56"} ("" when the field is emptied; the typed text when it is not a number, so the server can reject it).

It is a native <input type="range">, so it submits with its form, fires phx-change as it is dragged and takes the arrow keys, Home, End and Page Up and Down.

Value, marks and steps

show_value writes the value beside the label, filled paints the track up to the thumb, marks puts labels under the track (a click on one sets the value) and steppers adds minus and plus buttons:

Ledger UI's menu lists: a vertical list of links with one active entry.

<.menu_list variant="solid">
  <:item navigate={~p"/start"} active>Getting start</:item>
  <:item navigate={~p"/shipping"}>Shipping</:item>
</.menu_list>

An icon is the first child of an item; Ledger UI's icon colors (muted, darker on hover, current color when active) come with it:

<:item href="#"><svg class="size-5">…</svg><span>Payments</span></:item>

A trailing count (a badge, a number) goes in the :count slot of a menu_item, or in the count attr of an :item; it is pushed to the end of the row:

<.menu_item navigate="/inbox" variant="solid">
  <:icon><svg class="size-5">…</svg></:icon>
  Inbox
  <:count><.badge size="sm" shape="pill">12</.badge></:count>
</.menu_item>

variant follows Ledger UI's examples: link (text only), solid (filled; color picks primary or neutral), pill (rounded with a tinted hover), gradient and bordered.

Items that are not links take on_select (an event name or %JS{}), pushed with %{"value" => item_value}:

<.menu_list on_select="pick">
  <:item value="shipping">Shipping</:item>
</.menu_list>

variant="static" is the canvas lu-list: plain rows (menu_row) with an icon, a title over a sub line, a value at the right and an unread dot; see menu_row.

Streams render one menu_item per row:

<.menu_list id="pages" rows={@streams.pages}>
  <:row :let={{_id, page}}>
    <.menu_item navigate={page.path} active={page.id == @current}>{page.title}</.menu_item>
  </:row>
</.menu_list>

<.menu_list>

Renders the list. Items come from :item slots (each takes href/navigate/patch, active, value, and any HTML attribute), or from rows with a :row slot.

on_select is pushed with %{"value" => value} when an item that has a value is clicked; it goes to target when given; a %JS{} is executed instead.

<.menu_list variant="pill" on_select="pick">
  <:item value="shipping" active={@tab == "shipping"}>Shipping</:item>
  <:item navigate={~p"/payments"}><svg class="size-5">…</svg><span>Payments</span></:item>
</.menu_list>

A timer that ticks in the browser: a ring with the time in the middle for a cash register shift, a countdown or any stretch of time, and a small pill of it for a top bar.

<.timer id="shift" elapsed={@shift_seconds} running={@running} kicker="Register open"
  kicker_paused="Paused" label="Register 01 · Ana Souza" on_toggle="shift_toggled">
  <:actions>
    <.button variant="soft" phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.toggle("shift")}>Pause</.button>
    <.button variant="outline" phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.add("shift", 900)}>+15 min</.button>
  </:actions>
</.timer>

<.timer id="break" direction="down" total={900} elapsed={0} color="warning" on_finish="break_over" />

The mini variant is the pill for the top bar of a screen, with a pulsing dot while it runs:

<header class="flex h-14 items-center justify-between px-5">
  <span>PDV</span>
  <.timer id="shift-mini" variant="mini" elapsed={@shift_seconds} running={@running} label="Shift time" />
</header>

The server owns the time: elapsed is the seconds counted so far, running whether it counts, and total the seconds the ring stands for (8 hours by default). The browser counts from there without a round trip, from a monotonic clock, so a background tab never loses a second. A new elapsed, running, total or direction from the server replaces what the browser counted; a patch that changes none of them leaves the count alone.

format is hms (03:12:45), hm (3h12) or hh:mm (03:12), the mini clock of a top bar.

direction="up" shows the time elapsed and fills the ring as it passes; direction="down" shows the time left (total - elapsed) and empties it. The ring is drawn in color while it runs and in warning when paused; the kicker under it is green while it runs and orange when paused.

The timer has role="timer" and the accessible name label ("Timer" when there is none); the ticking text is not a live region, so a screen reader is not interrupted every second.

Controls

The buttons are the caller's, in the actions slot. They run in the browser, with no round trip, through LedgerUI.Timer, which also pushes from the server:

phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.pause("shift")}
phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.resume("shift")}
phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.toggle("shift")}
phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.add("shift", 900)}

LedgerUI.Timer.add(socket, "shift", 900)

pause, resume and toggle push on_toggle when the state changes; add takes time away with a negative number. Keep a server running assign in step with on_toggle so a later patch does not undo the choice:

def handle_event("shift_toggled", %{"running" => running, "elapsed" => elapsed}, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, running: running, shift_seconds: elapsed)}

Events

Each takes an event name or a %JS{} and goes to target when there is one.

  • on_toggle - a command paused or resumed it: %{"id" => id, "running" => boolean, "elapsed" => seconds}.
  • on_tick - every second: %{"id" => id, "elapsed" => seconds, "remaining" => seconds}. It is a round trip a second, leave it out unless the server needs it.
  • on_finish - once, when a countdown reaches zero (or a count up reaches total with stop_at_total); the timer stops: %{"id" => id, "elapsed" => seconds}.

Renders a timer.

<.timer id="shift" elapsed={@seconds} running={@running} kicker="Register open" kicker_paused="Paused">
  <:actions>
    <.button phx-click={LedgerUI.Timer.toggle("shift")}>Pause</.button>
  </:actions>
</.timer>

running :boolean true Whether it counts. A change from the server replaces the browser's state.
direction :string "up" up, down — up shows the time elapsed, down the time left (total - elapsed).
variant :string "ring" ring, mini — ring is the card with the ring, mini the pill for a top bar.
size :string "md" sm, md, lg — The ring's diameter (128, 168 or 208 px), or the pill's height.
color :string "primary" neutral, primary, secondary, info, success, warning, error — The ring while it runs (ring only); paused is always warning.

Variants

  • default - the classic bar, in the page flow.
  • float - a detached, centered pill of frosted glass (wrapped in .lu-lp-floatwrap).
  • clear - transparent over a hero image (white text); with sticky it turns solid, with border and shadow, once the page scrolls. Put the bar over the hero yourself (a negative margin on the hero, say).
  • mobile - the phone layout at any width: logo, Entrar and the menu button.

sticky pins the bar to the top of the page (position: sticky) and mounts the LedgerUI.LandingNav hook (register the kit's hooks), which sets data-stuck on the bar after stuck_after px of scroll (default 8); the CSS makes the bar solid while it is set. The server never resets that attribute.

Links and the mega menu

A :link with href, navigate or patch is a link (active marks the current page with aria-current). A :link with inner content is a trigger instead: a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls that opens the content as the mega menu under the bar, built with Phoenix.LiveView.JS (no round trip). A click outside the bar, or Escape, closes it. Fill it with landing_mega/1, landing_feature/1 and landing_mega_side/1.

With open_on="hover" (the default) it opens like laravel.com's: a mouse resting on the trigger opens the panel, the panel stays open while the pointer goes down into it, so its cards and links can be reached, and it closes once the pointer has left both (switching to another trigger swaps panels at once). A click or a tap opens it too; outside, Escape or leaving closes it. open_on="click" keeps it to clicks (a second click closes). In both, ArrowDown on a trigger opens the panel and focuses its first item, the arrows walk the items, Escape gives the focus back to the trigger and tabbing out of the bar closes it. Hover and keys come from the LedgerUI.LandingNav hook, mounted when there is a trigger or sticky (register the kit's hooks).

Phone

Below 768px (or with variant="mobile") the links and the primary button leave the bar and a menu button (a kit CSS btn) appears; it opens a panel under the bar listing every :link as a row (a trigger row goes to its href, "#" when it has none) and the :actions again, stacked and full width. So :actions is rendered twice: do not put an id on what is inside it. The mega menu is not shown on a phone.

Announcement

landing_announcement/1 is the thin strip to put above the bar. The slot of the actions is :actions (not :end, which is a reserved word).

The brand is the brand map or, for something else, the :logo slot.

A product card of landing_mega variant="cards": the product's logo and name, a large title, a link with an arrow and a preview of the product that runs off the bottom of the card. The whole card is the link.

tone is default (a soft glow of the accent from a corner), tint (a wash of the accent under thin diagonal lines) or dark (a near-black card, the same in light and dark pages); accent gives the card a color of its own (each product its brand color, as laravel.com does). The preview is the :preview slot (an <img> of the product, say) or, with mock, a drawn placeholder of an app screen. The logo is a Hugeicons name (logo) or the :logo slot.

Attr Type Default Values / notes
title (required) :string
name :string nil The product name beside the logo.
logo :string nil A Hugeicons name for the logo tile.
link_label :string nil
tone :string "default" default, tint, dark
accent :string nil The card's own accent (a CSS color): the link, the logo and the wash take it.
mock :boolean false Draw a placeholder app screen when there is no :preview.
href :string "#"
navigate :string nil
patch :string nil
class :any nil

Any other HTML/phx attribute goes to the root element.

Slots:

  • <:mark> — The logo, instead of logo (an <img> or an <svg>).
  • <:preview> — The picture of the product under the link.

<.landing_announcement>

The thin announcement strip above the bar: an eyebrow tag, the text (inner content), a link and a close button that hides it (JS.hide, no round trip) when dismissible.
